## D694 (DEEP) — Are SERAPIS-E's D3 stacks stable at the half-periods? Not by the loop alone.
Lock PREREG_D694; results/d3_stability_d694.txt. Per stack g(A) = 256E2(A,U) − 16E2(2A,U); with V ∝ e^K and K⁽¹⁾ = −Ng/(1024π⁶ ImS Imρ), a stack is stable where g is maximal.
Found (U = ρ): g has its maximum at the origin (Δg = −5.9 at δ = 0.01, all directions) and MINIMA at all three half-periods (Δg = +1.6 to +2.8 at δ = 0.01). At U = ½ + 14i: origin stable, (½,0) a saddle, (0,½), (½,½) minima of g. So under the one-loop potential alone the half-period stacks are UNSTABLE and roll to the origin; with all stacks at the origin K⁽¹⁾ = −45NE/(64π⁶ ImS Imρ): tilt of the WRONG sign (3× larger, negative) — no inflation. The expected ln-enhanced image-term instability is confirmed in sign; the origin is stabilised by the 256E2(A) term.
Size (estimate): tachyonic curvature δK'' ≈ −1.6e-4 per (unit a)² at U = ρ for C = 1.15e-6; with K_aa ~ ImU/Imρ (~1/200 at ρ), m_A² ≈ −0.1 H²; at horizon exit (U₂ = 14) ≈ −1 H². The instability is weak: Hubble-scale.
How to make it work (compare outward):
1. Fractional D3 branes at the Z2 fixed points: stuck, no position modulus — the cleanest fix; needs a twisted-tadpole-consistent placement at the half-periods (to be checked against the T⁶/(Z2×Z2) discrete-torsion literature). The untwisted annulus (the E2 piece used here) is unchanged; a twisted piece may add U-dependence (to compute).
2. A pinning mass m_A² ≳ H² from the tree-level D3 potential: in KKLT-type stabilisation D3 positions generically get m² ~ H² (the "η problem" of D3-brane inflation, BHK hep-th/0404087: "too large to allow for slow-roll") — here that problem works FOR us, but the minimum must sit at the half-periods (a Z2-symmetric k(A) gives extrema there; which is the minimum is model-dependent).
3. Imaginary-self-dual flux with D3s at the fixed points (flux forces vanish there by symmetry) — same requirement as 2.
VERDICT: SERAPIS-E's tilt sign rests on the D3 stacks being held at the half-periods by something stronger than ~H²; the loop correction itself pushes them to the origin. New stated caveat; does not change the frozen predictions (lock D693), but the microscopic claim is conditional on 1 or 2.

## D695 (DEEP, literature) — Pinning route 1 exists: stuck D3 branes at the Z2 fixed points
Source: Maiden, Shiu, Stefański, "D-brane spectrum and K-theory constraints of D = 4, N = 1 orientifolds" (hep-th/0602038), on T⁶/(Z2×Z2) orientifolds: (i) "stuck" branes sit at orbifold fixed points and the orientifold projection removes the moduli that would move them off — no position modulus; (ii) stuck branes carry NO twisted RR charge (before orientifolding: a pair of fractional branes with opposite twisted charges), so they add no twisted tadpole; (iii) which brane types exist depends on the discrete-torsion choice (hyper- vs tensor-multiplet model); (iv) K-theory constraints restrict their numbers.
Consequences for SERAPIS-E: the half-periods 0, ½, ½U, ½+½U of the inflaton T² are fixed points of the Z2 reflections, so stuck D3s can sit at the three non-origin ones. With no twisted charge, the twisted-sector annulus between them and the O-planes vanishes at the charge level, so the U-dependence is the untwisted E2 piece used in D689 (the counting N → per-stuck-brane normalisation changes C by O(1), absorbed into Im S·Im ρ ≈ 190–245 N → O(1) shift, still natural). The D694 instability is removed: no modulus, nothing to roll.
Remaining to check (stated): (a) that a stuck-brane configuration at the three half-periods (and not the origin) satisfies the untwisted D3 tadpole plus the K-theory parity conditions for one of the two torsion models; (b) the exact coefficient of the untwisted annulus for stuck branes (vs BHK's 128N/−8N for bulk D3s); (c) twisted NS-NS exchange (charge-neutral ≠ zero tension coupling) — may add a small U-dependent term.
VERDICT: route 1 is supported by the literature; SERAPIS-E's microscopic claim now rests on a definite, checkable configuration (stuck D3s at the three half-periods) instead of an unstable one.

## D701 (DEEP) — Casimir-plateau family: index rule, sign condition, and why ρ survives SUSY-breaking twists
Literature: Ghilencea–Hoover–Burgess–Quevedo, "Casimir energies for 6D supergravities compactified on T²/Z_N with Wilson lines" (hep-th/0506164): KK masses M² = (2π)²|n₂+ρ₂ − U(n₁+ρ₁)|²/(𝒜U₂), ρ_i = 0/½ periodic/antiperiodic; renormalised massless part ∝ −(1/𝒜²)(2πU₂)³[…] in the 6D-frame normalisation (×1/𝒜² more in 4D Einstein frame ⇒ our 1/A⁴), i.e. an Epstein-type s = 3 sum; massless periodic bosons give a NEGATIVE energy.
1. Index rule (derived): a D-dim field sees ρ_D ∝ E(U,s)/A^s with s = D/2 (6D: s = 3; 10D with the T⁴ large: s = 5; T⁴ small: s = 3); 4D Einstein frame V ∝ E/A^{s+1}; a codim-2 (in T²) tension gives −|T|/A². Eliminating A: V ⊃ −E(U,s)^{−2/(s−1)} ⇒ plateau 1 − c·y^{−e}, e = 2s/(s−1): s = 3 → e = 3 (SERAPIS-C, D700), s = 5 → e = 2.5, s → ∞ → 2. SERAPIS-E's e = 2 is the limit, not reached by this mechanism; a codim-1 source (n = 1) gives e = 1 ⇒ r ~ 1e-3+, excluded by the SERAPIS caps.
2. Sign condition: the area minimum needs a POSITIVE Casimir term with a negative tension (a negative Casimir with positive tension gives V = +T²/4bE but at a MAXIMUM in A — checked algebraically). Periodic bosons and Scherk–Schwarz-twisted fermions both contribute negatively; positivity needs more periodic (untwisted) fermions than bosons in the light spectrum — model-dependent, stated requirement.
3. Twisted boundary conditions keep the vacuum at ρ if the twist is democratic: identity Σ over the three half-period characteristics of E_s(A,U) = (4^{1−s} − 1)E(U,s) (checked numerically at U = ½+1.3i: s = 2: −0.75005 vs −0.75; s = 3: −0.937500006 vs −0.9375; s = 5: −0.99609375 exact). A Z2×Z2-symmetric sum over spin structures is therefore again ∝ E(U,s): full SL(2,Z), minimum at ρ. A single twist would break to Γ(2) and move the minimum.
Estimate: s = 5 (e = 2.5) variant r ≈ 3.3e-4 at n_s = 0.970 (scaling r ∝ 1/e² between D692 and D700; to compute).
VERDICT: the Casimir route predicts a discrete ladder of plateaus e ∈ {3, 2.5} with r ≈ 2.5e-4 and ≈ 3.3e-4, both below SERAPIS-E (4.7e-4); which rung is realised is set by the dimension of the light Casimir field. Sign requirement stated. Not frozen.

## D703 (DEEP) — Sign condition of the Casimir ladder: half realisable, half obstructed
Source: Arkani-Hamed, Dubovsky, Nicolis, Villadoro, "Quantum horizons of the Standard Model landscape" (hep-th/0703067): massless periodic fermions give POSITIVE Casimir energy, bosons (and antiperiodic fermions) negative; V ∝ −(n_B − n_F); on T² (their App. B.3) the massless-boson Casimir is ∝ −(1/A²)Σ′1/|n − mτ|⁴ (an Epstein E(τ,2)/τ₂² sum, here for 4D fields on T² → 2D, s = 2); they do not analyse the shape minimum.
1. Positive Casimir (needed by D701): REALISABLE — light periodic fermions outnumbering light bosons (ADNV: only neutrinos can flip the SM sign). In a supersymmetric bulk the towers cancel, so the residual is set by SUSY breaking (m3/2 R ≪ 1 ⇒ suppressed by (m3/2 R)²; expanding the massive Epstein sum lowers the effective index — to compute if pursued).
2. Negative net codim-2 tension (n = 2 term): OBSTRUCTED in string settings with RR charge cancelled — BPS objects have tension = charge (O3⁻: −½, D3: +1, O3⁺: +½), so tension sums to the (zero) total charge; non-BPS objects (anti-D3) add POSITIVE excess (charge cancellation with N_anti anti-D3s gives net tension 2N_anti > 0); ISD flux energy cancels O-plane tension (GKP no-scale), leaving the T² area flat at tree level rather than supplying −1/A².
Consequence: in the minimal string setting the D700 two-term competition is unavailable; positive tension + negative Casimir gives a MAXIMUM (D701). Escape routes (stated, not shown): (a) a genuinely negative n = 2 source from non-BPS O-plane configurations or from SUSY-breaking corrections to the O-plane/flux cancellation; (b) a 6D (non-string) supergravity bulk with negative brane tension (SLED-type models allow either sign as input).
VERDICT: the Casimir rungs e = 2.5, 3 (D700–D702) remain viable as effective-field-theory models but lose their string anchor; SERAPIS-E (e = 2), whose plateau uses no tension competition, is unaffected and remains the string-anchored branch. Loop stopped here (main open item now needs a model-building choice, not a lookup).

## D707 (DEEP, outward) — Species-scale route to the 1/E(τ,2) plateau: a real E(U,2) coupling exists, but not where the species scale lives
Follows D706 item 1. Searches 3 (one extended) + 2 fetches. Labels: LITERATURE unless marked.
1. LITERATURE — an exact E(U,2) Wilson coefficient exists. Basu, "The D⁴R⁴ term in type IIB string theory on T² and U-duality" (0708.2950): the D⁴R⁴ coefficient in 8D is E_{5/2}(M)^{SL(3)} − 8 E_2(M⁻¹)^{SL(3)} · E_2(U,Ū)^{SL(2)}, with U the torus complex structure. The SL(3) factors do not depend on U, so at fixed (τ_dil, volume, B/C) the U-dependence is exactly affine: c(U) = A − B·E(U,2). This is the first concrete string coupling we have found with the same s = 2 Eisenstein series as SERAPIS-E.
2. INFERENCE — the shape is affine, not inverse. A species scale defined from c(U), Λ_sp⁻⁴ ∝ A − B E(U,2), gives V ⊃ Λ_sp^k ∝ (A − B E)^{−k/4}. This reduces to a pure 1/E(U,2) only if A ≪ B·E (not generic: E_{5/2} and E_2 are O(1) at moderate coupling) and k = 4. So the D699 term would be a limiting case, with a new free ratio A/B — not a derivation.
3. LITERATURE — the standard species scale uses the LOWEST higher-derivative term (R² in 4D, F₁ in N=2), which is the s = 1 Kronecker-limit object −log(Im U|η(U)|⁴) (Cribiori et al. 2023; Enriques example in 2411.08467: N ≃ −6 ln[2τ₂|η|⁴]). D⁴R⁴ is subleading and does not set Λ_sp. So the natural species route gives s = 1, not s = 2. In our Epstein ladder (D700–D702) s = 1 is the log/η rung, not the e = 2 rung that fixes r ≈ 4.7e-4.
4. LITERATURE — inflation papers built on modular species scales (2407.12081, 2411.08467) find plateaus V ≃ V₀(1 − c/τ₂) at LARGE τ₂ with n_s ≈ 1 − 2/N, r ≈ 8/(a²N²) and Λ_sp ~ 10¹⁶ GeV; none discuss a vacuum at ρ. Our ρ-vacuum construction is not covered by them either way.
VERDICT: PARTIAL / WEAKENED. D706's hope that the species scale supplies 1/E(τ,2) does not hold in its simple form: the species scale naturally gives s = 1, and the only s = 2 coupling found (D⁴R⁴) enters affinely with an extra free ratio. Keep 1/E(τ,2) labelled ASSUMED (unchanged status). Useful by-product: Basu's E_2(U) coupling is a citable precedent that s = 2 Eisenstein dependence on the torus shape does occur in string effective actions.
Next (open): does the s = 1 species route, combined with the ρ-vacuum, give a viable plateau of its own? (i.e. the e→1 end of the D702 ladder — is it log-type and what r does it give?)
Sources: arXiv 0708.2950; 2411.08467; 2407.12081; Cribiori et al., Fortsch. Phys. 2023 (prop.202300150); Ibáñez 2604.27835 (review).

## D709 (DEEP, theory) — Any 1/E(τ,2) plateau from integrating out a modulus needs E at LEADING order: a no-go for loop-correction origins
Follows D707–D708. Searches 3 (one extended) + 1 fetch (BHK hep-th/0508043; the excerpt read did not reach eq. 3.46, so the sign of BHK's E₂ term is NOT re-verified here — our D691 notes use C = 15N/(64π⁶ Im S Im ρ) > 0 as the tilt).
1. ALGEBRA (exact, by hand; two lines). Let a modulus X (dilaton s, volume, area A) be stabilised by two terms, V = a·E(U,s)/X^p − b/X^q with p > q > 0, a, b > 0. Then ∂_X V = 0 gives a·E/X^p = (q/p)·b/X^q, and V_min ∝ −E^{−q/(p−q)}. A pure 1/E plateau (the SERAPIS-E form) needs q/(p−q) = 1, i.e. p = 2q — and then at the minimum the E-term is exactly HALF the competing term, for every value of a, b, E.
2. CONSEQUENCE (no-go, inference). If the E-term is a loop/α′ correction to the term it competes with, the minimum sits where the "correction" is 50% of tree level: perturbative control is lost by construction. This is the Dine–Seiberg problem in its sharpest form. Concrete case checked: dilaton s with tree term −b/s (from −3e^K|W0|², e^K ∝ 1/s) and the BHK loop shift ∝ E(U,2)/s² — it has p = 2q and does give V_min = −b²/(4aE(U,2)) exactly (the SERAPIS-E plateau after the usual uplift tuning), but s* = 2aE/b with a/b ~ N/(64π⁶ Re T) ⇒ s* ≪ 1 (strong coupling) unless N·E/Re T ~ 10⁶. NOT a controlled origin.
3. What survives: the E(U,2)-dependent term must be a LEADING-order energy of an independent sector, as the Casimir energy was in D700 (but D700's Casimir is s = 3, and its partner tension is obstructed, D703). A natural s = 2 candidate: the leading electrostatic/gravitational energy of D3 branes and O3 planes seen through the T² — a 1/r⁴ potential (6 transverse dimensions) summed over the T² lattice gives Σ′|n + mU|⁻⁴ ∝ E(U,2)/U₂² at leading order (HYPOTHESIS; this is the same annulus physics that produces BHK's E₂, so it is string-anchored). Then the question becomes concrete: which competing term, with which power q, makes p = 2q in the 4D Einstein frame? — a power-counting exercise, next.
4. LITERATURE context: loop blow-up inflation (2502.14953; overview 2604.07288) does inflate from loop-corrected Kähler moduli, but its plateau comes from the volume/blow-up structure, not from E(U) in a denominator; 2510.19927 (symmetry points of N=1 modular geometry) treats fixed-point vacua — to read if this line is pursued.
VERDICT: NEGATIVE for "1/E(τ,2) from a loop correction" (any perturbative origin, not just species scale) — exact algebraic reason, labelled. POSITIVE narrowing: the source must be leading-order brane/O-plane (or Casimir) energy with a p = 2q partner; this is where the plateau term must come from if SERAPIS-E is string-derived. 1/E(τ,2) remains ASSUMED.

## D712 (DEEP, theory) — The brane-interaction candidate for 1/E(U,2) hits the same sign wall as D703
Follows D709 item 3. No new searches (power counting + one symbolic check, sympy, inline; no prediction, so no lock).
1. BPS no-force (LITERATURE, standard): D3s and O3s are mutually BPS (tension = charge), so their gravitational and RR exchanges cancel and the leading-order interaction energy is ZERO. The E(U,2) dependence of D3 positions only appears at one loop (the BHK annulus), i.e. as a correction — which D709 rules out. So the D709 candidate needs a non-BPS source: an anti-D3.
2. Signs (inference from standard charges T, Q): an anti-D3 (T = 1, Q = −1) feels energy −2G Σ_j Q_j over the other sources and their images: attracted to D3s, repelled by O3⁻ (T = Q = −½). With charge cancellation (Σ_j Q_j = +1 per anti-D3) the net lattice energy is attractive.
3. Power counting (inference): with the T⁴ large compared with the T² separations, the 6D-transverse Green's function 1/r⁴ summed over T² images, |r|² = A|n + mU|²/U₂, gives Σ′ ∝ E(U,2)/A² (characteristic sums at half-periods recombine to E(U,2) by the D701 identity); the 4D Einstein-frame factor 1/𝒱₆² = 1/(A𝒱₄)² gives p = 4. The brane tension in the same frame scales as 1/A², i.e. q = 2 — so p = 2q holds and this sector WOULD produce an exact 1/E(U,2) plateau.
4. But (COMPUTED, sympy): V = aS/A⁴ + t/A² has V''(A*) = −t³/(a²S²), so the extremum is a MINIMUM only if the net tension t < 0. Numeric check: aS < 0, t > 0 → V(A*) = 0.25 > V(0.9A*), V(1.1A*): MAXIMUM; aS > 0, t < 0 → minimum. An anti-D3 adds POSITIVE net tension (D703), and its interaction is attractive (aS < 0): maximum, the area runs to collapse. Identical to D701/D703's Casimir case.
5. Side estimate (inference): the D709 half-ratio means interaction energy ≈ tension energy, i.e. separations r ~ (g_s N)^{1/4} l_s — the AdS-throat radius. Even with the right sign, the setup would sit in the warped-throat regime, not on a flat T².
VERDICT: NEGATIVE. Every two-term origin of an exact 1/E(U,s) plateau we have tried (Casimir s = 3, 5; brane interaction s = 2) needs a NEGATIVE codim-2 tension in the T², which charge-cancelled string vacua do not give (D703). The obstruction is now general and sharp, not a feature of one mechanism. 1/E(τ,2) remains an ASSUMED effective term; SERAPIS-E should be presented as an effective model with this stated gap, not as a string derivation.
Open (needs a model-building choice, not a lookup — same as D703): a genuinely negative codim-2 source (e.g. O-planes not cancelled by flux, or SUSY-breaking corrections to the GKP cancellation), or a 6D (non-string) supergravity bulk where tension sign is free.

## D717 (DEEP, theory + computed) — The supergravity route around the tension wall, and a ghost theorem for Epstein Kähler potentials
Lock PREREG_D717 (AION-locked before running); script theory/modular/sugra_rung_d717.py; results field_tests/results/sugra_rung_d717.txt (run stopped at the first case, see 3).
Idea (going round the D703/D712 wall instead of through it): ordinary N = 1 supergravity already has a negative term with no negative-tension source — the gravitino term −3e^K|W0|². With a modular-INVARIANT Kähler potential K = −(3α/2) ln E(τ,2), a constant W0 is allowed, and V = e^K|W0|²(K^{ττ̄}|K_τ|² − 3) + V_up (V_up > 0, e.g. an anti-brane) gives a plateau V_up − (3 − 3α)|W0|² y^{−3α} at the cusp: approached from below only for α < 1, exponent p = √(6α) < √6 — so this family could never reproduce SERAPIS-E's p = 2√2 (stated in the lock).
1. COMPUTED, case α = 1/3: V is negative somewhere on Re τ = ½ and its minimum sits at y ≈ 1.93, not at ρ → NOT VIABLE under the locked rule. Asymptotics confirmed (K^{ττ̄}|K_τ|² → 1.000 = 3α at y = 60).
2. WHY (exact, analytic; checked numerically): because the Epstein series is a Laplace eigenfunction, Δ_hyp E(τ,s) = s(s−1)E, the metric of K = −ln E is
   K_ττ̄ = −s(s−1)/(4y²) + |∂_τE|²/E².
   At every critical point of E (τ = i and ρ, where ∂E = 0) the metric is NEGATIVE for s > 1: K_ττ̄(ρ) = −2/3, K_ττ̄(i) = −1/2 for s = 2 (numerical: −0.66667, −0.50000, exact). The kinetic term is a ghost exactly where the vacuum should be. (Far out it is fine: +0.00495 at y = 10 vs 1/(2y²) = 0.005.)
3. GENERAL (inference from 2): any SL(2,Z)-invariant Kähler potential K = −c ln F with F a positive Laplace eigenfunction of eigenvalue λ > 0 has K_ττ̄ = −cλ/(4y²) < 0 at F's critical points. This connects to the "Laplacian swampland" programme (D706; 2506.03253: species-scale coefficients obey D²F = ηF with η > 0): those same objects cannot serve as −ln F Kähler potentials around a fixed-point vacuum. Escape routes: eigenvalue λ < 0, i.e. 0 < s < 1 (E(τ,s) in the critical strip); or K = −ln(2y) + small invariant corrections (the BHK structure, where E stays a perturbation).
VERDICT: NOT VIABLE as posed, but the reason is a clean theorem, not a dead end. Next: test the escape 0 < s < 1 (positive metric at the fixed points; does E(τ,s) stay positive with its minimum at ρ, and what plateau does it give?).

The metric sign flips as predicted (healthy at the fixed points), but E(τ,s) itself is negative near i and ρ, so K = −c ln E is undefined there, and −c ln(−E) blows up where E changes sign (y ≈ 7–15), a wall across the inflationary region. Reason (exact): the y^{1−s} term carries 2√π Γ(s−½) ζ(2s−1)/Γ(s), and ζ(2s−1) < 0 for ½ < s < 1, so it dominates negatively at moderate y. (s < ½ maps to 1 − s by the functional equation.)
The boundary s = 1 (Kronecker limit): K = −ln(2y|η(τ)|⁴) is modular-invariant with exactly the hyperbolic metric (ln|η|⁴ is a Kähler transformation), i.e. it IS the covariant completion W = (W0 + fX)η⁻² of D647, whose plateau is the e = 1 rung that D708 found NOT VIABLE (r ≈ 1.3e-3).
VERDICT: the Epstein-Kähler route is closed for every real s: s > 1 ghost (D717), ½ < s < 1 negative E (this note), s = 1 the known e = 1 rung. Together with the tension wall (D703, D712) and the species route (D707–D709), every mechanism tried for an exact 1/E(τ,2) plateau is excluded or sits on the e = 1 rung. Status: SERAPIS-E's plateau remains an assumed effective term; what is derived is the tilt (BHK), the vacuum at ρ, and the stuck-brane setup. ## D720 (DEEP; locked PREREG_D720; results/tr_rho_d720.txt + tr_rho_d720_structure.txt) — T_R at ρ: NULL by the locked method, because the Γ2 doublet's Majorana matrix is rank 1 at ρ

## D723 (CENTRE; locked PREREG_D723; results/n2_darkrad_d723.txt) — KILL for the doublet-only N sector at ρ: φ → N2N2 makes the universe dark-radiation dominated
Computed (order-of-magnitude bookkeeping; the verdict holds by many orders of magnitude):
- Neutrino bound: a massless N2 pairs with a light ν into a Dirac state of mass y_D v, so y_D < 4.0e-13 (Σm_ν < 0.07 eV).
- Thermalisation at T_R = 6.7e8–6.7e10 GeV needs y_D > 3.4e-4 – 3.4e-3, i.e. 9e8–9e9 times above the allowed value. N2 never thermalises and cannot decay (it is massless).
- Competing SM channel (D601 sfermion scaling, T_R,SM ≈ 30–70 GeV): Br_SM ≈ 1e-19 – 1e-14, so ΔN_eff ~ 1e14–1e19 vs the limit ~0.3 (ACT DR6 N_eff 2.86 ± 0.13). Anomaly and trace channels vanish at the fixed point (D601), so nothing rescues it within the doublet-only model.
VERDICT (locked): KILL for SERAPIS-E's vacuum at ρ with the Γ2 weight-2 doublet as the whole N sector.
Escape (reasoning, not computed): N2 needs a mass from extra structure, e.g. a third singlet N3 mixing with the doublet at ρ (the 2 ⊕ 1 of D664). With M2 ≠ 0 the seesaw allows y_D ≈ √(m_ν M2)/v. N2 then decays or thermalises into SM radiation if y_D ≳ 3e-4, i.e. M2 ≳ (3.4e-4 × 174)²/0.05 eV ≈ 7e7 GeV. If M2 > m_φ/2 ≈ 1.1e13 GeV the channel closes entirely. So SERAPIS-E needs an N sector beyond the bare doublet, with M2 ≳ 1e8 GeV at ρ. This is a stated condition on the model; the frozen inflation bands (lock D693) are not affected, but the reheating story (T_R, N*) now depends on that extra structure.
The paper's reheating/T_R sentences for SERAPIS-E need a caveat (not yet edited).

## D724 (CENTRE; locked PREREG_D724; results/two_plus_one_d724.txt) — MIXED: a 2 ⊕ 1 sector rescues ρ if the singlet mixes through the weight-2 doublet; the weight-4 mixing cannot
Computed (Takagi singular values; scan b ∈ {0, 0.3, 1, 3}, c ∈ {0.3, 1, 3}):
- W2 (N3–doublet mixing through the weight-2 doublet Y): rank 3 at ρ in EVERY case. Smallest/largest ratio R = 2.5e-4 (b = 3, c = 0.3) up to 0.71; for b = 0, R = 0.21–0.71, with an exactly degenerate pair (0.0475c). With M_heavy = 1e12–1e13 GeV the light state has ≳ 2.5e8 GeV, above the D723 escape bound (~1e8 GeV). RESCUE POSSIBLE.
- W4 (mixing through the weight-4 doublet (2Y₁Y₂, Y₁² − Y₂²)): rank 2 at ρ for ALL b, c (smallest SV ~1e-17). Reason (algebra, checked by the scan): at ρ, Y₂ = iY₁, so the weight-4 doublet is ∝ the null vector n = (1, −i) of A(Y), with nᵀn = 0, and it cannot lift the massless state. The KILL extends to this choice.
Weights (reasoning): consistent weights for W2 need k_N = k_N3 = −1 (2k_N + 2 = 0, k_N3 + k_N + 2 = 0). Then N3N3 needs a weight-2 SINGLET form, and Γ2 has none (its weight-2 space is the doublet). So b = 0 at leading order, unless a non-modular or higher-order source exists. b = 0 still gives rank 3 (R ≥ 0.21) but leaves an exactly degenerate pair at ρ. The Takagi phases in the degenerate b = 0 cases did not converge (residual up to 0.5), so their off-diagonal couplings are not reliable; their singular values are.
Inflaton couplings: with all masses non-zero, the stationarity theorem kills the diagonal couplings again, so sterility is restored for the non-degenerate states. Off-diagonal holomorphic couplings at ρ are O(0.01–0.9) for b > 0 (Kähler corrections for mixed weights not modelled). The reheating temperature now depends on this sector: open, next.
Paper: SERAPIS-E section updated with the D720–D724 caveat (frozen numbers kept, revision stated); builds at 13 pp.

## D739 (CENTRE; locked PREREG_D739; results/doublet_weights_d739.txt) — at ρ only the weight-2 doublet can lift the massless heavy neutrino; b = 0 is natural there

## D744 (DEEP; literature + reasoning; first "reverse ladder" tick) — the τ = i baryon problem, worked backwards: a degeneracy breaker η_N, and radiative resonant leptogenesis as the in-model candidate
Reverse path (reasoning):
1. Target: Y_B = 8.75e-11 at T_R ≈ 1–3e6 GeV, from inflaton decay. That needs ε·Br ≈ 3e-5.
2. Obstacle: the Γ2 doublet N is exactly degenerate at τ = i, so ε = 0. The tree-level 2⊕1 mixing over-splits it (ΔM/M ≥ 0.6, D738).
3. Requirement: from D728, ANY splitting η_N = ΔM/M between ~1e-8 and ~0.1 works. Seven decades, no tuning.
4. New term: η_N, the degeneracy breaker (added to the theory map as node eta_n, upstream of lepto_i).
5. In-model candidate: renormalisation-group running from the degeneracy scale Λ to M splits an exactly degenerate pair ("radiative leptogenesis").
Literature:
- Turzyński hep-ph/0311029: two exactly degenerate N with running-induced splitting falls SHORT of the observed asymmetry in the minimal SM case.
- Branco, González Felipe, Joaquim, Nobre, hep-ph/0507092 ("Enlarging the window for radiative leptogenesis"):
  - the asymmetry vanishes at Λ (alignment, Re H₁₂ = 0);
  - running generates both the splitting, δ_N ≃ 2(H₂₂ − H₁₁)t, and the phase, through y_τ²;
  - ε⁰ ≃ (3y_τ²/32π)·Im H₂₁·Re[(Y_ν)₃₁*(Y_ν)₃₂]/[H_jj(H₂₂ − H₁₁)];
  - mixing with a THIRD heavy neutrino (θ₂ ≠ 0) is "crucial" for m₁ = 0;
  - the hierarchical light spectrum is viable for 2e-5 ≲ m₁ ≲ 3e-2 eV, largely independent of M (1e5–1e10 GeV), for thermal leptogenesis.
Fit to our τ = i setup (reasoning):
- The ingredients match. The N doublet is exactly degenerate at τ = i by symmetry, a natural Λ-scale degeneracy. A third singlet N₃ is already needed for the light texture (D742's 3-3 entry). Normal ordering with small m₁ is in their viable range.
- In the MSSM-like spectrum, y_τ² is enhanced by tan²β.
- Differences: our production is NON-thermal (T_R ≈ 1e6 ≪ M), so their thermal Y_B does not carry over directly; and the N₃–doublet MASS mixing must be absent (or small) at tree level, otherwise D738's large splitting returns.
- Rough size (estimate): ε ~ (3y_τ²/32π)·t, t = ln(Λ/M)/16π² ≈ 0.16, y_τ ≈ 0.01·tanβ, gives ε ~ 5e-7·tan²β, i.e. ~1e-5 – 5e-5 for tanβ ≈ 5–10. The right range for the non-thermal requirement (~3e-5).
VERDICT: a promising, in-model route. It needs no added symmetry breaking, only the model's own running plus a third heavy neutrino it already has. To compute next (D745, locked).
MAP: node=eta_n status=estimate touches=[lepto_i] ripple=no

## D746 (DEEP; reverse ladder; reasoning + 2 searches, no computation) — what the SERAPIS-E plateau needs, stated as one term; no in-string source found yet
Target: V/V₀ = 1 − E(ρ,2)/E(τ,2), i.e. a constant V₀ (uplift) minus a NEGATIVE term ∝ 1/E(τ,2), which → e^{−2√2φ} on the plateau.
Requirement (reasoning). Three ways to get the shape:
- (i) An F-term piece −3e^K|W|² with |W|² ∝ E(τ,2)^{−1}. For a gaugino condensate this means a gauge kinetic function with a threshold f ⊃ (1/2a)·ln E(τ,2), the "Epstein threshold".
- (ii) A negative term ∝ g²(τ) with Re f dominated by a one-loop piece β·E(τ,2) at large Im τ.
- (iii) A ratio of invariants from the Kähler side: closed (Epstein-Kähler ghost, D717/D718).
New term named: the Epstein threshold, a ln E(τ,2) (or E(τ,2)-linear) contribution to a gauge kinetic function, distinct from the DKL threshold ln(2y|η|⁴), which is the s → 1 (Kronecker) member and gives the ρ-variant/covariant shapes, not E(τ,2).
Literature (2 searches):
- Non-holomorphic Eisenstein series of the axio-dilaton appear in type IIB higher-derivative couplings (E(τ,3/2), E(τ,5/2) for R⁴, D⁴R⁴; Green–Gutperle line; 0807.0389, 1001.2535). On T², E(U,s) appear in one-loop amplitudes.
- The one-loop D3/D7 annulus gives E(U,2) in the KÄHLER potential (Berg–Haack–Körs; our tilt C).
- I found no source giving ln E(U,2) or E(U,2) in a gauge kinetic function. Option (ii) is also numerically weak: β ~ 1e-3, E ~ 2e2 at horizon exit, so βE ~ 0.2 ≪ Re S ~ 4.
VERDICT: the requirement is now sharp: one negative-energy term scaling as E(τ,2)^{−1}. But no in-string source is known (search-limited claim). Node plateau_origin stays OPEN. This is the model's main unexplained input, together with ε at τ = i (eps_tilt). Next real step: a direct computation of D3-brane gauge thresholds at the half-periods (whether the annulus that gives E(U,2) in K also gives ln E(U,2) in f) is a research project, not a loop tick. Loop pauses.

## D756 (DEEP; literature, deeper at the D755 wall) — the IIB one-loop Kähler potential contains ONLY Eisenstein E₂ functions: SERAPIS-E's tilt is the natural one, and the ρ variant's DKL tilt has no loop origin there
Read (hep-th/0508043, text beyond offset 180k):
- Eq. (3.46), T⁶/(Z₂×Z₂): K⁽¹⁾ = ½Σ_I c·ℰ₂(A_i^I, U^I)/[(S−S̄)(T^I−T̄^I)] + ½Σ_I c·ℰ₂(0, U^I)/[(T^J−T̄^J)(T^K−T̄^K)]. ℰ₂ are spin-structure/orbifold sums of E₂(A, U).
- Eq. (4.3), T⁶/Z₆′: the same structure, with ℰ₂^{(2,P/W)}(0, U²) ∝ E₂(0, U²).
- The N = 1 result "cannot" be absorbed into ln K⁽⁰⁾. In the visible text NO ln(Im U|η|⁴) (DKL) term appears in K.
Consequences:
1. The D754/D755 lead is CLOSED for the IIB setting. The ρ variant's tilt L = −ln(2y|η|⁴) is not produced by the one-loop Kähler potential. It stays a fitted ε (D687), and its natural home would be heterotic (Green–Schwarz), where D755 showed it is ~50× too large.
2. SERAPIS-E's tilt is the IIB-natural one: Ê ∝ E₂(0,U) is exactly the second-term function, and E₂(A,U) at the half-periods is the first.
3. New detail for SERAPIS-E: the E₂(0,U) term is suppressed by the OTHER two Kähler moduli, 1/[(T^J−T̄^J)(T^K−T̄^K)], with no S. The tilt coefficient C therefore receives two contributions, C ≈ c₁/(Im S·Im T^I) + c₂/(Im T^J·Im T^K). D692's Im S·Im ρ ≈ 190–245N is then "the effective volume product". The frozen bands are unchanged (they depend on C only), but the microscopic reading is broader.
VERDICT: going deeper at the wall resolved it, by elimination: in IIB orientifolds the one-loop tilt is E₂-shaped. SERAPIS-E is the derived branch, while the ρ variant (DKL) and τ = i (I₁) tilts are fitted inputs. ## D760 (DEEP, reverse; literature, no computation) — what would make the species scale track E(τ,2)? Nothing known does
Reverse step from D759. The candidate V ∝ y²(d ln E/dy)² needs a species number N_sp ∝ E(τ,2) (Λ_sp² ≃ M_P²/N_sp), with E the same non-holomorphic weight-2 Epstein function as the BHK tilt.

- ∂N ∝ G̃₂, the almost-holomorphic weight-2 form, which vanishes at i and ρ.
- Its potential is V = K²|τ₂G̃₂|²Λ⁴ (eq 1.5), with a Starobinsky-like large-τ₂ limit (eq 4.10).
- The only Eisenstein series in it is E_{3/2} for 10D IIB (Λ⁶ = 1/E_{3/2}). Species-scale functions in lower dimensions (2310.07213) are R⁴ coefficients: E_{3/2} for the axio-dilaton and Ê₁ = −π log(Im τ|η|⁴) for the T² structure. Neither is E(τ,2).
Deduction (requirement → term): the D759 form would need a higher-derivative gravitational coupling whose moduli-dependent coefficient is E(U,2). New term "E₂-species": an N = 1 orientifold R² coefficient built from the same annulus/Möbius N = 2 sectors as BHK. By the D747/D756 pattern, the moduli dependence those sectors give to holomorphic-anomaly-type couplings (gauge thresholds, F₁-like) is log η (DKL/Ê₁) type, while E₂ appears in the Kähler potential. That is an inference from memory, not checked against a computed R² amplitude.
VERDICT: WALL. No known string coupling makes the species scale track E(τ,2).
- The D759 candidate keeps its numbers, but its plateau has no microscopic source. Label: phenomenological, post-hoc.
- The literature's version is a different model: the F₁ (log η) species plateau of 2407.12081. It lives in an N = 2 IIA setting, while the BHK tilt is N = 1 IIB. Grafting one onto the other mixes settings, so it is not pursued.
Deeper next: an explicit N = 1 orientifold R² threshold, to test the inference above. It is a known-type string amplitude, a separate project; the loop pauses here.

Correction to P1's falsifier (ii): a δ_CP ≈ 0/π measurement only weakly disfavours P1. The sharp test is the reverse: CP violation discovered ⇒ gCP excluded.

## D778 (REVERSE, ρ-side; Jl tick 17; locked PREREG_D778; results/rho_weights_d778.txt) — NOT RESTORED: no Dirac-weight assignment with lepton doublets fixes the ρ spectrum; the residual Z₃ forbids it (theorem); the remedy is lepton SINGLETS
Computed: all 25 Dirac-weight assignments (w_d, w₃) ∈ {0, 2, 4, 6, 8}², with complex coefficients on the locked grid and c ∈ {0.6, 1, 3}. K4: (2, 2) reproduces D777. Result: zero NO and zero IO points for every assignment.
A diagnostic after the locked run shows either a degenerate pair, e.g. (4, 4) → (0.99, 0.99, 1.20) and (0, 6) → (0.71, 0.90, 0.90), or a singular M_D.
Reason (theorem) [derived]:
- At ρ the residual ST ≅ Z₃ assigns each field a charge q = (rep phase) + (weight phase).
- A Majorana mass entry m_ij can be non-zero only if q_i + q_j ≡ 0 (mod 3).
- The two components of a Γ₂ doublet carry DIFFERENT charges (ST has eigenvalues ω, ω² on the doublet, shifted equally by the weight phase).
- So a light-lepton doublet always yields either a (q, −q) pair, which gets a Dirac-type degenerate mass, or a state with no partner, which is massless. Three non-degenerate light masses need all three light leptons at q = 0, which a doublet cannot do.
- This holds for the seesaw too (m_ν inherits the light fields' charges).
- It is the reason modular-flavour fits at ω use τ slightly OFF the fixed point (2405.18813 quotes |τ − τ*| ~ 0.01–0.1). SERAPIS-E's vacuum sits exactly at ρ (a symmetry-fixed minimum).
Remedy (creation, testable): put the lepton doublets in Γ₂ SINGLETS, L ∈ 1 ⊕ 1 ⊕ 1′ (1 and 1′ both have Z₃ charge 0, plus the weight phase chosen so that q = 0).
- Then m_ν is unconstrained by Z₃, and three distinct masses are allowed.
- The heavy-ν doublet sector, needed for reheating and leptogenesis at ρ (D724–D776), is unaffected: the N masses may stay degenerate, since they are heavy.
- Cost: no Γ₂ predictivity for the PMNS structure (lepton flavour becomes generic).
VERDICT (locked rule): NOT RESTORED with lepton doublets. ρ-branch lepton doublets are EXCLUDED by the residual Z₃ (exact).
Next (forward): verify the singlet remedy. Seesaw with L = 1 ⊕ 1 ⊕ 1′ and the D724 heavy sector at ρ, singlet Dirac couplings (weight-0 constants and the weight-6 E6 entries allowed by q = 0). Find the NO fraction with Σm_ν ≤ 0.064 eV. Also check whether leptogenesis (D775) survives with this Dirac structure (Casas–Ibarra is agnostic; just confirm a fit exists).

## D780 (REVERSE, ρ-side; Jl tick 19; derivation, no computation) — exact Z₃ at ρ: the inflaton is Z₃-charged, so its decay products carry Z₃ charge, and the charged heavy-ν pair cannot decay through renormalisable couplings; ρ reheating must be redone
Charge bookkeeping (lesson D778):
1. δτ at ρ transforms under the residual ST ≅ Z₃ with a non-trivial phase (weight −2 at a fixed point), so inflaton quanta carry Z₃ charge q_φ ≠ 0 [derived].
2. Heavy states (D779): N_Y (charge 0), Dirac pair N_n (q) / N₃ (−q), q ≠ 0, plus the neutral singlets S₁, S₂.
3. Inflaton decays φ → N_a N_b need q_a + q_b ≡ −q_φ ≠ 0, so EVERY channel contains at least one charged N_n or N₃ [derived]. This matches D725's open channels (LL pair and HL), all of which involve the pair.
4. Realistic light masses force a common lepton charge q_L = −q_H (D778). The renormalisable Dirac coupling L·N·H then needs q_N = 0, so N_n and N₃ cannot decay to L + H [derived]. D725's statement "light states decay via seesaw y_D 0.02–0.13" is WRONG at ρ.
5. Gauge-invariant SM bilinears (H_uH_d, constrained by the μ-term, and L H_u) are Z₃-neutral, so electroweak vevs do not break Z₃ in renormalisable couplings [derived].
6. Modular symmetry is a gauge symmetry in string theory, so Z₃ is exact: no gravitational breaking [literature-level statement, from memory].
Consequences:
- If no operator of any dimension carries the pair's charge, the lightest Z₃-charged state is STABLE. Produced with Y ~ (3/4)T_R/m_φ ~ 1e-5 at M ~ 1e11–1e12 GeV, it overcloses by ~1e14. FATAL.
- If a higher-dimension operator with charge q exists (SM fermion charges are partly free, fixed only by the Yukawas and anomalies), the pair decays through it: Γ ~ M⁵/Λ⁴. With Λ = M_P and M = 1e12, Γ ≈ 3e-14 GeV; the pair (which carries ALL the inflaton energy) then reheats a second time at T₂ ~ √(Γ M_P) ~ 300 GeV. With Λ = M_s ~ 1e16–1e17 GeV, T₂ ~ 3e4–3e6 GeV.
- Either way, D725's T_R = 3e8–3e9 GeV is NOT the final reheating temperature at ρ. The effective T_R is much lower, N* shifts, and the leptogenesis of D731/D775/D776 (produced before the second reheating) is diluted or reset.
VERDICT: CORRECTION. ρ-branch reheating (D725), and everything built on its T_R (leptogenesis D731/D775/D776, the gravitino/wino chain D732–D736), must be recomputed with Z₃ charge conservation. The frozen SERAPIS-E bands are locked and stay as frozen.
- Sign of the shift: a lower T_R lowers N* and n_s (D725: N* 49.7–50.5 at T_R 3e8–3e9). With T₂ ~ 300 GeV–3e6 GeV, N* is ~1.5–4 e-folds lower, and n_s may drop out of the band. That must be computed.
- The τ = i branch is NOT affected the same way: its residual Z₂ allows odd leptons with Majorana masses (2q ≡ 0 mod 2), so odd heavy states can decay to odd leptons.

## D797 (FORWARD, i-side; Jl tick 36; research + derivation, no lock): P3 (the 1/E anti-D3 metric) has no literature source; the natural one-loop routes give E(τ,2) with the WRONG placement, so P3 stays open but sharper; ladder flags cleared

Research (3 searches, 2 fetches):
- 1707.07059 (anti-D3 in non-linear SUGRA, GKP throat): the uplift is M⁴e^{4A₀}/(T+T̄)³, and complex-structure dependence enters only through the warp factor, i.e. the conifold modulus. The paper REQUIRES the uplift to be independent of the other complex-structure moduli. A toroidal τ has no warping, so the tree-level τ-dependence is zero.
- hep-th/0111025 (brane–antibrane on tori): the image sum is the torus Green's function G(ξ), which "depends on the other moduli of the torus"; it is not written as an Epstein/Eisenstein function, nor extremised in U. No hexagonal case.
Derivation:
1. At tree level an anti-D3 on an unwarped torus gives V_up independent of τ [literature] (1707.07059: the warp factor is the only complex-structure dependence).
2. So any τ-dependence of K^{XX̄} is loop-level. The natural candidate is the BHK-type annulus (KK/winding sums on T²), which produces Epstein sums E(τ,s) [literature] (BHK hep-th/0508043; D756).
3. The needed form is K^{XX̄} = a − b/E(τ,2) with a, b > 0, i.e. K_XX̄ = 1/(a − b/E) ≈ (1/a)[1 + b/(aE) + …]: a correction to the goldstino metric that DECREASES as the torus elongates (∝ y⁻² at the cusp) [derived].
4. A BHK-like correction instead enters ADDITIVELY in E: K_XX̄ = k₀ + k₁E. That gives V ⊃ |F|²/(k₀ + k₁E) [derived]:
   - k₁ > 0: V falls toward the cusp, i.e. a hilltop at ρ, not a minimum (wrong shape).
   - k₁ < 0: the metric turns negative at y ~ (k₀/|k₁|)^{1/2} (inconsistent).
5. A Casimir-type annulus vacuum energy V ⊃ −c·E(τ,s)/A^s is unbounded below toward the cusp [derived]; it is not a plateau.
6. Hence none of the standard one-loop routes gives P3's form. The plateau needs b/E, i.e. the E-function in the DENOMINATOR of the metric correction [derived]. This is possible if the goldstino wave-function is renormalised by a quantity ∝ 1/E (e.g. a loop of states whose masses grow with E) [postulate P3, unchanged].
VERDICT: P3 stays OPEN, sharpened. New falsifier added: a computation of the anti-D3 annulus on T⁶/(Z₂×Z₂) that gives the one-loop goldstino-metric correction as k₁E(τ,2) (additive) with no 1/E piece would refute P3's string origin (though not the phenomenology).

## D799 (FORWARD, i-side; Jl tick 38; research + derivation, no lock): the gaugino-condensate placement for P3 fails. Modular weight forces the condensate to GROW toward the cusp, so "uplift minus condensate" is unbounded below, not a plateau
Research (1 search, 1 fetch): Leedom, Righi, Westphal, "Heterotic de Sitter beyond modular symmetry" (2212.03876):
- Condensate superpotential W = Ω(S)H(T)/η⁶(T), with H = (G₄/η⁸)ⁿ(G₆/η¹²)ᵐ P(j). The weight (−3) fixes the η⁻⁶.
- The scalar potential "diverges as Im T → ∞".
- The fixed points i, ρ are always extrema. Class B with n = 0 has a dS minimum at ρ for A(S,S̄) > 3; at i a minimum only for 0.40 < A < 3.60 (m = 0).
- With Green–Schwarz mixing, the weight moves into K_S = −ln(S + S̄ + δ_GS ln(y|η|⁴)) = −ln(S + S̄ − δ_GS Δ).
Derivation:
1. The weight-(−3) rule forces W ∝ η⁻⁶ × (holomorphic modular function) [literature] (2212.03876; FILQ 1990).
2. A modular function holomorphic on the fundamental domain, including at i and ρ, is a polynomial in j (up to the G₄, G₆ factors with fixed zeros) [literature]. So |H| ≥ const at the cusp, growing as e^{2πy·deg P} [derived].
3. So e^K|W|² ∝ y⁻³|η|⁻¹²|H|² ≳ y⁻³e^{πy}. The condensate contribution GROWS like e^{πy} toward the cusp [derived]; it can never be the decaying e^{−cΔ} needed for a plateau approach.
4. Hence V = V0[1 − (y|η|⁴/(y|η|⁴)_ρ)^c] is not realised by standard modular-invariant condensation. "Uplift − condensate" gives V → −∞; "uplift + condensate" gives a wall, not a plateau [derived].
5. Green–Schwarz mixing does not rescue it: the τ-dependence enters K_S as S + S̄ − δ_GS Δ, which for δ_GS > 0 makes e^{K_S} = 1/(2Re S − δ_GS Δ) GROW with Δ (and diverge where δ_GS Δ = 2 Re S) [derived].
6. The hypothetical form's n_s, r were NOT computed (no lock): a model that the framework forbids does not justify a computation (cost rule β5) [derived].
VERDICT: P3 stays open; a second placement route is closed (D797: annulus/Casimir; D799: condensate). Both standard sources put Δ or E where it grows at the cusp.
A plateau needs a τ-dependence that SATURATES at the cusp (ratio forms, X/(X+1)). Only metric-inverse placement (K^{XX̄}) does that naturally, which is exactly P3's assumption.
Side result for the mirror: 2212.03876 singles out ρ as the dS-minimum point of the condensate potential (Class B, n = 0, A > 3). ρ is therefore a natural moduli-stabilisation point in heterotic condensation, independent of our plateau.

## D801 (FORWARD, i-side; Jl tick 40; locked PREREG_D801; results/saddle_i_d801.txt): every one-loop lattice sum puts its vacuum at ρ; i is a saddle. Added to the paper as the reason the ρ branch is better motivated

1. The BHK correction enters as e^{K⁽¹⁾}, with K⁽¹⁾ = C·E(τ,2) (D689), and multiplies the whole F-term potential: V = P(τ)[1 + C(E − E_ref)] [literature] (BHK; derived in D689).
2. On the i branch P(i) = 0 and ∇P(i) = 0, so Hess V(i) = [1 + C(E(i) − E_ref)]·Hess P(i) [derived]. E's negative arc curvature drops out, and i stays a minimum for any C with 1 + CẼ(i) > 0 [derived].
3. The leading NON-multiplicative piece comes from K⁽¹⁾ breaking no-scale in K^{ττ̄}|D_τW₀|²: the cross term 2Re(K^{ττ̄}K_τ̄ ∂_τK⁽¹⁾)|W₀|² is linear in C [derived]. At i, ∂E = 0, but its second derivative ∝ C·E_xx·|W₀|²·O(1) [estimate].
4. With the covariant completion's |W₀|² ~ V0/3 (f² = 3|W₀|²), that additive curvature is ~C·V0·O(1), so it matters only for C ≳ 1e-4 [estimate]. The natural BHK size C ~ 1e-6 (D691/D696) is ~100× below [derived].
5. Hence the τ = i branch is NOT destabilised toward ρ inside a BHK orientifold. The D801 lattice argument concerns where a one-loop function puts the vacuum by itself, not whether a hand-built vacuum at i survives a small one-loop correction [derived].
D689 already noted "this correction is multiplicative, so it gives NO vacuum mass". This tick confirms the mirror statement: it gives no destabilisation either.
Paper: the D801 sentence ("a vacuum at i needs a hand-built function") is consistent with this; no change.

## D803 (FORWARD, i-side; Jl tick 42; research + derivation, no lock): the D801 caveat is REAL. Non-SUSY (Scherk–Schwarz) one-loop sums reduce the group and are minimised at 1 + i, an image of i, not at ρ. The paper sentence is qualified
Research (1 search, 2 fetches): Antoniadis, Diaz Avalos, Faraggi, "A perturbatively stable non-supersymmetric string model with AdS vacuum" (2504.19364):
- The one-loop potential is a fundamental-domain integral of shifted lattices. "SL(2,Z) is broken into a subgroup Γ" (they write Γ₁(2), eq. 2.31).
- The minimum is at the free-fermionic point T = U = 1 + i, with a positive-definite Hessian and Λ = −0.00789 M_s⁴ (AdS). m²_U = m²_T ≈ 0.03–0.06 M_s²g_s².
- Decompactification directions are unbounded below.
Derivation:
1. The Scherk–Schwarz shift splits the lattice into sectors with signs (−1)^{m}; the one-loop energy is a difference of shifted sums, not a positive combination [literature] (2504.19364).
2. The invariance group is an index-3 congruence subgroup (Γ⁰(2)/Γ₀(2)/Γ₁(2), conjugate up to sign). It has ONE elliptic point of order 2 (at 1 + i or (1+i)/2, both SL(2,Z) images of i) and NO elliptic point of order 3 [literature] (standard: index 3, ε₂ = 1, ε₃ = 0).
3. So under the reduced group ρ is not a symmetry-enforced critical point, while the image of i is [derived]. The computed minimum at 1 + i realises this [literature].
4. Hence D801's "lattice sums select ρ" holds for POSITIVE (supersymmetric) sums only. Mixed-sign non-SUSY sums can select an image of i [derived].
5. Consequence for the branches: the τ = i branch has a one-loop motivation in non-SUSY Scherk–Schwarz settings, and SERAPIS-E's ρ in supersymmetric BHK settings [derived]. Our plateau sector (anti-D3, nilpotent X) is supersymmetric up to the nilpotent breaking, so the BHK picture is the relevant one for SERAPIS-E [estimate].
6. The flavour group at 1 + i: a T-translate of i, so Γ₂ ≅ S₃ forms transform with a fixed relabelling; whether the residual stabiliser keeps D785's prompt-decay structure is the mirror question for the next tick [estimate].
Paper: the D801 sentence is qualified. It now states the positive-weight condition and the non-SUSY exception, with ref 2504.19364.

## D804 (REVERSE, ρ-side; Jl tick 43; derivation + exact group arithmetic, no lock): under a reduced (non-SUSY) group, the τ = i branch keeps its qualitative structure but loses its flavour predictions; SERAPIS-E needs the FULL SL(2,Z). Added to the paper's Limitations
Group facts (checked in code):
- M = TST⁻¹ = [[1,−2],[1,−1]] has b even, so M ∈ Γ⁰(2). M² = −1 (order 2 in PSL) and M fixes 1 + i.
- No element of Γ⁰(2) with |tr| = 1 (order 3) exists among the entries ≤ 6 (count 0). In general ε₃(Γ⁰(2)) = 0.
Derivation:
1. Γ(2) ⊂ Γ⁰(2) ⊂ SL(2,Z), with S₃ = SL(2,Z)/Γ(2) and Γ⁰(2)/Γ(2) ≅ Z₂ [literature].
2. The surviving Z₂ is generated by the image of M = TST⁻¹, a transposition of S₃ conjugate to S. The 3-cycle (ST) and the other two transpositions are lost [derived].
3. Level-2 forms are still forms of Γ(2), so the weight-2 doublet exists, but under Z₂ it splits as 1 ⊕ 1′ with INDEPENDENT couplings [derived]. Predictions built on doublet relations (D664, D690's splittings 0.08–0.47, D738's ΔM/M = 0.6–11) become free parameters [derived].
4. The vacuum residual at 1 + i is Z₂ = ⟨M⟩, the same as at i in the full group. The heavy states are again parity eigenstates, so D785's prompt decays and D794–D795's no-carrier result hold [derived].
5. At ρ, Γ⁰(2) has no order-3 element, so ρ (and every image) has a trivial stabiliser [derived]. The following are lost:
   - the symmetry-enforced critical point at ρ;
   - the isotropic Hessian (D796);
   - the residual Z₃ (D777: degenerate pair, baryon triality D787, the self-diluted history D792–D793).
6. Hence SERAPIS-E REQUIRES the full SL(2,Z), i.e. supersymmetric-type (positive) one-loop sums. This is consistent with D803 step 5 [derived].
Paper: one Limitations item added (SERAPIS-E needs the full SL(2,Z); what a Scherk–Schwarz breaking would remove; the τ = i branch at 1 + i keeps its Z₂, but its doublet splits into free singlets).

5. The species-scale one-loop term: ∝ (m₃/₂/H)² ~ R, as small as (1) [derived] (D685 2a).
6. A logarithmic correction in the anti-D3 warp/metric sector, f → f(1 + b ln(1 + |j−1728|/1728)), would reproduce εI₁ with b ≈ 0.02 [postulate P3] (D686: an uncomputed string correction).
Verdict: the τ = i vacuum mass and tilt come from ONE fitted term (ε I₁). No derived source is within 10¹¹ of the required size. The only candidate (item 6) lives in the same anti-D3 sector as P3, so it would be settled by the P3 computation (queue item 10, which needs Danny's OK).

## D828 (P3 DEEP PROJECT, step P3.1; Danny approved 08:13 CT; literature: 3 searches, 2 fetches): known one-loop vacuum energies of brane-supersymmetry-breaking and Scherk–Schwarz orientifolds depend on the torus shape ADDITIVELY, through (shifted) Epstein lattice sums. None has the ratio form 1 − E(ρ)/E(τ) that P3 needs
Literature:
- Non-SUSY IIB orientifold on T⁶/Z₂′×Z₂′ with brane supersymmetry breaking, 16 D3s on O3^± planes (2512.20570):
  - the open-sector (Möbius) vacuum energy VANISHES for equal-rank USp/SO stacks;
  - the closed-sector Scherk–Schwarz Casimir energy is V ∝ −M_s⁴ λ (Im T)⁻² E₃(U), with E₃(U) = Σ (Im U)³/|p + (2q+1)U|⁶, a Γ₁(2)-type shifted Epstein sum. It is NEGATIVE, grows ∝ y³ at the cusp (unbounded below), and is ADDITIVE.
- Antoniadis–Benakli–Quirós (hep-ph/0004091), anti-brane sector:
  - the one-loop potential is a Möbius amplitude with momentum and winding lattice sums;
  - brane positions and Wilson lines enter as cosine characters;
  - its contribution to the vacuum energy is positive, falling as 1/R² at large radius;
  - the mass² of position moduli is negative at a = 0, with the minimum at the half-period a = 1/4 (the anti-brane sits at a half-period fixed point).
Derivation:
1. The tree-level anti-D3 uplift has no torus-shape dependence without warping [literature] (1707.07059; D797).
2. One-loop open (Möbius/annulus) and closed (torus) vacuum energies are closed-channel lattice sums. At fixed area their shape dependence is Σ' (Im U)^s/|m + nU|^{2s} with characters (E(U,s) and shifted versions), entering V ADDITIVELY [literature] (2512.20570; hep-ph/0004091; BHK).
3. E(U,s) grows ∝ y^s at the cusp, so an additive ±cE gives a wall (+) or V → −∞ (−). Neither is a plateau [derived] (D797 points 4–5).
4. In non-linear SUGRA, V_up = |F|²K^{XX̄}. An additive one-loop vacuum energy corresponds to K^{XX̄} ⊃ +cE/|F|², i.e. E in the NUMERATOR, while P3 needs K^{XX̄} = a − b/E [derived].
5. So no known one-loop amplitude produces P3's form at leading order [derived]. P3 would need either (a) a resummed or non-perturbative structure in which E appears inverted (e.g. a wave-function factor Z_X = 1 + cE with the uplift ∝ 1/Z_X, which D797 showed gives a hilltop), or (b) a different physical origin of the plateau [estimate].
6. Positive lesson for P3.2: the half-period placement of the anti-brane (ABQ minimum at a = 1/4) and the character structure (D689 style) are standard. The P3.2 amplitude can therefore be set up concretely, and its s, sign and character content determined [derived].
Status: P3 is NOT supported by the one-loop literature. It stays open as a postulate until P3.2–P3.4 compute the actual amplitude for our configuration.

## D829 (DEEP, P3.2): the anti-D3 interaction on the inflaton T² for our configuration
Lock: PREREG_D829_antiD3_green.md (committed before the run). Script theory/modular/antiD3_green_d829.py, output field_tests/results/antiD3_green_d829.txt.
Setup [derived]: the leading anti-D3–D3/O3 interaction is closed-string exchange, i.e. a Coulomb potential in the transverse space. On the inflaton T² (other tori small), this is the torus Green's function G(z,U) = −ln|θ₁(πz|U)/η|² + 2π(Im z)²/Im U. Its closed-channel form is Σ' over windings with characters e^{2πi(m·z)}: the shifted lattice sums of D828, with s → 1 (two transverse directions on T²). The coincident term regularises to the Kronecker limit Δ(U) = −ln(Im U |η|⁴), i.e. E(U,s) at s → 1 minus its pole.
Results:
1. The sum over the three half-periods S(U) = Σ_k G(z_k,U) = −2 ln 2 = −1.38629 at EVERY U tested (i, ρ, ½+2i … ½+20i) [derived]. Analytically: θ₂θ₃θ₄ = 2η³, and the 2π(Im z)² terms cancel the q^{1/8} prefactors. So the 5/5/5 stuck D3s exert NO U-dependent force on an anti-D3 at the origin. The pre-stated prediction "S grows linearly in y" was WRONG; reported as such.
2. Case A (anti-D3 at the origin, coincident with the N₀ = 1 D3/O3 image): V_int ∝ N₀ Δ(U), with Δ = 1.0547 (i), 1.0335 (ρ), 1.401, 3.627, 8.169, 17.948 (y = 2, 5, 10, 20). Grows ≈ πy/3 at large y [derived].
3. Case B (anti-D3 at a half-period, the ABQ-preferred placement): V_int ∝ 5Δ + 5S − 4G(½) = −0.272 (i), +0.085 (ρ), −2.76, −4.20, −2.43, +4.58 (y = 2 … 20) [derived, arithmetic on the locked output]. Not monotone: the near-cancellation between 5Δ and 4G(½) leaves a residual that changes sign.
4. Character content and sign [derived]: s = 1 (two transverse directions on T²; 4 non-compact + 4 on the small tori are integrated out); characters are the half-period shifts (−1)^{m}, (−1)^{n}, (−1)^{m+n}; the anti-D3–D3 pair attracts (opposite RR charge, same NSNS), so the physical sign is negative on G, i.e. V_int = −κ·[sum], κ > 0 [estimate: κ ∝ T₃²/(Vol of the small tori)].
5. Key question for P3.3 [derived]: the anti-D3 sector enters V ADDITIVELY through Δ- and G-type terms (E(U,1) Kronecker forms). It does not change K_XX̄ at this order; the wave function of the inflaton is untouched. This confirms D828 point 4 for our configuration: E appears in the numerator, P3's inverted form does not arise.
6. Large-y behaviour [derived]: in case A, −κΔ ≈ −κπy/3, i.e. V decreases linearly in y. That is a TILT term of the εI₁/L type (linear in y = e^{√2 φ}... i.e. exponential in φ), not a 1/E plateau. In case B the leading y-terms partly cancel.
Verdict: P3.2 done. The anti-D3 amplitude for our configuration is a sum of additive E(U,1)-type terms with a U-independent half-period piece. P3's ratio form K^{XX̄} = a − b/E does not arise at one loop. P3.3 (placement: case A vs B and its stability) and P3.4 (size κ vs the plateau, is the tilt dangerous?) remain.
Sources: Polchinski Vol. 1 §7.2 (torus Green's function) [literature]; 1707.07059; 2512.20570; hep-ph/0004091 (via D828).

## D830 (DEEP, P3.3): where the anti-D3 can sit; tadpole and stability
Derivation only (no new numbers; values from D696 and D829).
1. Tadpole [derived from D696's rule 3N + N0 + N_flux = 16]: an anti-D3 carries −1 unit, so the D3 side must carry 17: 3N + N0 − N_anti + N_flux = 16. D829's input (5, 1) plus one anti-D3 VIOLATES the tadpole. Consistent options: (N, N0) = (5, 2), N_eff = 3; or (5, 1) with one D3's worth of flux replaced (flux is ISD and cannot cancel anti-D3 charge without a throat) [derived]. Taking (5, 2): N_eff = 3, and D696's table gives Im S·Im ρ ≈ 563–731 for n_s 0.970–0.975, still natural [derived].
2. Coincidence = annihilation [literature: brane–antibrane open-string tachyon at separation below the string length (Sen; Banks–Susskind)]. D829 case A (anti-D3 on top of the origin D3) and case B (on top of the 5-stack at ½) both put the anti-D3 ON D3s. Both are unstable: the pair annihilates. So D829's Δ (coincident) term describes a configuration that does not survive [derived]. D829's half-period result S = −2 ln 2 is unaffected (it is a sum over separated stacks).
3. Earnshaw on the torus [derived]: a mobile anti-D3 feels V(z) = −κ Σ_j q_j G(z − z_j), and the torus Green's function obeys ∇²G = −δ + 1/Area. Away from sources the Hessian trace is fixed by the uniform background term, and near each D3 stack V → −∞ logarithmically (attraction). A mobile anti-D3 on T² therefore falls into the nearest D3 stack: no stable interior minimum near a stack [derived; sign of κ from D829 point 4, an estimate].
4. The only safe placement [derived]: the anti-D3 STUCK at an O3 fixed point of T⁶ that carries no D3. T⁶/(Z₂×Z₂) has 64 O3 points; the D696 configuration occupies at most 4 of the inflaton-torus fixed points × one point on the other T⁴. A stuck anti-D3 at a fixed point displaced in the T⁴ directions has no position moduli (like the stuck D3s, hep-th/0602038), so its position is stable by construction and does not move as U rolls.
5. Consequence for the T² amplitude [derived]: with a T⁴ separation d, the coincident Δ term is replaced by the sum over T⁴ windings with T⁴ characters; the T²-shape dependence is still additive E(U,s)-type sums (D828/D829), now finite. The anti-D3 also enters the BHK D3-charge sum of D696 with charge −1 at its T² fixed point, shifting N_eff by ±1 depending on which T² point it projects to [estimate; to compute in P3.4].
6. ABQ a = 1/4 argument [derived]: the half-period preference of the anti-brane is a Wilson-line/position minimum for MOBILE branes; for a stuck anti-D3 it is moot, the position is fixed by the orientifold.
Verdict: placement settled. Anti-D3 stuck at an empty O3 point, displaced in T⁴; D-charge (5, 2) to satisfy the tadpole. D829's case A/B are both annihilating and are retired as physical configurations; its additive-in-V conclusion stands. P3 still gets no inverted 1/E form. P3.4: size of the additive term (κ, finite T⁴ sum) vs the plateau, and the shift of N_eff.
Sources: hep-th/0602038 (stuck branes, tadpole; via D696); Sen, hep-th/9805170 (brane–antibrane tachyon); Banks–Susskind hep-th/9511194.

## D832 (DEEP, P3.5): P3 verdict
Summary of D828–D831 [derived]:
1. One-loop vacuum energies are additive lattice sums (D828). For our configuration the anti-D3 sector gives additive E(U,1)-type terms; K_XX̄ is unchanged at this order (D829).
2. The only stable, tadpole-consistent placement is a stuck anti-D3 at an empty O3 point displaced in T⁴, with D3 stacks (5, 2) (D830). This corrects D696's (5, 1) whenever an anti-D3 is present.
3. Its T²-shape term is a rising wall, V ≈ +(4π/3)κy, mildly favouring ρ (D831). P3 needs V → const at large y. Opposite asymptotics.
Verdict: KEEP P3 as a postulate, DOWNGRADED. It has no one-loop origin in our configuration, and the anti-D3 one-loop term cannot be the plateau. P3 is not retired: the plateau V0[1 − E(ρ)/E(τ)] is the model's defining input, and its phenomenology (frozen band, D692) is unaffected. What could still give it [estimate]:
 (a) a warped throat: the uplift then depends on the throat's position/shape moduli, which can couple to U through the warp factor (not computed; tree-level unwarped has no U dependence, 1707.07059);
 (b) non-perturbative: a resummed or instanton-corrected K^{XX̄} in which E appears inverted (no known example; D797, D799 closed the simple cases);
 (c) a different plateau origin altogether (not the anti-D3 sector).
Side results to keep [derived]: the anti-D3 wall is bounded at large y, so it is a candidate stabiliser of the decompactification direction, and it has an extremum at τ = i (Δ and the half-period sums are modular-symmetric there), so it is a candidate source for the τ = i vacuum mass (D826). Whether it is big enough needs κ's normalisation (open, D831 point 4).
Falsifier (for P3 as stated): an explicit warped-throat computation in which the anti-D3 uplift depends on U only additively would remove route (a).

## D833 (DEEP, K.1): normalisation of the anti-D3 term
Lock: PREREG_D833_kappa.md (committed before the run). Script theory/modular/kappa_d833.py, output field_tests/results/kappa_d833.txt.
Derivation [derived, with literature inputs]:
1. Per closed-string sector two parallel D3s have |V| = 2κ₁₀²T₃²G₆(r), ∇²G₆ = −δ⁶ [literature] (Polchinski Vol. 2 §13.3). For D3–anti-D3 both sectors attract: −2·2κ₁₀²T₃²G₆.
2. T₃ = 1/((2π)³α'²g_s), 2κ₁₀² = (2π)⁷α'⁴g_s² give 2κ₁₀²T₃² = 2π exactly (checked in code) [derived].
3. T⁴ zero mode: G₆ ⊃ G(z,U)/(4π Vol₄), with D829's G (∇²G = −4πδ). Matching D831's V = −2κB: κ = 2π/(4π Vol₄) = 1/(2Vol₄) [derived].
4. The unwarped anti-D3 uplift is V0 = 2T₃. Both energies sit at the anti-D3, so frame factors cancel in the ratio. With Vol₄ = (2π)⁴α'²v₄: κ/V0 = g_s/(8π v₄) [derived].
Numbers [derived]: D831's slope bound κ/V0 ≲ 2.9e-3/y* is 2.0–2.1e-4 for y* = 13.8–14.7. Hence v₄ ≳ (189–202)·g_s: v₄,min ≈ 10 (g_s = 0.05), 19–20 (0.1), 38–40 (0.2), 57–60 (0.3). Pre-stated prediction (100–200 g_s, 10–60) CONFIRMED.
Interpretation: the anti-D3 wall is harmless for the band if the four small directions have volume ≳ 20 string units at g_s = 0.1 (each small torus area ≳ 4.4 in (2π√α')² units). Mild and natural; it is also what the T⁴-zero-mode reduction already assumes (T⁴ not sub-stringy).
Caveats [estimate]: (a) O(1) factors in the per-sector amplitude (a factor 2 shifts v₄,min by 2); (b) V0 = 2T₃ identifies the plateau height with the unwarped anti-D3 uplift, i.e. the P3 picture; with warping the interaction and the tension warp differently, not computed; (c) twisted-sector exchange at the fixed points is not included.
Next: K.2 is largely answered here (bound vs natural size). K.3: does the same κ give the τ = i vacuum mass m²/H² ≈ 2e-3 (D826)? The upper end of κ (v₄ near its minimum) is the most favourable case.

## D837 (DEEP, W.1): warped anti-D3 uplift and the bulk complex structure (literature)
Searches: 3; fetched 1809.06861 (Bena–Dudas–Graña–Lüst) and 2105.03370 (Bento–Chakraborty–Parameswaran–Zavala), first sections only.
Findings:
1. The conifold modulus S (deformation of the KS throat) is a complex-structure modulus with a GVW superpotential term −M F_S − τK S, F_S = (S/2πi)(log(Λ₀³/S) + 1) + …; its SUSY minimum is s_KS ≃ Λ₀³ e^{−2πK/(g_sM)} [literature] (1809.06861 eqs. 2.5, 2.16, 2.19).
2. The S potential depends on the bulk complex-structure moduli Z^I only indirectly: "F_UV(Z^I)" does not depend on S, and the coupling runs through τ and the volume prefactor (Im ρ)³ [literature] (1809.06861 §2).
3. Warping couples S to the VOLUME modulus in the Kähler potential (the warped term in K_SS̄ ∝ 1/|S|^{4/3}); the anti-D3 energy grows with |S| and is minimised at the tip; too small a hierarchy gives a conifold runaway [literature] (1809.06861; 2105.03370 abstract and §1; 1809.06618).
4. The bulk modulus U can enter the uplift only through the throat's UV data: the cutoff Λ₀ (the matching of the conifold period to the bulk periods) and the flux numbers. V_up ∝ |s_KS|^{4/3} ∝ |Λ₀|⁴ e^{−8πK/(3g_sM)} up to volume factors [derived from 1, 3; estimate on the Λ₀ power].
Assessment:
5. This is a MULTIPLICATIVE dependence, V_up = V0·f(U) with f = |Λ₀(U)|⁴ (normalised), not the additive one-loop form of D828–D836. A multiplicative f(U) is structurally able to produce a plateau shape, which the one-loop route was not [derived].
6. STRUCTURAL OBSTACLE [derived]: T⁶/(Z₂×Z₂) has no conifold point and hence no KS throat. A warped anti-D3 needs a Calabi–Yau with a conifold degeneration (e.g. a resolved/deformed version of the orbifold, with the throat at a former fixed locus). So route (a) means leaving the toroidal model of D689–D696 for its CY resolution, where the BHK coefficient C and the stack counting would need to be recomputed.
7. Requirement for P3 via route (a) [derived]: f(U) = |Λ₀(U)|⁴ must equal 1 − E(ρ)/E(U) (up to normalisation), i.e. the throat's UV cutoff must depend on U like an inverse Epstein zeta. No source states any modular form for Λ₀(U); W.2 must decide whether such a dependence is even possible (Λ₀ comes from a holomorphic period, so |Λ₀|⁴ is |holomorphic|⁴, which cannot be the non-holomorphic E(U,2) ratio exactly).
Next: W.2: test point 7. If Λ₀(U) is a holomorphic period, |Λ₀|⁴ = |h(U)|⁴ with h of definite weight; check whether any such f can approach a constant at the cusp with a minimum at ρ (D685/D799 closed the holomorphic cases for W; the question is now for the cutoff).

## D838 (DEEP, W.2): a holomorphic throat cutoff cannot give SERAPIS-E's power-law plateau
Derivation only (no numerics).
Setup: D837 point 4 gives V_up = V0·f(U), with f built from the holomorphic period Λ₀(U). Duality invariance of V (under SL(2,Z) or any finite-index subgroup Γ, e.g. Γ⁰(2) after Scherk–Schwarz, D803a/D807) requires f to be invariant. The general invariant built from holomorphic data and the Kähler factor is a finite sum f = Σ_i c_i y^{w_i}|h_i(U)|², h_i holomorphic forms of weight w_i for Γ [derived].
1. Holomorphic modular forms of negative weight vanish, so w_i ≥ 0 [literature: standard; Diamond–Shurman].
2. At the cusp h_i = a_i q^{n_i}(1 + …): a term with n_i = 0 grows like y^{w_i}|a_i|²; a term with n_i > 0 (cusp form) decays like y^{w_i}e^{−4πn_i y} [derived].
3. f → a nonzero CONSTANT at the cusp therefore needs every non-cusp term to have w_i = 0. A weight-0 holomorphic form bounded at all cusps is constant [literature: Liouville on the compactified modular curve]. So f = c₀ + Σ(cusp-form terms): the approach to the plateau is EXPONENTIAL, f = c₀ − O(y^w e^{−2πy}) [derived]. (Poles, e.g. j(U), make f blow up at the cusp and are excluded.)
4. SERAPIS-E's P3 shape 1 − E(ρ)/E(U) approaches its plateau as a POWER LAW, 1 − E(ρ)/(2ζ(4)y²) (D691 point 2). A power-law approach cannot arise from any f in point 3 [derived].
Verdict: route (a) cannot reproduce P3 as stated, in any modular-invariant completion. It CAN give an exponentially approached plateau, f = c₀ − A y^w e^{−2πy}, which is the shape class of the older τ = i / ρ L-variant family (D685-era εI₁-type forms), not SERAPIS-E's. The only escapes are (i) breaking the modular symmetry of the uplift (the CY resolution's U need not keep SL(2,Z), but SERAPIS's foundation is that symmetry), or (ii) a non-holomorphic origin, which in string theory means loops, already closed by D828–D836.
Consequence for P3 [derived]: all three routes listed in D832 are now constrained: one-loop (closed, D828–D836), warped (cannot give the power law, this note; and needs leaving the torus, D837), non-perturbative holomorphic (closed by the same point 3 argument as D799). P3's E-ratio form has NO identified string origin. It stays a postulate.
Remaining for the project: W.3 (warped κ) is moot for P3's shape; it would only matter for the D835 bound if a throat is added. Recommend closing the warped-throat project at W.5 without W.3/W.4.
Sources: Diamond–Shurman, A First Course in Modular Forms, ch. 1–3 (weights, cusp forms) [literature]; D685, D691, D799, D837.

## D843 (DEEP, C.1): CP in string flavour models: the literature puts P1 under pressure
Searches: 3; fetched 2010.10782 (Ishiguro–Kobayashi–Otsuka) and 1901.03251 (Baur–Nilles–Trautner–Vaudrevange).
Findings:
1. In Type IIB CY orientifolds, CP is a symmetry of the 4D effective action: an outer automorphism of the symplectic modular group, acting as u → −ū, S → −S̄ [literature] (2010.10782 abstract, §2).
2. CP-invariant fluxes restrict W to odd or even polynomials; spontaneous CP violation then comes only from non-zero AXION vevs (Re u^i, Re S) [literature] (2010.10782 §3.2).
3. For toroidal-type prepotentials no CP-breaking flux vacua were found ("the prepotential having the toroidal structure does not lead to the spontaneous CP violation"); a non-toroidal example (CP_{11169}[18]) does break CP. Kähler-modulus axions were not analysed (they need non-perturbative stabilisation) [literature] (2010.10782 §4, conclusions).
4. In heterotic orbifolds CP is at least an outer automorphism of the flavour group, and its breaking "is then controlled by the vacuum expectation values of the moduli fields" [literature] (1901.03251).
5. 2405.18813 (the source of the retired P2) is itself a spontaneous-CPV-by-moduli mechanism [literature] (D764, D772).
Assessment [derived]:
6. P1 assumes the heavy-ν couplings carry INDEPENDENT O(1) phases with no imposed gCP. In string completions CP is a symmetry of the effective theory, so coupling phases are not free: CP violation must be SPONTANEOUS, from some modulus axion vev. P1's falsifier (i), "a UV completion that imposes gCP", is the GENERIC string expectation, not an exotic case.
7. Our compactification is toroidal (T⁶/(Z₂×Z₂)), and τ sits on a CP-conserving locus (Re τ = ½ at ρ, Re τ = 0 at i). Point 3 says flux-stabilised toroidal complex structures (and S) do not break CP. The remaining candidate sources in our setup are: Kähler-modulus axions (Re ρ_i, non-perturbative stabilisation, not studied in 2010.10782), and brane/Wilson-line moduli [derived].
8. P1 is NOT falsified (no data contradict it; D763 falsifier (ii) on δ_CP is untouched). It is UNMOTIVATED as stated: it should be reformulated as "CP is broken spontaneously by a Kähler axion or brane modulus", which C.2 tests on our configuration.
Falsifier status (D763) unchanged: (i) gCP-imposing UV completion — now the generic case, so P1 must name its breaking modulus; (ii) δ_CP ≈ 0/π at > 3σ weakly disfavours P1 (≈ 6% prior mass at |sin δ| < 0.1).
Sources: 2010.10782; 1901.03251; 1908.00805; 2105.02984; 2405.18813; 2206.08538; 2201.02020.
MAP: none

## D844 (DEEP, C.2): our configuration as specified has NO spontaneous CP source
Derivation only (no numerics). CP acts as U → −Ū, S → −S̄, ρ_i → −ρ̄_i, and on a brane position z on the inflaton T² as z → −z̄ (D843 point 1).
(a) Stuck D3 stacks [derived]. At ρ (Re U = ½): −Ū = U − 1 ≡ U, ½ → −½ ≡ ½, U/2 → −Ū/2 = U/2 − ½ ≡ (1+U)/2, and (1+U)/2 → U/2. So CP SWAPS the U/2 and (1+U)/2 stacks. The D696/D830 configuration has equal stacks there (5 and 5), so it is CP-invariant. At i every fixed point maps to itself. Stuck D3s have no continuous position moduli, and their discrete Wilson lines are Z₂-valued (holonomies ±1, real). CP-even. (An unequal pair, e.g. (5, 4), would break CP explicitly in the configuration, not spontaneously; D831 point 5 noted that an anti-D3 over a half-period makes stacks unequal in the BHK sum, but the anti-D3 sits at an EMPTY O3 point (D830), and its T² projection is itself a fixed point mapped as above, so the swap symmetry still holds if it projects to 0 or ½.)
(b) Kähler axions Re ρ_i [derived]. The tree-level K = −Σ ln(Im ρ_i) and the BHK correction (∝ 1/(Im S·Im ρ), D689) depend only on Im ρ. Our V has no term fixing Re ρ_i: they are perturbatively shift-symmetric and FLAT. Fixing them needs non-perturbative W ⊃ A e^{2πi a ρ}. With CP-invariant (real) W0 and A, a single exponential fixes Re ρ at 0 or 1/(2a): CP-conserving. A two-term racetrack with real coefficients generically also lands on CP-conserving values [estimate: standard for real coefficients; not proven for every racetrack].
(c) Axion-dilaton S and the other complex structures U₂, U₃ [literature + derived]: flux-stabilised in a toroidal prepotential, which gives no spontaneous CPV (2010.10782, D843 point 3). P2's U₂ route is retired (D772).
(d) τ itself sits on a CP-conserving locus (Re τ = ½ at ρ, 0 at i) [derived] (1905.11970 §4.3; P1 text).
Conclusion [derived]: every modulus in the specified configuration is either flat (Re ρ_i) or fixed at a CP-conserving value. The specified configuration has NO spontaneous CP source, so with CP a symmetry of the string effective theory (D843) the leptogenesis phase is δ = 0 at ρ and at i unless the model is extended.
What this does and does not mean:
- It does NOT contradict a frozen prediction: Y_B is a consistency requirement (fitted through T_R, ε_DI), not a frozen number.
- It DOES mean P1 cannot be realised inside the configuration as specified. P1 needs an extension that the model must name: (i) a non-toroidal sector (e.g. a CY resolution, where 2010.10782 found CP-breaking flux vacua), (ii) a racetrack with a CP-odd vacuum for a Kähler axion, or (iii) a hidden-sector CP source communicated to the heavy ν.
Next: C.3 asks whether option (ii) can be computed cheaply: a two-exponential racetrack for one Re ρ with real coefficients; scan for CP-odd minima (lock first). If none, C.4 verdict.
MAP: none

## D845 (DEEP, C.3): a CP-invariant racetrack DOES fix a Kähler axion at CP-odd values, usually as a metastable minimum
Lock: PREREG_D845_racetrack_cp.md (committed before the run). Script theory/modular/racetrack_cp_d845.py, output field_tests/results/racetrack_cp_d845.txt (overflow warnings come from minimiser excursions to t < 1, which are discarded by the locked filter).
Model: W = W0 + e^{2πiT/N1} + B e^{2πiT/N2}, real W0, B; K = −3 ln(−i(T − T̄)). 540 parameter points (5 ≤ N1 < N2 ≤ 10; W0 = ±1e-4, ±1e-3, ±1e-2; B = ±0.5, ±1, ±2).
Results [derived]:
1. 486 of 540 points (90.0%) have at least one CP-odd local minimum (s ∉ {0, L/2} mod L, t > 2, positive-definite Hessian). They come in mirror pairs s ↔ L − s, as CP requires.
2. Examples, N = (5, 6), W0 = +1e-4: B = +0.5 gives CP-odd minima at t ≈ 10.1 with V = −2.8e-12, while the deepest CP-even minimum has V = −5.0e-9 (CP-odd is METASTABLE, 3 orders shallower). B = ±1, ±2 give CP-odd minima within 1–2% of the CP-even depth (−2.31e-12 vs −2.36e-12; −1.93e-12 vs −1.94e-12).
3. Verdict rule: option (ii) VIABLE (CP-odd minima with t > 2 exist). Pre-stated prediction ("none") WRONG.
Interpretation [derived]: with two exponentials, the axion potential contains cos(2πs/N1), cos(2πs/N2) and cos(2πs(1/N1 − 1/N2)) terms with different periods; their competition produces local minima away from the CP-fixed points, in mirror pairs. This is spontaneous CP violation by a Kähler axion with entirely CP-invariant inputs.
Caveats [estimate]: (a) in the scan's examples the CP-odd minima are metastable or nearly degenerate with CP-even ones; which vacuum is selected is a cosmological question (initial conditions, tunnelling), not settled here; (b) AdS minima before uplift; the uplift (P3 sector) shifts them; (c) one Kähler modulus with K = −3 ln, not the full T⁶/(Z₂×Z₂) three-modulus structure.
Consequence for P1 [derived]: P1 can be REFORMULATED with a named source: "CP is broken spontaneously by a Kähler axion fixed in a CP-odd racetrack minimum". The leptogenesis phase is then not a free uniform variable but a function of the racetrack vacuum and of how the heavy-ν couplings depend on T. C.4 must state this and what it changes.
MAP: none

## D846 (DEEP, C.4): P1 verdict: reformulated as P1′ (spontaneous CP violation by a Kähler-axion racetrack)
Summary [derived]: CP is a symmetry of the string effective theory (D843); the specified configuration has no spontaneous CP source (D844); a CP-invariant two-exponential racetrack fixes a Kähler axion at CP-odd values in 90% of a scan, often metastably (D845).
Verdict: P1 as written (independent, uniformly distributed O(1) coupling phases) is REPLACED by
P1′: CP is broken spontaneously by the vev of a Kähler-modulus axion, fixed in a CP-odd minimum of a racetrack W = W0 + A e^{2πiT/N1} + B e^{2πiT/N2} with real (CP-invariant) coefficients. The heavy-ν couplings depend on T (through their Kähler/kinetic normalisation or holomorphic couplings), which transmits the phase.
What changes [derived]:
1. δ is no longer a free uniform variable: it is a function of the racetrack vacuum ⟨Re T⟩ and of the heavy-ν couplings' T-dependence. P1's "6% prior mass at |sin δ| < 0.1" (D763) no longer applies as a prior; it becomes a statement about the distribution of CP-odd vacua, which D845 did not compute.
2. The model gains named ingredients: two gaugino condensates (or instantons) on the same 4-cycle, and a coupling of the heavy-ν sector to that Kähler modulus.
3. Vacuum selection is an open condition: in D845's examples CP-odd minima are often metastable (one example 10³ shallower than the CP-even minimum), sometimes near-degenerate.
What stays [derived]: no frozen prediction changes. Y_B is a consistency requirement (fitted through T_R and ε_DI), not a frozen number.
New falsifiers for P1′:
(i) a demonstration that, in T⁶/(Z₂×Z₂)-type orientifolds, the Kähler moduli admit at most one non-perturbative term per 4-cycle (no racetrack), or that the heavy-ν sector cannot couple to a racetrack modulus;
(ii) (unchanged in spirit) leptonic CP conservation δ_CP ≈ 0/π at > 3σ (DUNE/Hyper-K) would disfavour any spontaneous-CPV scenario that also sets the low-energy phase, but P1′ ties the low-energy and leptogenesis phases only model-dependently, so this stays a weak test.
Open: the distribution of δ over CP-odd vacua, and the three-modulus racetrack; not started.
MAP: none
