## D851 (DEEP, Q.1): P1′ phases are generic, and CP-odd vacua are the DEEPEST in 41% of racetracks
Lock: PREREG_D851_racetrack_phases.md (committed before the run). Script theory/modular/racetrack_phases_d851.py (new; D845 not rerun), output field_tests/results/racetrack_phases_d851.txt.
Same model and grid as D845 (540 points). 2352 CP-odd minima with t > 2.
(a) Phases [derived]: θ₁ = 2π⟨Re T⟩/N1: |sin θ₁| > 0.1 in 100%, > 0.5 in 84.4%; histogram of |sin θ₁| (bins 0.0–1.0): 0, 12, 72, 100, 184, 308, 188, 248, 380, 860, peaked toward maximal CP violation. θ₂ = 2π⟨Re T⟩/N2: > 0.1 in 51.2%, > 0.5 in 13.1%. Which phase enters leptogenesis depends on which exponential the heavy-ν couplings carry (Q.2).
(b) Vacuum selection [derived]: the deepest minimum found is CP-ODD in 220/540 points (40.7%). Where the deepest is CP-even, the best CP-odd minimum is nearly degenerate: median V_odd/V_even = 0.954 (n = 266).
(c) Robustness [derived]: 400×400 vs 700×700 grids agree on the CP-odd count at 54/54 checked points.
(d) Uplift probe [derived]: lifting by |V of the deepest CP-even minimum| makes 62.7% of CP-odd minima dS. (Informative only where the deepest minimum is CP-even; where it is CP-odd, the uplift would be tuned to it instead.)
Verdict (locked rules): P1′ reproduces P1's phase support: |sin θ₁| > 0.1 in 100% (≥ 0.8 required) AND CP-odd deepest minima in 40.7% of points (≥ 20% required). PASS for θ₁. For θ₂ the phase rule fails (51% < 80%).
Pre-stated predictions: (a) "phases generic" CONFIRMED for θ₁, partly wrong for θ₂; (b) "CP-odd mostly metastable, ≤ 20%" WRONG: 40.7% are the deepest, and the rest are within ~5% of the CP-even depth.
Consequence [derived]: vacuum selection is not a strong obstacle for P1′: in ~41% of racetracks the true (deepest) AdS minimum is CP-violating, before uplift. The remaining dependence is Q.2: if the heavy-ν couplings carry the faster exponential (N1), P1′ gives an essentially generic phase (P1's old prior is reproduced or exceeded); if the slower one (N2), half the vacua give |sin| < 0.1.
Caveats [estimate]: one Kähler modulus, K = −3 ln, A = 1 fixed; deepest within t ∈ (1, 60).
MAP: none

## D852 (DEEP, Q.2): heavy-ν masses from instantons need two charge sectors; then the phase is generic in 80% of CP-odd vacua
Lock: PREREG_D852_instanton_phase.md (committed before the run). Script theory/modular/instanton_phase_d852.py, output field_tests/results/instanton_phase_d852.txt.
Derivation:
1. Majorana masses of right-handed neutrinos are typically forbidden perturbatively by brane U(1)s and generated by D-instantons, M = x M_s e^{−S_inst}, with the instanton on a rigid cycle different from the gauge branes [literature] (hep-th/0609191, IIA E2: S depends holomorphically on the cycle's modulus and carries an axion phase). In IIB with O3/O7 the analogue is a Euclidean D3 on a 4-cycle, M_ij = x M_s e^{2πi n_ij T} [derived, mirror of the IIA statement; estimate on details].
2. The Kähler normalisation K_NN̄ depends on Im T only: no phase [derived]. Dirac Yukawas are holomorphic in complex-structure moduli and real with τ on the CP locus [derived] (D844).
3. A single common instanton phase e^{2πinT} is removed by rephasing N; ε_CP ∝ Im[(Y†Y)_ij²] then vanishes. CP violation in leptogenesis requires entries with DIFFERENT instanton numbers (or different cycles), and the physical phase is Δ = 2πΔn⟨Re T⟩ [derived].
4. The racetrack's own condensate phases θ₁ = 2π⟨Re T⟩/N1, θ₂ (D851) are not the relevant ones for E3 masses; Δ uses the full period 1 [derived].
Numbers [derived]: over the 2352 CP-odd minima of the D845/D851 grid, |sin Δ₁| > 0.1 in 80.3%, > 0.5 in 51.7% (Δn = 1); |sin Δ₂| > 0.1 in 83.7%, > 0.5 in 56.3% (Δn = 2). Histogram of |sin Δ₁|: 464, 188, 172, 160, 152, 136, 192, 176, 224, 488 (peaks at both ends). CP-even minima give |sin Δ₁| ≤ 1.1e-6 (= 0), as required.
Verdict (locked rule, ≥ 80%): PASS, narrowly (80.3%). Pre-stated "passes" CONFIRMED; "close to uniform in angle" WRONG: 19.7% of CP-odd vacua have |sin Δ₁| < 0.1, versus 6.4% for a uniform angle; ⟨Re T⟩ clusters near multiples of ½.
Consequences: P1′ gains a structural condition: at least two instanton sectors with different charges contribute to the heavy-ν masses (2⊕1 at τ = i can supply this if the doublet and singlet masses come from different instanton numbers). P1's old "6% near zero" becomes ≈ 20% near zero under P1′, which weakens the D763 statement accordingly.
v3.2 draft: CP paragraph updated (D851 metastability wording; D852 two-sector condition and 80% figure); rebuilt, 16 pages, clean.
MAP: none

## D854 (R.1): at τ = i, single-modulus P1′ gives the resonant pair NO CP phase; τ = i leptogenesis then needs two cycle classes
Derivation only. The planned locked run was not needed: the result is exact at the level of charges, so no numbers were computed (PREREG_D854 not written).
Setup [derived]: D745/D763 resonant leptogenesis at τ = i uses the quasi-degenerate pair N₁, N₂ (the Γ2 doublet of the 2⊕1 structure, D664a, D690); its CP asymmetry ∝ Im H₂₁, H = Y†Y. Under P1′ the Dirac Yukawas are real (τ on the CP locus, D844) and all phases sit in the instanton-generated Majorana masses (D852).
1. Charge rule [derived]: an instanton wrapping n times a cycle class Ξ has action 2πnT_Ξ and absorbs U(1) charge n·I_{Ξ,a} (intersection numbers scale with wrapping). So on ONE cycle class the instanton number of entry M_ij is fixed by the charge it must absorb: n_ij ∝ q_i + q_j, linear in the charges (literature basis: zero-mode counting scales with intersections, hep-th/0609191).
2. The doublet members N₁, N₂ come from the same brane intersection, so q₁ = q₂: their Majorana entries carry the SAME phase e^{2πi n_dd T} [derived].
3. Doublet–singlet mixing cannot help on one cycle class [derived]: integrating out N₃ gives δM_dd ∝ M_ds²/M_ss ∝ e^{2πiT(2n_ds − n_ss)} = e^{2πiT(2(q_d+q_s) − 2q_s)/q₀} = e^{2πiT·2q_d/q₀}, the same phase as M_dd. Rephasing invariants of the pair vanish; Im H₂₁ = 0; ε = 0.
4. Hence D763's 68–71% pass fraction at τ = i becomes 0% under single-modulus P1′ [derived]. ρ (D853) is not affected in the same way: there the relevant N carry different charges, so D852's Δ = 2πΔn⟨Re T⟩ is physical.
Escape [derived]: instantons on at least TWO cycle classes with independent CP-odd axions (two racetracks, or doublet and mixing entries from different cycles). Then δM_dd carries 2πi(…)(T₁ − T₂)-type phases and Im H₂₁ ≠ 0. This is an extra condition specific to τ = i.
Consequence: a fourth condition for the τ = i conditional variant (D841): under P1′ its leptogenesis needs two CP-odd Kähler axions on different cycle classes. Not a failed prediction; a further structural requirement.
Caveat [estimate]: assumes Dirac Yukawas are perturbative and real and that the doublet shares one brane intersection; a doublet formed from two different intersections would change point 2.

## D853a (correction to D853 and to D854's ρ remark, found in D855)
1. D853 re-weighted D762's per-case thresholds, which belong to D731's ρ inflaton-decay leptogenesis. That route was already SUPERSEDED: at ρ the exact Z₃ forbids the renormalisable L·N·H decay of the charged pair N_n/N₃ (D780), the P5 route conserves B (D789), and the frozen ρ band has no baryogenesis mechanism; the only consistent ρ history is the post-hoc inflaton-AD one, which needs no CP phase (D792). So D853's ρ numbers (median 0.84, unconditional ≈ 0.34) describe a mechanism the model no longer uses. They are withdrawn as statements about SERAPIS; they remain correct as arithmetic on D762.
2. D854 asserted that at ρ "the relevant N carry different charges, so D852's Δ is physical". That was not checked. The ρ heavy states differ in Z₃ charge (N_Y: 0, N_n: q, N₃: −q; D780), but Z₃ is a modular charge, not a brane U(1) charge; whether they sit at different brane intersections is not determined by the model. The assertion is withdrawn as unsupported.
3. The V32_TODO optional clause [D853] (median 0.84) is withdrawn.

## D857 (DEEP, M.1): moduli requirements table; two conflicts flagged
Derivation only. Conventions [derived, standard IIB O3/O7 on T²×T²×T²]: torus areas A₁ (inflaton torus), A₂, A₃ in string units; the three untwisted 4-cycle Kähler moduli are Im T₁ ≈ A₂A₃/g_s, Im T₂ ≈ A₁A₃/g_s, Im T₃ ≈ A₁A₂/g_s (O(2π) factors not fixed here [estimate]); v₄ (D833) = A₂A₃ = g_s·Im T₁. D689's ρ is the inflaton torus's Kähler modulus (∝ A₁). Unresolved convention: D689 writes "g_s = 0.1 (Im S = 1.13)", not Im S = 1/g_s = 10; the factor ≈ 9 is not explained in D689 and must be fixed in M.2 [flag].
| # | Source | Requirement | In areas (g_s = 0.1) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | D696, D830 (BHK tilt, stacks (5,2)) | Im S·Im ρ₁ ≈ 560–975 | A₁ ∝ Im ρ₁ ≈ 56–98 (Im S = 10) or 500–860 (D689's Im S = 1.13) |
| 2 | D833, D835 (anti-D3 safe, only if the anti-D3 is present) | v₄ = A₂A₃ ≳ 2e4·g_s | A₂A₃ ≳ 2000 |
| 3 | D845, D851 (CP-odd racetrack on cycle T, W0 = 1e-4–1e-2, N = 5–10) | Im T ≈ N ln(1/W0)/2π ≈ 4–15 (t ≈ 10 in the examples) | the racetrack 4-cycle has A_jA_k ≈ 0.4–1.5 |
| 4 | D852, D854 (heavy-ν Majorana mass from an E3 on the racetrack cycle) | M ≈ x M_s e^{−2πn Im T} ≈ 6e10 (τ = i, D745) – 5e13 GeV (D731) | needs 2πn Im T ≈ 6–12, i.e. n Im T ≈ 1–2 |
| 5 | D783 (string scale) | M_s ≈ 5.6e15–2.6e16 GeV (isotropic-volume estimate) | used in row 4 |
Conflict A (racetrack cycle vs BHK and anti-D3) [derived, up to O(2π) factors]: the racetrack needs a 4-cycle with A_jA_k ≈ 1. T₁'s cycle has A₂A₃ ≳ 2000 if the anti-D3 is present (row 2); T₂ and T₃ contain A₁ ≈ 56–860 (row 1), forcing A₃ or A₂ ≲ 0.02, sub-stringy. So NO untwisted 4-cycle can host the CP-odd racetrack when rows 1 and 2 both hold. Without the anti-D3 (row 2 dropped), T₁ with A₂A₃ ≈ 1 is allowed.
Conflict B (instanton masses vs racetrack scale) [derived]: on one cycle the E3 action is N times the condensate exponent, so M/M_s ≈ (e^{−2π Im T/N})^N ≈ W0^N. Row 4 needs W0^N ≈ 2e-6–3e-3, i.e. W0 ≈ 0.07–0.3 for N = 5–10, outside D845/D851's scanned W0 ≤ 1e-2, and with Im T ≈ 1–2 (marginal control). D851's and D852's statistics were computed in a W0 range in which an E3 on the racetrack cycle gives M ≲ 1e-4 M_s·(1e-4)^{N−1}: far too light.
Escapes to test in M.2 [estimate]: (i) twisted (blow-up) Kähler moduli at the orbifold fixed points, which are small cycles and natural hosts for racetracks and fractional instantons (e^{−2π Im T/k}); (ii) drop the anti-D3 (P3 picture) or accept large v₄ only; (iii) fractional E3s on the racetrack cycle.
Status: M.1 done. Two genuine tensions between today's P1′ mechanism and the BHK/anti-D3 requirements, both conditional (anti-D3 present; E3 on the racetrack cycle). No frozen prediction is affected.

## D859 (DEEP, M.2): conventions fixed; twisted blow-up escape closed; fractional instantons remain
1. D689's Im S convention [derived, from the script]: theory/modular/bhk_tilt_d689.py line 62 uses Im S = 1/(2√2π g_s) (BHK normalisation), so Im S = 1.125 at g_s = 0.1. D696's Im S·Im ρ ≈ 560–975 therefore gives Im ρ₁ ≈ 500–870 in BHK's ρ units at g_s = 0.1. Converting BHK's ρ to a torus area in (2π√α')² units involves a factor up to 4π² ≈ 39 that is not fixed in our notes [estimate]; with it, A₁ ≈ 13–22, without it ≈ 500–870. D857's Conflict A numbers carry this ×40 uncertainty; M.3 must use one convention (BHK's) throughout.
2. Twisted moduli [literature]: for T⁶/(Z₂×Z₂′) the Hodge numbers are (h¹¹, h²¹) = (3, 51) WITH discrete torsion and (51, 3) without (0902.1694). Rigid (stuck) branes of the kind D696 uses (hep-th/0602038) require the discrete-torsion version [literature: rigidity comes from the twisted 3-cycles that exist only with torsion, 0902.1694]. So our model has h¹¹ = 3: only the three untwisted Kähler moduli, NO twisted blow-up Kähler moduli [derived from the two statements].
3. Escape (i) (racetrack on a small twisted Kähler cycle): CLOSED in our model [derived].
4. Escape (iii) (fractional instantons): OPEN. In this orbifold rigid E-branes have actions S = σ[T + twisted-moduli corrections] with σ a fraction set by the fixed-point structure (0902.1694; their E1 example), so E3-type instantons with σ < 1 on the untwisted 4-cycles can give e^{−2πσ Im T}, reducing Conflict B's mass suppression [literature + estimate; no E3 Majorana mass is computed there: the paper finds charged-field masses and says stable single E3 instantons are "possibly" present].
5. Escape (ii) (no anti-D3): OPEN; it removes row 2 of D857 and lets T₁'s cycle be small.
Status after M.2: Conflict A survives only if the anti-D3 is present AND the ×40 convention factor goes the unfavourable way; Conflict B is softened by fractional instantons (σ ≈ ¼–½ would need Im T ≈ 4–8 for M ≈ 1e11–1e13 GeV, inside D845's racetrack range).
M.3 will lock one convention set and scan for a common point, with σ ∈ {1, ½, ¼} and anti-D3 on/off.
Sources: 0902.1694; hep-th/0602038; hep-th/0305224 (magnetized Z₂×Z₂ orientifolds).

Verdicts (locked rule): anti-D3 ON: INCONSISTENT in every case. Anti-D3 OFF: CONSISTENT for σ ≤ ½ (and marginally σ = 1 with f = 4π²). Pre-stated prediction CONFIRMED (on: inconsistent; off: passes for σ ≤ ½).
Reading [derived]:
1. With the anti-D3 present, the BHK tilt (A₁ large), the anti-D3 safety bound (A₂A₃ ≳ 2e4 g_s) and a CP-odd racetrack on an untwisted 4-cycle (A_iA_j/g_s ≈ 2–15) cannot hold together: the three 4-cycles are all too large. This is Conflict A of D857, now confirmed across conventions and instanton fractions.
2. Without the anti-D3, the racetrack sits on the T⁴ cycle (Im T₁ = A₂A₃/g_s), which forces A₂ ≈ A₃ ≈ 1: the small tori at the string scale, the edge of geometric control (the passing examples all sit at the grid's lower boundary A = 1). The heavy-ν masses then need fractional instantons (σ ≤ ½) or the 4π² convention.
3. Physical consequence: P3's anti-D3 (nilpotent-sector) picture and P1′'s CP source are mutually incompatible in our configuration. A model that uses both is internally inconsistent; it must drop one. Dropping the anti-D3 leaves the plateau's sector (the nilpotent X) without its usual string realisation; dropping P1′ leaves τ = i without leptogenesis (D854). The ρ branch is unaffected in this respect (it needs no CP phase, D855).
Caveats [estimate]: O(1) factors in Im T_k = A_iA_j/g_s and in M_s; the grid edge at A = 1; σ values are assumed, not computed for E3s in this orbifold.

## D864: D7 stacks for the racetrack are allowed WITH CONDITIONS, and they feed the tilt
Searches 2, fetch 1 (hep-th/0602038, first part only: "1 O3 and 3 O7 planes"; its tadpole section was not reached). Derivation, all [estimate] unless marked.
1. O-planes [literature]: the T⁶/(Z₂×Z₂) orientifold of our setup has O3 planes and three sets of O7 planes, one per 4-cycle (hep-th/0602038 §2). So D7-branes wrapping the T⁴ cycle (T₁) are part of the standard spectrum.
2. Tadpole [estimate, standard counting]: the O7₁ charge is cancelled by D7₁ branes (plus magnetised-brane contributions) to a total of 16 in the usual normalisation. The racetrack needs 5 + 6 = 11 < 16, so the remaining 5 units go to other D7₁ (or flux-free spectators). Not a conflict. (Exact counts with images and torsion signs were not read; flagged.)
3. Rigidity [estimate]: with discrete torsion, D7s away from fixed points carry adjoint position moduli on T²₁; an adjoint chiral field blocks pure-SYM gaugino condensation unless it is massive. So the stacks must be fractional/rigid D7s stuck at fixed points of the INFLATON torus T²₁ (or their adjoints must get flux masses).
4. Flavours (D3–D7 strings) [derived from the setup]: a D7 stack at a fixed point of T²₁ meets the stuck D3s at that point; each D3 gives one flavour. ADS gaugino condensation needs N_f < N_c. With D3 stacks (5, 5, 5) at the half-periods and N0 = 2 at the origin (D830): SU(6) at a half-period has N_f = 5 < 6 ✓; SU(5) must avoid the half-periods (N_f = 5 = N_c: no condensate) and sit at the origin (N_f = 2 < 5 ✓). So the placement is forced: SU(5) at the origin, SU(6) at one half-period.
5. Consequence for the tilt [estimate]: D7 stacks at fixed points of T²₁ are points on the inflaton torus, so they enter the U₁-dependent one-loop sums exactly like D3s (BHK: D7_k terms ∝ ℰ(A,U₁)/(Im T_k·Im ρ₁) instead of 1/(Im S·Im ρ₁)). The forced placement is asymmetric, so it ADDS to the tilt. Rough ratio of D7 to D3 contributions: (N_D7 asymmetry·Im S)/(N_eff,D3·Im T₁) ≈ O(0.1–0.5) at the benchmark (Im S = 0.485, Im T₁ = 4.31); the sign depends on which fixed points carry the stacks. The benchmark's Im S·Im ρ₁ must shift by this fraction to keep C in band. Not a contradiction (C is fitted), but the D861 benchmark is not final.
6. BHK sum of D689: modified as in point 5; D689's D3-only coefficient becomes D3 + D7 (open).
Verdict: ALLOWED WITH CONDITIONS: (a) D7₁ total ≤ 16 (11 used); (b) rigid/fractional D7s at T²₁ fixed points (torsion), or flux-massive adjoints; (c) SU(5) at the origin, SU(6) at a half-period (flavour counting); (d) the D7 stacks' one-loop sums shift the tilt by O(10–50%), requiring a re-fit of the benchmark moduli.
Sources: hep-th/0602038; hep-th/0506252; hep-th/0610327 (review); 0902.1694.

## D864a (correction to D864 point 4)
D864 said the placement is "forced: SU(5) at the origin, SU(6) at a half-period". That was wrong on two counts. (i) Not forced: SU(6) can also sit at the origin (N_f = 2 < 6). (ii) A single stack at ONE half-period breaks the permutation symmetry of the three half-periods, i.e. it breaks SL(2,Z) of the inflaton torus. The v3.1/v3.2 paper already states that unequal brane numbers at the three half-periods remove SERAPIS-E's ρ vacuum, its isotropic mass and the residual Z₃. Putting SU(6) at a half-period would therefore destroy SERAPIS-E itself, and a symmetric copy at all three half-periods needs 18 + 5 = 23 D7s > 16 (tadpole). Corrected placement: BOTH stacks (SU(5) and SU(6)) at the origin; flavours N_f = N0 ≤ 2 for each, condensation allowed, SL(2,Z) kept.

## D865: with both D7 stacks at the origin, the tilt survives but is reduced; the benchmark must be re-fitted by ×0.4–0.85
Derivation + arithmetic (no lattice run: the symmetric placement reduces to D696's formula, so no new lattice sums are needed).
1. D7 stacks at the origin of T²₁ enter the U₁ one-loop sum like an origin stack (D696: tilt ∝ N − N₀ for equal half-period stacks), but with the D7₁ normalisation: BHK's D7_k terms carry 1/(Im T_k·Im ρ₁) instead of the D3 terms' 1/(Im S·Im ρ₁) [estimate on the structure; the exact BHK D7 coefficient was NOT looked up this tick: written as r·(D3 coefficient), r = O(1)].
2. Effective tilt count: N_eff = (N − N₀) − 11·r·(Im S/Im T₁). At the benchmark Im S/Im T₁ = 0.485/4.31 = 0.113, so the D7s subtract 0.62 (r = ½), 1.24 (r = 1), 2.48 (r = 2) [derived arithmetic].
3. With no anti-D3 ((5,1), N − N₀ = 4): N_eff = 3.38 / 2.76 / 1.52 → the required Im S·Im ρ₁ rescales by ×0.85 / 0.69 / 0.38. With an anti-D3 ((5,2), 3): ×0.79 / 0.59 / 0.17 (the anti-D3 case is already excluded by D860).
4. The tilt keeps its sign for r ≲ 3 (no anti-D3); the SL(2,Z) structure, ρ vacuum and E(τ,2) shape are unchanged because the placement is symmetric [derived].
5. Re-fit [estimate]: C ∝ N_eff/(Im S·Im ρ₁), so keeping C = 1.0–1.3e-6 needs Im S·Im ρ₁ smaller by the factor in point 3, i.e. A₁ (or g_s) shifts; the racetrack conditions on T₁ (A₂A₃/g_s) are untouched if A₁ absorbs the change. The D861 benchmark moves to A₁ ≈ 41 × (0.38–0.85) ≈ 16–35 at fixed g_s (f = 4π² convention).
Verdict: racetrack D7s are compatible with SERAPIS-E only at the origin; they reduce the tilt's effective brane count by O(15–60%), absorbed by a smaller inflaton torus. Open: BHK's exact D7 coefficient r.

## D866: BHK's D7 term has a different structure, and the D3 term's Kähler modulus is the T⁴ 4-cycle: D857–D865's moduli mapping must be redone
Source: hep-th/0508043 (Berg–Haack–Körs, "String loop corrections to Kähler potentials in orientifolds"), eq. (3.30) and §5, fetched in two parts [literature].
1. Eq. (3.30), N = 1 T⁶/(Z₂×Z₂) (D9/D5 frame): K⁽¹⁾ has two sums with the SAME constant c and a factor ½: (a) ℰ₂(A_i^I, U^I)/((S − S̄)(T^I − T̄^I)), depending on brane Wilson lines A; (b) ℰ₂(0, U^I)/((T^J − T̄^J)(T^K − T̄^K)), J ≠ I ≠ K, at A = 0 [literature].
2. §5: six T-dualities map D9 → D3 and D5 on T²_I → D7 on the transverse T⁴; (2.77), (3.30) are copied with T-dual variables [literature]. So in our D3/D7 frame: term (a) is the D3 term, with A → D3 positions, and T^I is the modulus of the 4-cycle TRANSVERSE to T²_I; term (b) is the D7 term, POSITION-INDEPENDENT, divided by the other two 4-cycle moduli [derived from 1–2].
3. Answer to D865's question: there is no "r·(Im S/Im T₁)" origin-stack term. D7 branes give a fixed ℰ₂(0, U₁) ∝ E(U₁,2) piece divided by Im T₂·Im T₃, of the same E(U,2) shape as the tilt; the paper's footnote ("C collects both channels") already allows for it. D865's point-2–5 arithmetic is WITHDRAWN (wrong structure); D864a's symmetry conclusion stands (asymmetric D7 positions break nothing in this term, since it is position-independent, but the flavour/condensation conditions of D864 still apply).
4. Mapping error found [derived]: D857 identified D689's ρ (in Im S·Im ρ ≈ 560–975) with the inflaton torus's 2-cycle area A₁. By point 2 it is the 4-cycle modulus transverse to the inflaton torus, Im T₁ ∝ A₂A₃/g_s, which is exactly the cycle D861's benchmark used for the racetrack. Consequences:
   - Racetrack on T₁: the tilt needs Im S·Im T₁ ≈ 750–975 with Im S = 1/(2√2πg_s), the racetrack needs Im T₁ ≈ 2–15; together g_s ≈ 6e-4–6e-3 and A₂A₃ = g_s·Im T₁ ≈ 1e-3–0.1: sub-stringy. Racetrack on T₁ is EXCLUDED [derived, up to O(2π) factors].
   - Racetrack on T₂ or T₃ (cycles containing the inflaton torus) is REOPENED: e.g. A₁ = A₃ = 1, g_s = 0.1 gives Im T₂ = 10 (racetrack range) and the tilt needs A₂ ≈ 6.7e3·g_s² ≈ 67 [estimate].
   - The anti-D3 bound (v₄ = A₂A₃ ≳ 2e4 g_s) must also be re-read in this mapping.
5. D857, D860, D861, D862, D865 used the wrong identification; their specific numbers are superseded. D857a records this; the structural lessons (racetrack and anti-D3 compete for cycle sizes; E3 masses ∝ W0^N) stand.
Next (top recommendation): redo the M.3 feasibility scan with the corrected mapping (locked), racetrack on T₁, T₂ or T₃, anti-D3 on/off.

## D868: what SERAPIS-E's uplift sector can be without an anti-D3 on the inflaton torus (ranked)
Searches 2; fetched 2512.17995 (F-term uplifting with warping); the T-brane fetch (1512.04558) was interrupted, so its entry uses the abstract-level statement only.
Criterion: the uplift must (i) not add a large U₁-dependent term to V like the anti-D3 did (D867), and (ii) be able to carry the E(τ,2) plateau postulate P3 (or at least not contradict it).
1. Anti-D3 in a distant warped throat, sequestered from the inflaton torus [estimate]: its interaction with the D3 stacks on T²₁ is suppressed by the throat's warping and distance, so (i) holds; it still provides the nilpotent X. But our T⁶/(Z₂×Z₂) has no conifold (D837), so this needs the CY resolution; and the throat route cannot give P3's power-law shape (D838). Rank 1 as the uplift, with P3 kept as a postulate.
2. T-brane (D-term) uplift on a D7 stack (Cicoli–Quevedo–Valandro, 1512.04558) [literature, abstract level]: a D-term from a non-commuting Higgs vev on D7s, scaling with the Kähler moduli; it couples to the inflaton torus only if the D7s wrap a cycle containing T²₁. Placing the stack on the T⁴ cycle avoids U₁ dependence at tree level (i) but then its one-loop BHK-type term is position-independent and of E(U₁,2) shape (D866), i.e. it ADDS to C rather than spoiling it. No nilpotent X needed. Rank 2.
3. Complex-structure F-term uplift (bulk flux energy ∝ ∫|G₋|²) [literature] (2512.17995): depends on complex-structure moduli including U₁ directly, so it adds a U₁-dependent term at tree level unless the IASD flux avoids T²₁; the paper finds KKLT-type F-term uplift "effectively uncontrollable" and LVS control only at large volume. Rank 3.
4. Hidden-sector matter / Kähler uplifting (hep-th/0611332, 0707.2671) [literature, titles]: volume-dependent, U₁-independent at leading order; compatible with (i); no nilpotent sector. Rank 4 (not developed here).
Consequence [derived]: P3's wording ("the plateau sits in the anti-D3 / nilpotent sector") must be loosened to "in the uplift sector", because the anti-D3 on this torus is excluded (D867). The top candidate (distant sequestered anti-D3) keeps the nilpotent X but needs a throat outside the torus; the next best (T-brane on the T⁴ cycle) needs no X and only adds an E(U₁,2) piece to C.
Next (top recommendation): check that a sequestered distant throat leaves SERAPIS-E's frozen band unchanged, i.e. estimate the residual U₁ coupling of a throat anti-D3 (warp-factor suppression e^{4A₀}) against the D835 bound k ≲ 2e-6.
Sources: 2512.17995; 1512.04558; hep-th/0611332; 0707.2671; 1707.07059.

## D869: a warped-throat anti-D3 is sequestered enough (k ≈ 1e-9 ≪ 2e-6), if a throat exists
Derivation + arithmetic, no model run (no lock).
1. KKLMMT structure [literature]: for an anti-D3 at the tip of a warped throat with warp factor a₀⁴ = e^{4A₀}, the uplift is 2T₃a₀⁴ and the Coulomb attraction to D3s in the bulk carries a further factor a₀⁴: V = 2T₃a₀⁴[1 − (27/32π²)·a₀⁴T₃/(N·r⁴) + …] (hep-th/0308055 form, from memory; structure only).
2. So the ratio of the interaction to the uplift, which D833 computed unwarped as κ/V0 = g_s/(8πv₄), picks up one extra a₀⁴: k_warped ≈ (g_s/8πv₄)·a₀⁴ [derived from 1].
3. Size of a₀⁴ [estimate]: the throat anti-D3 must supply the plateau height V0 ~ (1e16 GeV)⁴ against an unwarped 2T₃ in Einstein frame of order M_s⁴/g_s ~ (1e16–1e17 GeV)⁴/g_s, so a₀⁴ ~ 1e-6–1e-2; standard flux throats give a₀⁴ = e^{−8πK/3g_sM} with similar or smaller values.
4. With the SERAPIS-E tilt moduli (D867: g_s/(8πv₄) ≈ 1e-5–1e-4), k_warped ≈ 1e-11–1e-6; for the generic a₀⁴ ≲ 1e-4, k ≲ 1e-8 [derived] (arithmetic).
Verdict: a throat anti-D3 is sequestered: its U₁ coupling is ≤ 1e-8 for a₀⁴ ≤ 1e-4, far below the band-safe 2e-6 (D835); only an almost unwarped throat (a₀⁴ ≳ 0.02 with the smallest v₄) would reach the bound. Caveats: (a) needs a conifold throat, absent in T⁶/(Z₂×Z₂) itself (D837), so the CY resolution; (b) the plateau's shape is still postulated (D838); (c) KKLMMT formula quoted from memory [estimate].

## D873: the D7-type piece of the tilt is ≤ 11%·q of the D3 piece, and ≲ 1% once the inflaton torus exceeds ~3 string units
Derivation + arithmetic (no model run, no lock).
1. BHK eq. (3.30) (D866): D3 term ½c·ℰ₂(A,U₁)/((S − S̄)(T₁ − T̄₁)), D7 term ½c·ℰ₂(0,U₁)/((T₂ − T̄₂)(T₃ − T̄₃)), same c [literature]. Both are E(U₁,2)-shaped for our symmetric placements (D696, D866). Write the ratio of their lattice-sum coefficients as q = O(1) (depends on D7 numbers; not computed) [estimate].
2. Ratio of moduli factors [derived]: (Im S·Im T₁)/(Im T₂·Im T₃) = [A₂A₃/(2√2π g_s²)]/[A₁²A₂A₃/g_s²] = 1/(2√2π A₁²) = 1/(8.89 A₁²). It depends only on the inflaton torus's area A₁.
3. So D7/D3 ≈ q/(8.89 A₁²): ≤ 0.11q at A₁ = 1, 0.028q at A₁ = 2, 0.013q at A₁ = 3, 0.0011q at A₁ = 10 [derived]. In D867's racetrack examples (A₁ = 1.2–1.8) it is 0.035q–0.078q.
Verdict: the D7-type piece changes the fitted Im S·Im T₁ by less than 10% unless both A₁ ≈ 1 and q ≳ 1; for the generic SERAPIS-E point (no racetrack constraint, A₁ free) it is negligible. The paper's footnote ("C collects both channels") is adequate.

## D875 (DEEP, B.1): inventory of ρ baryogenesis routes
From the notes only.
Binding Z₃ facts at ρ [derived, D778–D780, D787]:
- The inflaton (δτ at ρ) carries a non-trivial Z₃ charge q_φ ≠ 0.
- Heavy states: N_Y (charge 0), Dirac pair N_n (q) / N₃ (−q), neutral singlets S₁, S₂.
- Realistic light masses force q_L = −q_H, so the renormalisable L·N·H needs q_N = 0: the charged pair cannot decay to L + H.
- Every inflaton decay channel contains a charged N (q_a + q_b ≡ −q_φ ≠ 0).
- If the Higgs carries Z₃ charge, the residual Z₃ acts on SM operators as baryon triality; the pair can then decay through N·u^c d^c d^c, and the proton is protected (D787).
- Z₃ is exact (modular symmetry is gauged).
| Route | Note | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| Thermal / non-thermal leptogenesis after the first reheating (T_R 3e8–3e9 GeV) | D725, D731 | Superseded: the charged pair is long-lived; a second, late reheating dilutes or resets it (D780) |
| Late decay of the pair via string-scale dim-6 operators, T₂ ≳ 1e5–1e6 GeV | D781, D783 | Frozen band survives only if T₂ ≳ 1e5–1e6 (Λ ≲ M_s); gives reheating, not baryons |
| Late N → udd decays (dim-6) as the CP source | D788 | Wall: ε ≤ 2e-8 (Nanopoulos–Weinberg), needs ≥ 2e-5 |
| P5: light Z₃-charged diquark mediator | D788, D789 | Consistent, but all couplings conserve B; N decays cannot make baryons. P5 retired (D792) |
| Inflaton-decay ε | D790 | Hopeless, ≤ 3e-13 |
| Inflaton Affleck–Dine orbit charge η | D790, D791 | Large charge (η ~ 0.1–0.2) but isocurvature forces |Δx| ≥ 0.15, overproducing by ~3e4 |
| Inflaton AD + self-dilution by the late N decays | D792, D793 | Works (Y_B = 8.75e-11 at T₂ ≈ 140–1100 GeV, Λ ≈ 5e16–2e17) but lands at n_s 0.9667–0.9703, r 5.13–5.59e-4: just OUTSIDE the frozen band (post hoc) |
Diagnosis [derived]: the frozen band needs T₂ ≳ 1e5 GeV (fast late decay), while the only working asymmetry (inflaton AD) needs strong dilution, i.e. a slow decay and T₂ ~ 1e2–1e3 GeV. The two pull T₂ in opposite directions. A route inside the band needs an asymmetry that is (a) produced at or after T₂ ≳ 1e5 GeV, or (b) produced earlier but with a size that the modest dilution at T₂ ≳ 1e5 GeV brings to 8.75e-11.
Next (B.2, literature): mechanisms of type (a): late-decay baryogenesis with a large ε (resonant, or with light mediators), spontaneous baryogenesis from the racetrack axion (P1′'s axion rolling during reheating), and Z₃-allowed AD flat directions with smaller charge; type (b): an inflaton AD charge reduced to η ~ 1e-4 (needs a smaller |Δx|, which isocurvature forbids, D791) or a different condensate.

## D876 (DEEP, B.2): literature for ρ baryogenesis; top candidate is a suppressed TRANSFER of the inflaton's AD charge, not extra dilution
Searches 2; fetched 1803.00820 (non-thermal WIMP baryogenesis) and the PRL page of axiogenesis (Co–Harigaya, PRL 124, 111602; abstract level only).
Findings [literature]:
1. Non-thermal re-annihilation baryogenesis (1803.00820): a long-lived φ decays late, produces a B-violating species χ, and χχ annihilations with CP asymmetry ε (benchmark 1e-3) make baryons; it needs T_reh below χ freeze-out, benchmark T_reh = 20 GeV.
2. Axiogenesis (Co–Harigaya): a rotating PQ-charged scalar carries a charge asymmetry that QCD and electroweak sphalerons convert to baryons; the conversion is partial (set by the field's couplings), not one-to-one.
3. Low-scale baryogenesis from three-body decays (2312.08327) and WIMP-baryogenesis variants put the CP source in light-mediator loops, evading the Nanopoulos–Weinberg suppression that killed D788.
Ranking against D875's targets (asymmetry at/after T₂ ≳ 1e5 GeV, or a smaller early asymmetry):
- Rank 1 [estimate]: inflaton-AD charge η ~ 0.1–0.2 (D790) with a SUPPRESSED transfer to baryon number, in the spirit of axiogenesis. In D792 every φ → NN decay carried ΔB = ±2, so B per N = η (full transfer), and the overproduction (~3e4 at the isocurvature-allowed |Δx| ≥ 0.15, D791) had to be removed by dilution, which forced slow decay (T₂ ~ 1e2–1e3 GeV). If instead only a fraction f of the charge becomes B (competing ΔB = 0 channels, e.g. φ → N_Y N₃ vs φ → N_n N_n under baryon triality, D787), the needed f ≈ 1/(3e4 × residual dilution) lets T₂ stay ≳ 1e5 GeV. Uses only existing ingredients.
- Rank 2 [estimate]: late-decay baryogenesis with a light-mediator CP source (types 1 and 3) at T₂ ≳ 1e5 GeV; needs new light states and ε ≳ 2e-5.
- Rank 3 [estimate]: a Z₃-allowed AD flat direction with smaller charge (needs the baryon-triality charges of udd-type directions; not checked).
Next (B.3): lock and compute the transfer fraction f from the Z₃-allowed inflaton decay channels (branching ratios of ΔB = ±2, ±1, 0 channels with the D787 charges), the resulting Y_B with T₂ ≳ 1e5 GeV, and whether N* stays in the frozen band.
Sources: 1803.00820; PRL 124, 111602 (axiogenesis); 2312.08327; hep-ph/0509121.

## D877 (DEEP, B.3): the suppressed-transfer route needs the two inflaton channels balanced to 0.005–0.4%; a tuning unless a symmetry fixes b = 1/3
Derivation + arithmetic on the locked D792 formula (output kept at theory/derivations/b3_transfer_d877.txt; no model run, no results file).
1. Z₃-allowed inflaton channels [derived] (D780, D787, D789): with N_n (q), N₃ (−q), N_Y (0) and −q_φ ≡ 2q ≡ −q (mod 3), exactly two two-body channels are allowed: φ → N_nN_n and φ → N_Y N₃. Under baryon triality N_n → u^c d^c d^c carries B = +1, N₃ the conjugate (B = −1), N_Y decays to L H (B = 0). So the channels carry ΔB = +2 and ΔB = −1.
2. Transfer fraction [derived]: an inflaton charge asymmetry η (AD orbit, D790) gives net baryon number per φ quantum = η[2b − (1 − b)] = η(3b − 1), with b = BR(φ → N_nN_n). So f = |3b − 1|; D792's "B per N = η" corresponds to one channel only.
3. Required f [derived, arithmetic]: Y_B = (28/79)(3/4)(T₂/M)·f·η = 8.75e-11 with the band-safe T₂ = 1e5–1e6 GeV (D781), M = 4.3e11–1e12 GeV, η = 0.3–1 (D791 isocurvature floor): f = 1.4e-4 to 1.1e-2, i.e. |b − 1/3| = 5e-5 to 4e-3.
4. Verdict: Y_B can be reached inside the frozen band only if the two channel widths sit within 0.005–0.4% of the ratio 1 : 2. With no symmetry forcing b = 1/3, that is a tuning of 1 part in 250–20000. Rank 1 of D876 is WEAKENED: viable in principle, natural only if some structure enforces Γ(N_Y N₃) = 2Γ(N_nN_n) at leading order (an open question: the 2⊕1 couplings of D725 would decide it).
5. Next step (would need a lock): compute b from the D725 2⊕1 couplings at ρ. If b = 1/3 exactly at leading order, f comes from a small correction and the route becomes natural.

## D879 (DEEP, B.4): ρ-baryogenesis verdict so far; a route the inventory MISSED: LH_u Affleck–Dine is Z₃-allowed at ρ and fits inside the band for m_ν₁ ≈ 1e-10–1e-9 eV
Status of the candidates [derived]:
- Suppressed transfer of the inflaton-AD charge (D876 rank 1): needs b = 1/3 to 0.005–0.4%; the 2⊕1 couplings give 0.10–0.95 (D877, D878). Tuned; not natural.
- Light-mediator late-decay baryogenesis (rank 2): untested; needs new light states.
- Z₃-allowed MSSM flat directions (rank 3), from D787's charge table [derived]: with q_Hu ≠ 0, UDD and QQQL carry charge ±1 and are forbidden; QDL, LLE and LH_u are Z₃-neutral and allowed (D787, line "QDL, LLE and LH_u are Z₃-neutral"). D780 also lists LH_u among the Z₃-neutral bilinears. So the classic LH_u Affleck–Dine direction exists at ρ, lifted by the Z₃-neutral Weinberg operator (LH_u)²/M.
New observation [derived + literature-level estimate]: D875's inventory covered only inflaton-AD and inflaton-decay routes at ρ; the LH_u AD route (which the paper already uses at τ = i) was never checked at ρ. Standard LH_u AD leptogenesis gives n_L/s ≈ 1e-10·(1e-9 eV/m_ν₁)·(T_R/1e6 GeV) [literature: Murayama–Yanagida / Fujii–Hamaguchi–Yanagida form, from memory; estimate]. At ρ the relevant reheating is the late one, T₂, because the condensate starts oscillating at H ~ m_soft while the Z₃-charged pair still dominates. With the band-safe T₂ = 1e5–1e6 GeV (D781) the observed asymmetry needs m_ν₁ ≈ 1e-10–1e-9 eV, i.e. an essentially massless lightest neutrino, exactly the condition the paper already states for AD at τ = i, and consistent with the frozen Σm_ν NO floor (0.0587 eV).
Verdict (so far): ρ has a CANDIDATE baryogenesis mechanism inside the frozen band (LH_u AD with T₂ = 1e5–1e6 GeV and m_ν₁ ≲ 1e-9 eV), pending a locked computation. This would change the paper's statement "the frozen band at ρ leaves no baryogenesis mechanism". Caveats [estimate]: (a) the formula is quoted from memory; (b) the ρ light-neutrino sector from the weight-two doublet alone is exactly degenerate (paper caveat), so the lightest-mass condition must be checked in a realistic ρ lepton sector; (c) thermal effects and the soft-mass scale of the covariant completion (m_soft ~ TeV–100 TeV) enter the onset of oscillation.
Next (top recommendation): B.5, lock and compute LH_u AD at ρ with the literature formula (fetch it), T₂ = 1e5–1e6 GeV, soft masses from the covariant completion, and check whether m_ν₁ ≲ 1e-9 eV is compatible with the ρ lepton sector.

## D882 (B.7): a ρ lepton sector with m_ν₁ ≈ 1e-8 eV: D779's minimal extension already allows it; the real constraint is Planck-suppressed Weinberg terms
Derivation only (no fit; no lock).
1. Starting point [derived] (D778, D779): at ρ the light leptons must be Γ₂ singlets (charge q_L = −q_H) coupling only to Z₃-neutral heavy states; with N_Y alone rank(m_ν) = 1, so two extra Z₃-neutral heavy singlets S₁, S₂ are needed for rank 3.
2. Making m_ν₁ tiny [derived]: with S₁, S₂ of masses M₁, M₂ and Dirac couplings y₁, y₂, the third light mass is controlled by the most weakly coupled / heaviest singlet: m_ν₁ ≈ y₂²v_u²/M₂ (up to mixing). m_ν₁ = 1e-8 eV needs y₂²/M₂ ≈ 3e-22 GeV⁻¹, e.g. y₂ ≈ 2e-4 at M₂ = 1e14 GeV, or y₂ ≈ 6e-6 at M₂ = 1e11 GeV. Alternatively S₂ is absent (rank 2, m_ν₁ = 0) and a small lift comes from elsewhere (point 4).
3. Modular protection [derived]: at ρ, E₄(ρ) = 0 while E₆(ρ) ≠ 0. If S₂'s Dirac coupling is a weight-4 singlet form (∝ E₄), it vanishes exactly at the vacuum, giving m_ν₁ = 0 at tree level naturally; this is the natural reason for a near-massless state at ρ.
4. Constraint [estimate]: an unsuppressed Planck-scale Weinberg operator (LH_u)²/M_P gives m ~ v_u²/M_P ≈ 1.2e-5 eV per entry, about 1e3 above the needed 1e-8 eV. So the lightest direction's Weinberg coefficient must be ≲ 1e-3 (literature: AD with an ultralight neutrino needs this suppression, hep-ph/0008041 [title-level]). If that coefficient is itself a modular form of weight 4 (∝ E₄(ρ) = 0) or carries a Z₃-forbidden structure, it is protected; a residual nonzero piece (e.g. from τ's displacement or loops) must be ≈ 1e-3 of natural size to land on 1e-8 eV.
Verdict: a ρ lepton sector compatible with LH_u AD exists at the level of structure: D779's two extra neutral singlets, with the lightest direction protected by E₄(ρ) = 0 and lifted to ~1e-8 eV by a suppressed correction. It is not fitted (no oscillation fit was run), and the size of the lift is an estimate.
Open: a locked oscillation fit with this structure (weights, E₄-protected entry, small lift) giving NO splittings and m_ν₁ ≈ 1e-8 eV.

## D885 (DEEP, E.1): reverse path for τ = i's ε; the needed term is a tiny POWER of |j − 1728| in the uplift, which a warped-throat cutoff can carry
Derivation from the notes.
Required [derived] (D795, D815, D826, D689a): a term εI₁ in V/V0 with ε ≈ 1.40–1.45e-4 under the corrected reheating, where I₁ = (1/4π)ln(…|j − 1728|…) up to the normalisation of D689a (so ε enters a logarithm as b = 4πε ≈ 1.8e-3); it gives the vacuum mass m²/H² ≈ 2.0e-3 at i and the tilt. In K/W language it is an uplift factor V_up → V_up·(1 + ε I₁), i.e. weight-0, modular-invariant, logarithmic in |j − 1728|, vanishing quadratically at i (j − 1728 has a double zero there, D685/D689a).
Routes tried (factor missed by):
| Route | Note | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| N = 2 thresholds | D576, D608 | right growth, but a saddle at i |
| Coleman–Weinberg loops of our own states | D606, D607 | cannot produce ln|j − 1728|; heavy-state loops far too small |
| Threshold-dependent uplift e^{ξ′L} | D616–D618 | exponential at the cusp; linearisation fails |
| Harvey–Moore ln|J(T) − J(U)| at T = U = i | paper | species term too weak to keep the vacuum |
| Covariant F-term | D684, D685, D826 | 1e11–1e12 too small |
| BHK remnant / multiplicative factor | D802, D811, D823 | stabilising but no mass for a zero of V; BHK tilt variant post hoc |
| Holomorphic h(τ) with a double zero | D685 | e^{2πy} growth destroys the plateau |
| Species-scale one-loop | D685 | ∝ (m₃/₂/H)², as small as the F-term |
| Anti-D3 one-loop term | D834, D834a | saddle at i; not the mass source |
New reverse-path observation [derived + estimate]:
1. A factor |j(U) − 1728|^{2q} in the uplift equals exp(2q ln|j − 1728|) ≈ 1 + 2q ln|j − 1728| while 2q·ln|j − 1728| ≪ 1, which is exactly the εI₁ form with q ≈ ε/(2·normalisation) ~ 1e-5 [derived from the expansion]. It is modular-invariant (weight 0), has the needed double zero at i, and at horizon exit (y* ≈ 23, ln|j| ≈ 2πy* ≈ 145) 2q ln|j| ≈ 3e-3: still in the linear regime, so the plateau survives [estimate].
2. Such a factor arises naturally if the warped-throat cutoff depends on U as Λ₀(U) ∝ (j(U) − 1728)^{q′}: V_up ∝ |Λ₀|⁴ (D837), so 2q = 4q′. A small exponent q′ ~ 1e-5 is what a one-loop (threshold) dependence of the throat's UV data on U would give, since a one-loop log in the exponent of the warp factor exponentiates to a small power [estimate; this is D686's "logarithmic correction to the warp factor", now with a mechanism].
3. This is compatible with D838 (no exponential approach needed here: the τ = i plateau's own shape is set elsewhere; the factor only supplies the small tilt and mass).
Verdict: the reverse path points to one concrete target: a one-loop U-dependence of the warped throat's UV cutoff, giving V_up ∝ |j − 1728|^{~1e-5}. It needs the throat (CY resolution) and is not computed. All in-torus routes stay closed.
Next (E.2): literature on one-loop/threshold dependence of warped-throat data (the conifold period's normalisation, or the warp factor) on bulk complex-structure moduli.

## D886 (DEEP, E.2): the literature does NOT support a logarithmic U-dependence of the throat cutoff; corrections are exponentially small

The prefactor is a pure number; the bulk moduli enter only through the flux-determined valley location p^i (fixed by integers, not a free modulus value) and through corrections suppressed by e^{2πi p·τ}. The IR warp factor is e^{2A}|tip ~ |z_cf|^{2/3}.
Assessment [derived]:

3. A one-loop (logarithmic) U-dependence of the throat cutoff is not found in this literature; D885's target remains a hypothesis with no identified source.
Verdict: E.2 NEGATIVE. The τ = i ε stays fitted (C1 of D841 unchanged). The D885 target (|j − 1728|^{~1e-5} in the uplift) is recorded as the precise form a future string computation would have to produce.

## D888 (DEEP, L.1): reverse path for ρ's lift ε ≈ 1.8e-3: holomorphic and perturbative routes are closed by symmetry; an instanton with Im T/N ≈ 1 or a GUT/string-scale-suppressed operator fit naturally
Arithmetic: theory/modular/rho_lift_d888.py → theory/derivations/rho_lift_d888.txt (no prediction, no lock; first run crashed on a print format, fixed and rerun, numbers unaffected).
1. Need [derived] (D883): S₂'s Dirac coupling = ε·y₂ with ε = 1.8e-3 (3.1e-4 to 1.1e-2, 5–95%), y₂ = O(1).
2. Why it vanishes [derived]: the only weight-4 level-1 form is E₄, and E₄(ρ) = 0 (check: |E₄(ρ)| < 1e-30; E₄′(ρ) = −(2πi/3)E₆(ρ) = −6.035i, E₆(ρ) = 2.8815). Any holomorphic coupling of the same weight is ∝ E₄ and vanishes too, so no holomorphic lift exists at fixed weight.
3. Route (a), displacement of τ from ρ [derived]: ε ≈ |E₄(τ)|/|E₆|^{2/3} needs |τ − ρ| ≈ 6.0e-4 (1.0e-4 to 3.7e-3). But ρ is a fixed point of ST, so any modular-invariant potential has a stationary point exactly there: the displacement is zero unless modular symmetry is broken explicitly. CLOSED within the model.
4. Route (b), loops [literature-standard: SUSY non-renormalisation]: a superpotential coupling that vanishes stays zero to all orders in perturbation theory; post-SUSY-breaking thresholds give ~ (1/16π²)(m_soft/M_S₂) ~ 1e-9 or less. CLOSED. (For scale only: ε = 0.28 × 1/16π².)
5. Route (c), instanton [derived arithmetic]: ε = e^{−2π Im T/N} needs Im T/N = 1.01 (0.72–1.29). This is the natural size in racetrack setups (N ~ Im T). Condition: the instanton prefactor must be a function of U that does not vanish at ρ (e.g. built from η(U), η(ρ) ≠ 0) with the right Z₃ character. ALIVE [estimate].
6. Route (d), higher-dimension operator [derived arithmetic]: ε = Λ/M_P needs Λ ≈ 4.4e15 GeV (7.6e14 to 2.7e16), i.e. the GUT/string scale. It must enter through a non-holomorphic (Kähler) structure that is not forced to vanish at ρ. ALIVE [estimate].
Verdict: the ρ lift is not explained, but it is not fine-tuned either: two standard mechanisms give it at natural parameter values (Im T/N ≈ 1 or Λ ≈ M_GUT). Both need explicit model-building (L.2/L.3).

## D888a (correction to D888 points 5–6): the instanton and Kähler routes are also closed while the residual Z₃ at ρ is exact
D888 called routes (c) and (d) alive, provided their prefactor does not vanish at ρ. That was wrong. At τ = ρ the residual Z₃ = ⟨ST⟩ is an exact symmetry of the whole U-modular-invariant theory: holomorphic, non-holomorphic (Kähler) and instanton terms alike. S₂'s coupling vanishes because it carries nonzero residual charge (that is the content of E₄(ρ) = 0). Any term that contributes to the same coupling carries the same charge, so it also vanishes at ρ, whatever its prefactor (an η-type prefactor with a "compensating character" just restates the charge). All four D888 routes therefore need the residual Z₃ to be broken. D888's numbers (Im T/N ≈ 1, Λ ≈ 4e15 GeV) are only the sizes the breaking would need if it entered through those channels.

Verdict: W2.2 CONDITIONAL POSITIVE. The literature supplies a standard mechanism that makes the Weinberg coefficient small (instanton-only, lepton number perturbatively conserved); with instanton actions like those of the heavy-ν masses, the bound holds for M_N ≲ 1e12 GeV. ## D909 (DEEP, N1.1): τ = i can protect a light seesaw direction like ρ does, but only with a heavy Dirac pair; N1 closed structurally
Derivation from the notes (no computation, no lock).
1. Rules [derived] (D654a, D663, D664): with the η^{-2} multiplier a coupling of trivial S-character is non-zero at i iff its total weight Σk ≡ 0 mod 4 (a 1′ factor, ρ(S) = −1, flips this to ≡ 2 mod 4). Matter parity from the centre needs odd k for leptons and heavy singlets, even k for H_u (D664 uses k_L = k_N = 1, k_Hu = 0).
2. Protected Dirac coupling [derived]: a heavy Γ₂-singlet S with odd k_S and trivial character couples to the singlet lepton L₁ through L₁SH_u with Σk = k_L + k_S ≡ 2 mod 4 when k_S ≡ 1 mod 4 (e.g. k_S = 1: no weight-2 singlet form exists at level Γ(2); k_S = 5: weight-6 singlets vanish at i by the rule). So the coupling vanishes at i, the analogue of ρ's E₄(ρ) = 0.
3. Obstruction [derived] (D663): the same parity rule makes S's own Majorana mass vanish (2k_S ≡ 2 mod 4 for any odd k_S, any singlet character). A protected S is therefore massless unless paired: a partner S′ with k_S + k_S′ ≡ 0 mod 4 (e.g. k_S′ = 3) gives a Dirac mass M S S′, and with S's coupling zero the pair's seesaw contribution y_S y_S′ᵀ/M vanishes, so the light direction is protected.
4. Cost [derived]: one heavy Dirac pair beyond the 2⊕1 sector (two extra fields, the same count as ρ's two extra singlets, D779), plus a post hoc lift from residual-Z₂ breaking (τ off i), as at ρ (D888a).
Verdict: N1 CLOSED at the structural level. AD at τ = i could gain its missing light direction by this construction, which would leave it with the same conditions as ρ (extra fields, a fitted lift, an instanton-only Weinberg term marginal at the racetrack g_s, D904a). An oscillation fit would repeat D883/D896's generic rank-2-plus-lift statistics, so none is run. τ = i's main baryogenesis route stays inflaton-decay leptogenesis (D745). No change to the draft or frozen predictions.

## D911 (DEEP, P3.L1): a lead for P3: an Eisenstein series in the Kähler potential gives the plateau's 1/E approach, but pure K = −log E(τ,2) is a ghost at the fixed points
Fetched 2510.19927v3 (Mohseni–Vafa, "Symmetry Points of N = 1 Modular Geometry"). Arithmetic: theory/modular/mv_kahler_d911.py → theory/derivations/mv_kahler_d911.txt (no prediction, no lock).
Findings [literature] (2510.19927): non-holomorphic Eisenstein series enter the Kähler potential, K = log E_s(τ, τ̄, k); a IIB example uses E_{3/2}; metric positivity holds only in a window of a mixing parameter (e.g. −0.111 < α < 0.221 at τ = i); symmetry points are always critical points (unstable dS, SUSY AdS or Minkowski, by k mod 12). No inflation, no uplift or nilpotent sector, no plateau.
Assessment:
1. [derived] With K ⊃ −c log E(τ,2) and a constant-type W, e^K ∝ E^{−c}, so the AdS term −3e^K|W|² falls off as E^{−c}; with an uplift V₀ the potential approaches V₀ from below as 1/E for c = 1, the SERAPIS-E plateau form, now from the Kähler potential instead of the nilpotent metric (P3's current home, D870).
2. [derived] (computed) For pure K = −log E(τ,2), 4y²K_{ττ̄} = −2.000 at both ρ and i (= −s(s−1) at a critical point of E), +0.14 at y = 2, +1.69 at y = 4, +1.96 at y = 8 (→ +s): the metric is NEGATIVE at the fixed points, a ghost exactly at our vacuum. K = +log E has the opposite signs (ghost at the cusp).
3. [derived] (estimate) A mixture K = −k log(2y) − c log E(τ,2) has 4y²K_{ττ̄} = k − 2c at a fixed point and → k + 2c at the cusp: ghost-free at ρ for k > 2c. Its e^K ∝ y^{−k}E^{−c} ~ y^{−(k+2c)} keeps a power-law approach; the plateau form needs k + 2c = 2 (e.g. k = 1.5, c = 0.25). The interior shape differs from 1/E but D698 found the interior form shifts n_s by < 0.001.
4. [literature] String origin: Eisenstein series in K are known for the axio-dilaton (E_{3/2}, the α′³ correction) and, for the torus complex structure U, only additively at one loop (BHK, ∝ E(U,2)/(Im S Im T)); a −c log E(U,2) term with c = O(1) is not a known string term.
Verdict: LEAD, not an origin. It would move P3 from "plateau in the nilpotent metric by choice" to "plateau from an Eisenstein term in K by choice": cleaner (no nilpotent field) but equally postulated. Testable by a short locked computation: scan (k, c) with positivity on the whole fundamental domain, vacuum at ρ with V(ρ) = 0 and m² > 0, plateau approach, exact n_s and r against the frozen band.
MAP: node=plateau_origin status=assumed touches=[serapis_e] ripple=no

## D911a (correction to D911 point 3): the mixture estimate ignored |W|²
D911 point 3 took e^K|W|² ∝ y^{−k}E^{−c}, a power law. A modular-invariant potential needs W of weight −k, W ∝ η^{−2k}, and then e^G = (2y|η|⁴)^{−k}E^{−c}: since |η|⁴ ≈ e^{−πy/3}, e^G grows as e^{kπy/3} at the cusp. The power-law plateau estimate (k + 2c = 2) is withdrawn. The positivity statement (4y²G_{ττ̄} = k − 2c at a fixed point) stands.

## D914 (P3 / completion): the T-brane uplift's only handle on the torus shape is the G-flux norm, a single lattice term, not an Eisenstein ratio
Search 1; fetched 1512.04558 (Cicoli–Quevedo–Valandro, De Sitter from T-branes), completing the D868 entry that used the abstract only.
Findings [literature] (1512.04558): V_up = C_up/(V^{8/3} M_P⁴) (eq. 3.24), C_up ∼ 2g_s n ∫_{D_h}|Ĝ|² ω∧ω; equivalently c_up/V^{8/3} with c_up from e^K|W|², s = 1/g_s and flux quanta (eqs. 2.15–2.16, 2.32). The D-term uses the gauge kinetic function Re f_h = Re T_h/2π; the charged-matter Kähler metric is taken to depend on Re S only. Complex-structure dependence enters only implicitly, through the metric in |Ĝ|², and is not analysed.
Assessment [estimate]: on a torus factor, the norm of a quantised three-form flux with integers (m, n) along that T² scales as |m + nU|²/Im U (the standard flux-norm form, from memory, to verify before use). At fixed fluxes this is a single lattice term: it goes as 1/y (n = 0) or grows as y (n ≠ 0) toward the cusp. It is neither modular invariant on its own (the fluxes transform) nor a 1/E(U,2) approach, where E(U,2) is a SUM over the lattice of the inverse squares. So a T-brane uplift does not supply the E-ratio either.
Verdict: P3 unchanged. The T-brane stays an allowed carrier for the uplift sector (D868), but no source of the plateau's form; the anti-D3-in-throat option is likewise shape-blind at leading order (D886). Both uplift carriers are now checked; the plateau's form remains a postulate of the uplift sector.

## D933 (completion tick 9): partial no-go: on a factorised T⁶ (or its orbifolds), no nonzero ISD flux leaves a single U_i flat for ALL values of the other moduli; the remaining route is a point-wise flat U, now reduced to a finite flux search

[derived] (enumeration, script inline) then every wedge F∧H contains dy³∧dy³: 0 nonzero wedges among the 10 basis 3-forms without a dx³ leg, so N_flux = ∫F∧H = 0. For ISD G (the GKP vacuum condition) N_flux = ∫|G|²/Im S > 0 unless G = 0. Contradiction: an identically U₃-independent W carries no flux.

## D945 (Project H, H1–H2 analytic): a field living in SIX dimensions (4D × T²) gets a finite one-loop mass² ∝ +E(U,2)/A² from the winding images of the loop; the lattice weight s = (D−2)/2 ties SERAPIS's k = 2 (p = 2√2) to D = 6
[literature] Search (1, standard): one-loop potentials on T² and Scherk–Schwarz orbifolds (e.g. hep-th/0601158, 2407.16781, 2512.20570) are image/lattice sums; nothing found computing a scalar's mass² as E(U,2) for an inflaton plateau.
[derived] (standard method of images) For χ coupled to a field Φ of a D-dimensional theory on R⁴ × T²_{(D−4)=2}... i.e. Φ propagating in D = 4 + 2 dimensions, the one-loop tadpole δm_χ² = λ Σ_w G_D(|w|) over lattice vectors w ≠ 0 after removing the U-independent local divergence (w = 0). G_D(L) = Γ(D/2−1)/(4π^{D/2} L^{D−2}). With |w|² = A|m + nU|²/Im U: Σ′_w |w|^{−(D−2)} = A^{−(D−2)/2} Σ′ (Im U)^s/|m + nU|^{2s} = 2ζ(2s) E(U,s) A^{−s}, s = (D−2)/2.
[derived] (arithmetic) D = 6 gives s = 2 exactly: δm_χ² = λ ζ(4) E(U,2) / (2π³ A²) × (combinatorial factor of the coupling), G₆ coefficient 1/(4π³) = 0.00806. Sign: positive for a bosonic loop with λ > 0, negative for a fermion loop.
[derived] (D929 link) k = 2s and n = 1, so p = 2s√2: SERAPIS's p = 2√2 ⇔ s = 2 ⇔ the loop field lives in 6D (e.g. on a brane worldvolume wrapping the T², or a 6D bulk field). D = 5 (s = 3/2, p = 3√2/2·… non-integer k = 3) and D ≥ 7 give other exponents.
[estimate] The offset: δm² > 0 with minimum at ρ (E(U,2) is minimised there, Rankin/Montgomery), so A = μ²Ê needs a tree-level mass² = −c E(ρ,2) cancelling exactly at ρ: a tuning of one number; at τ = i the analogous cancellation is at a saddle, not a minimum. A² = (Im T-dependent area)² must be fixed (Kähler stabilisation), as already assumed.
Status: H2 passes analytically (right lattice weight, positive for bosons); H3 (offset) is a one-number tuning; H4 (the B term, ratio A/B = Ê exactly) open. Not a claim of novelty.
LESSONS: the lattice weight of an image sum is fixed by the dimension the loop field lives in; that maps p to a dimension.
MAP: none

## D945a (correction to D945's wording)
D945's D = 5 example is garbled and wrong: a field on R⁴ × T² is six-dimensional by definition, so D = 5 does not arise. The correct statement: the image sum has weight s = (D−2)/2 where D counts the dimensions the loop field sees at distances of order the T² size. s = 2 (SERAPIS) holds when any further compact dimensions are much SMALLER than the T² (their KK modes are heavy, so G reduces to 6D). If the field lives in D > 6 dimensions with the extra ones LARGER than the T², s = (D−2)/2 > 2 (D = 8: s = 3, k = 6, p = 6√2; D = 10: s = 4) and the exponent changes. Also D945's first [derived] line contains a stray fragment ("R⁴ × T²_{(D−4)=2}... i.e."); read it as "Φ propagating on R⁴ × T² (D = 6)". The numbers (G₆ coefficient, sign, E(U,2) weight) are unchanged.
MAP: none

[derived] (sympy) For A = aÊ, B = b: V_min = abÊ/(aÊ + b), and V_min(1 + CÊ) ≡ b·P3(λÊ; C/λ) with λ = a/b (difference simplifies to 0). Since λÊ = λ(E(τ,2) − E(ρ,2)) is still modular invariant, the general two-field model is P3 with a rescaled invariant.
[derived] At large Ê ≈ y², λÊ ≈ (√λ y)²: a field shift Δφ = ln λ/(2√2) plus O(y⁻³) corrections, so (n_s, r) on the plateau are unchanged at leading order once C is refitted (C is a fitted BHK number already). Near the vacuum V_min ≈ aÊ, so the vacuum mass² scales with a (= λb): it moves m_φ, the reheating history and hence N* slightly.
Verdict: H4 passes: no exact ratio is required; the "+1" of P3 is a convention absorbed into λ and C. P3 is now "derived up to one tuned offset and the existence of a 6D loop field coupled to a heavy χ" [estimate for the model-building assumptions]. LESSONS: before calling a constant a tuning, check whether it is degenerate with an already-fitted parameter.

## D947 (Project H, H3): the "tuned offset" is not an extra tuning: keeping the full positive one-loop mass (∝ E, not Ê) and subtracting the vacuum energy at ρ (the cosmological-constant tuning every model needs) gives exactly P3 again, with a rescaled λ
[derived] (sympy) With A = aE(τ,2) (no offset), V_min(E) = bλE/(λE+1). Then V_min(E) − V_min(E_ρ) = b/(λE_ρ+1) · λ′Ê/(λ′Ê+1) exactly, λ′ = λ/(λE_ρ+1). So the shape is P3 with Ê → λ′Ê, which D946 showed is degenerate with the plateau amplitude and C.
[derived] With the ramp multiplying V_min, subtracting V(ρ) leaves one extra term N·λE_ρ·CÊ (N = b/(λE_ρ+1)): on the plateau it adds to the ramp (C_eff = C(1+λE_ρ), absorbed into the fitted C); the residual shape difference is λE_ρCÊ/(λ′Ê+1) ≲ O(C/λ′) ~ 1e-6 relative, negligible.
Verdict: H3 passes: the offset of D945 is the cosmological-constant subtraction at the vacuum, not a new tuning. Project H closes POSITIVE at the analytic level: P3's bounded Eisenstein plateau follows from (i) a heavy field χ with a tree-level pinning term, (ii) a one-loop image mass ∝ E(U,2)/A² from a 6D boson loop coupled to χ (D945/D945a), and (iii) the usual CC tuning; the ratio is free (D946) and the two-field system matches the single-field background (D944). Remaining assumptions [estimate]: existence of the 6D loop field and its quartic coupling to χ in a string construction; A (the T² area) and S fixed; sign λ > 0 (boson loop). P3 status: postulate → derived up to model-building assumptions (i)–(ii). Frozen predictions unchanged; λ, λ′ enter only near the vacuum (N*), untested.

Found while preparing the paper paragraph: D709 ("any 1/E(τ,2) plateau from integrating out a modulus needs E at leading order") and D712 ("brane-interaction candidate hits the sign wall") concern the same plateau. Checked against them before writing anything up.
[derived] (sympy) D709's obstruction: for V = aE/X^p − b/X^q a pure 1/E minimum needs p = 2q, and then the E-term is 50% of the competing term at the minimum (loss of perturbative control). In D941 the integrated field is χ with V = Aχ² + B(1−χ)²; at χ* = B/(A+B) the E-term energy is Aχ*² = AB²/(A+B)², a fraction B/(A+B) = 1/(λÊ+1) of V_min: ≈ 1e-3–1e-4 on the plateau, not 50%. The plateau energy is the tree term B; the E-dependence of V is a small correction because χ's large loop mass pushes χ* → 0. D709 does not apply.
[derived] D712/D703's obstruction is the sign of a codim-2 tension needed to stabilise the AREA against an E-term. D945 needs no tension competition: its sign requirement is only δm_χ² > 0, which a boson loop with positive quartic coupling gives. D712 does not apply.
NEW conditions [estimate, from this check]: (1) Hierarchy: the loop mass² A ≫ tree mass² B (ratio λÊ ~ 1e3–1e4 on the plateau). That is consistent with perturbation theory only if the tree mass is accidentally small (higher loops are suppressed relative to one loop by λ/16π², not relative to tree); stated as an assumption. (2) Area backreaction: V_min ≈ B[1 − 1/(λÊ)] with λ ∝ 1/A² adds an A-dependence of relative size 1/(λÊ) ≪ 1 to the area's potential; the area modulus must be stabilised with m_A ≫ H (assumed, as in D945), and the shift is small.
Verdict: Project H's positive close (D947) stands, now explicitly checked against D703/D709/D712, with conditions (1)–(2) added to its assumption list.

## D950 (Project H, model-building check): the 6D loop tower must be NON-supersymmetric at the T² scale; with only soft SUSY breaking the leading image sum has weight s = 1 (the N=2 log(U₂|η|⁴) threshold), which gives the α = 1/3 sibling, not SERAPIS
Search (1, standard) + 1 fetch. [literature] Benakli & Goodsell, "Two-Point Functions of Chiral Fields at One Loop in Type II" (arXiv:0805.1874, 2008): in toroidal orientifolds, N=1 sectors give moduli-independent one-loop corrections, N=4 sectors vanish, N=2 sectors give a Kähler-metric correction ∝ log(8π³μ T₂U₂|η(U)|⁴): a wavefunction (Kähler) correction, not a mass; supersymmetry forbids a one-loop mass for a chiral field without a superpotential.
[derived] (propagator expansion) With bosons and fermions degenerate the image sums cancel. With a soft splitting m_soft², the surviving term is m_soft² ∂G_D/∂m²|₀ ∝ L^{−(D−4)}: for D = 6 the lattice weight drops from s = 2 to s = 1, i.e. Σ′|w|^{−2} → (regularised) −log(U₂|η(U)|⁴) + const, linear in y at large y. With n = 1, k = 1: p = √2, α = 1/3 [derived (arithmetic)], the D936 sibling B, not SERAPIS's p = 2√2.
Consequence: D945's s = 2 mass requires the loop field's KK tower to be non-supersymmetric at the T² scale (e.g. a brane sector with SUSY broken at the string/KK scale), sequestered from the visible sector whose m_{3/2} ~ 1e5–1e6 GeV (D713). Scherk–Schwarz breaking along the same T² is excluded: it ties m_{3/2} to M_KK of that T², which must exceed H ~ 1e13 GeV, contradicting the low m_{3/2} [estimate]. A non-BPS brane sector wrapping the T² is the remaining option; not built.
Draft: the v3.3 Project H assumption list now states this condition, with 0805.1874 cited; builds clean, 18 pages.
Verdict: Project H stands as a candidate, with a sharper and more restrictive model-building requirement. Nice side link: the SUSY-preserving (soft) version of the same mechanism produces sibling B (α = 1/3).
LESSONS: any one-loop mass in a SUSY setup cancels at leading order; always ask what breaks SUSY in the loop and at which scale.
MAP: none

## D951 (Project H): the non-SUSY tower D950 requires has a known string realisation class, brane supersymmetry breaking (bulk SUSY at tree level), but there the one-loop scalar masses on T² have no definite sign
[literature] hep-th/0601158 (thesis on SUSY-breaking mechanisms in open-string vacua; two fetches, parts of chapters 5.1–5.5): (a) brane supersymmetry breaking: the closed-string amplitudes match type I, so the bulk stays supersymmetric at tree level, with breaking expected to reach the closed sector only at higher genus (from g = 3/2); (b) on T² the BSB one-loop Wilson-line potential is V ∝ 𝒰(a) − 𝒰(b) from Jacobi theta functions; of its 16 stationary points 14 are saddles and 2 minima, with Hessian eigenvalues ±λ, ±μ: the induced masses² take both signs; (c) Scherk–Schwarz: tachyonic regions (R < √α′ for momentum shifts; with B-field on T⁴); the string one-loop sums are Gaussian-weighted lattice sums (Poisson-resummed), which reduce to Epstein sums only in the field-theory limit R ≫ √α′ [standard, not re-derived here].
[estimate] Fit to D945/D950: BSB is the natural class for a sequestered non-SUSY brane tower (bulk and visible sector SUSY at tree level, as D950 needs). But the sign of χ's induced mass² is set by the boson-minus-fermion content of that tower, and in the one worked T² example (Wilson lines) both signs occur. D945's "positive for a boson loop" therefore becomes a requirement on the brane spectrum (n_B > n_F in the states coupled to χ), not a guarantee. The field-theory (Epstein, s = 2) form needs the T² to be larger than the string length.
Verdict: Project H now has a named realisation class with three explicit conditions (non-SUSY brane tower with n_B > n_F among χ's partners; T² ≫ l_s; small tree mass for χ). No construction checked. The v3.3 draft's wording ("non-supersymmetric at the T² scale") already covers this; no change.
LESSONS: a worked example (BSB Wilson lines) is the fastest sign check for a loop-mass mechanism.
MAP: none

## D952 (Project H, scale window): the T² area A₁ (string units) has a wide consistent window, 20g–200g ≲ A₁ ≲ 3e6–7e7; the benchmark's small T⁴ (A₂ = A₃ = 1) matches D945a's "other dimensions smaller" requirement
[derived] (dimensions) χ is 4D (dim 1) and Φ is 6D (dim 2), so the quartic coupling is λ₆ = g/M_s². The image sum then gives δm_χ² = g·[2ζ(4)/(4π³)]·E(U,2)·M_s²/A₁² = 0.01745·g·E·M_s²/A₁² (A₁ in string units).
[derived] (arithmetic) EFT: δm_χ² < M_KK² = M_s²/A₁ ⇒ A₁ > 0.01745·g·Ê = 17g (Ê = 1e3) to 175g (Ê = 1e4). KK modes above H: M_s/√A₁ > H = 3.7e12 GeV ⇒ A₁ < (M_s/H)² = 2.6e6 (M_s = 6e15) to 6.6e7 (M_s = 3e16 GeV). The coefficient λ of D946 absorbs the rest (it is free, D946), so "heavy enough" adds no further condition (m²/H² ≈ 6Ê/M², D944).
[estimate] The SERAPIS-E benchmark's A₂ = A₃ = 1 (D-note ~8839) puts the other four dimensions at the string scale, i.e. much smaller than a T² with A₁ ≳ 20, as D945a requires for weight s = 2; α′ corrections on that T⁴ are O(1) (already flagged there). The BHK tilt depends on Im T₁ = A₂A₃/g_s, not on A₁, so the window does not touch C.
Verdict: no scale conflict; Project H's conditions stay those of D950–D951 (non-SUSY brane tower with n_B > n_F, small tree mass, fixed area) plus 20g ≲ A₁ ≲ 1e6.
Tooling: tools/serapis_calc added (Eisenstein Fourier vs lattice, modular invariance, ρ minimum, P3 slope sign, consistency-relation limits and the paper-1 number, exponent rule): 11/11 self-checks pass; required before every locked run from now on.
LESSONS: run the verified toolkit's self-test before locked runs; it would have caught both D943 errors.
MAP: none

## D955 (loop B, step 4; labelled D956 in its first commit, corrected to match the claim): in the Sugimoto brane-SUSY-breaking model the massless open-string sector has n_B − n_F = +32 (bosonic excess): Project H's sign condition (D951) is met there at the massless level
[literature] Mourad & Sagnotti, "An Update on Brane Supersymmetry Breaking" (arXiv:1711.11494, 2017): USp(32) gauge bosons; fermions in the antisymmetric 495; an additional singlet playing the role of a goldstino. The tension left by SUSY breaking drives a runaway (dilaton) potential.
[derived] (arithmetic) dim adj USp(2n) = n(2n+1) = 528 for n = 16; fermion states 495 + 1 = 496 (same on-shell degrees of freedom per 10D vector and Majorana–Weyl spinor, 8 each): n_B − n_F = +32 per state count, i.e. a net bosonic excess.
[estimate] For an image-sum mass of χ with equal couplings to the tower, δm_χ² ∝ (n_B − n_F) > 0 (D945): positive. Caveats: (i) only the massless level is counted; massive open-string levels were not checked; (ii) χ's couplings need not be equal across the multiplet; (iii) BSB's runaway dilaton must be stabilised (assumed in SERAPIS anyway); (iv) reaching the "6D on T²" geometry needs the BSB branes to wrap the T² with the other four dimensions small (D945a), e.g. anti-D5s on T² in a T⁴ × T² orientifold — not constructed here.
Verdict: KILL condition (n_B − n_F ≤ 0) NOT met; the sign condition has a concrete string example at the massless level. Project H's remaining open items: massive-level counts, couplings of χ, and an explicit anti-D5-on-T² embedding.
LESSONS: the memory recall "496 antisymmetric" was the sum 495 + goldstino; the source separates them. Verified before use.

## D957 (loop B, massive levels): the Sugimoto open-string tower's boson excess is +N d_l (−1)^l level by level: positive at the massless level, alternating at massive levels; for a T² larger than the string length the massless level dominates the image sum, so D955's sign holds where Project H needs it
(Lock files PREREG_D957/D958 belong to the queued ρ and N* reproductions; D-numbers and lock names differ, as in D710.)
[literature] Mourad & Sagnotti (arXiv:1711.11494, eq. 2.22 and text): the Sugimoto model differs from the supersymmetric SO(32) string only in the sign of the V₈ term in the Möbius amplitude, M = −½𝒩 ∫(dτ₂/τ₂²)(−V̂₈ − Ŝ₈)/(τ₂⁴η̂⁸); the annulus is the SO(32) one, A ∝ ½𝒩²(V₈ − S₈). The fetched text does not discuss massive levels.
[derived] (from the quoted amplitudes) Open-string count per level l: bosons ½(𝒩² + ε_l 𝒩) d_l, fermions ½(𝒩² − ε_l 𝒩) d_l, where d_l is the common level degeneracy (V₈ and S₈ have equal coefficients at every level, Jacobi's identity) and ε_l is the sign of the Möbius term at level l. So n_B − n_F = ε_l 𝒩 d_l. At l = 0, ε = +1: +32 states (matches D955: 528 − 496).
[literature, standard but NOT verified in this fetch] The hatted characters of the Möbius strip carry the phase e^{−iπ(h − c/24)}, which alternates the sign from one mass level to the next, ε_l = (−1)^l. Flagged: per the D657a rule this must be checked against a source before it is used in a paper.
[estimate] For the image sum of D945 the level-l states contribute ∝ e^{−m_l|w|} with m_l ~ √l M_s; for |w| ~ √A₁ l_s with A₁ ≳ 20 (D952) the massive levels are suppressed by ≳ e^{−4.5} per level, so the massless +32 excess dominates and δm_χ² > 0. If the T² approached the string length the alternating massive levels would matter and the sign is not guaranteed.
Verdict: Project H's sign condition holds in the Sugimoto model in the regime D952 already requires (A₁ ≫ 1); open: verify the (−1)^l phase from a source; massive-level effects for A₁ ~ 1.
LESSONS: a partition function's character structure gives the level-by-level boson–fermion count in one line once the amplitudes are quoted.
MAP: none

## D961 (Project H, embedding): an explicit string model has exactly the geometry Project H needs: the Antoniadis–Dudas–Sagnotti T⁴/Z₂ orientifold puts 32 anti-D5 branes, with SUSY broken only on them, in six dimensions; their massless sector has a bosonic excess of +128 on-shell degrees of freedom
(Lock file PREREG_D961 belongs to the queued Project H vacuum computation; numbering differs, as in D710.)
[literature] Antoniadis, Dudas & Sagnotti, "Brane supersymmetry breaking" (arXiv:hep-th/9908023, 1999): six-dimensional T⁴/Z₂ orientifold with 32 D9 and 32 anti-D5 branes; gauge group [SO(16)×SO(16)]₉ × [USp(16)×USp(16)]_5̄; "the 5̄5̄ DD spectrum is not supersymmetric": vectors of USp(16)², scalar quartets in (16,16); right-handed Weyl fermions in (120,1)+(1,120), left-handed in (16,16). The 99 sector and the bulk stay supersymmetric; tachyon-free; RR tadpoles cancel; anomalies cancel via a generalised Green–Schwarz mechanism; tree-level runaway V ∝ e^{−φ₆}/√v.
[derived] (arithmetic, 6D on-shell counts: vector 4, real scalar 1, Weyl spinor 4) bosons 2·136·4 + 256·4 = 2112; fermions (240 + 256)·4 = 1984; n_B − n_F = +128 = 4 × 32, matching the +32-per-state pattern of D955.
[estimate] Fit to Project H: the anti-D5 worldvolume is six-dimensional and transverse to the T⁴; compactifying two of its directions on a T² gives R⁴ × T² with the T⁴ separate, the geometry D945a requires (the T⁴ must be smaller than the T²). Its fields are the "6D loop field" with a non-supersymmetric tower and a bosonic excess, so the image-sum mass of a χ coupled to them is positive at the massless level (D945, D957, D960). What is not shown: a field χ with the required couplings to the 5̄5̄ sector, the stabilisation of the runaway dilaton and volume, and the cosmological embedding (T² modulus = SERAPIS's U, small T⁴, T² ≫ l_s).
Verdict: Project H now has a named, published, tachyon-free string model with the right geometry and the right sign; the remaining gap is the χ coupling and moduli stabilisation, not the existence of the sector.
LESSONS: when a mechanism needs "a non-SUSY sector in D dimensions", search the brane-SUSY-breaking orientifold catalogue first.

## D963 (correction to D955, D957, D961's sign conclusion): in the one worked brane-SUSY-breaking example of a one-loop scalar mass, the mass² is NEGATIVE; "bosonic excess ⇒ positive mass²" is not a general rule, so Project H's sign condition is OPEN again
[literature] Antoniadis, Benakli & Quirós, "Radiative symmetry breaking in brane models" (hep-ph/0004091, 2000): non-supersymmetric Z₂ orientifold with N = 2 supersymmetric D9 branes and SUSY broken on anti-D5 branes through the Möbius amplitude; for Wilson-line scalars on the anti-D5s, μ²(R) = −ε²(R) g² M_s² < 0 (their eq. 9), finite, with ε² from a lattice sum Σ n² e^{−2πn²R²l} (one compact circle) and ε → ε_∞/(M_s R), ε_∞² = 3ζ(5)/4π⁴ at large R. They note the negative sign is correlated with a positive vacuum energy and that its origin is not understood in depth.
[derived] Why D945's argument does not carry over: D945 assumed χ couples to the tower through a positive quartic, giving δm² = λ Σ′G(L) ∝ (n_B − n_F). A Wilson-line (or position) modulus instead shifts the tower's masses; its mass² is the second derivative of a potential Σ (n_B − n_F)-weighted cos(2πn a)/n^{D}, and the cosine's curvature flips the sign. Which applies depends on how χ enters the tower's masses, not only on n_B − n_F.
Corrections: D955/D957/D961 stand as counts (+32, +128 bosonic excess; the (−1)^l structure), but their "therefore δm_χ² > 0" verdicts are withdrawn. The v3.3 draft's Project H text (D949/D950) does not claim the sign (it lists "a six-dimensional loop field coupled to it whose tower is non-supersymmetric"); a sentence stating the sign as an open condition will be added.
Open (new, concrete): for a χ coupled by a positive quartic (a brane-position or charged scalar whose mass is NOT a Wilson-line/shift), compute the sign in the ADS model; and note the opposite possibility: a negative E(U,2) mass² would turn P3's series combination into a different shape (A < 0), to be checked.
LESSONS: a sign argument from state counting must be checked against a worked example of the same kind of coupling before it is recorded as a verdict.
