## D964 (Project H, follows D963): a NEGATIVE one-loop mass gives no plateau at all: χ is stable only while aE < B, and V_min = −B·X/(1 − X) (X = aE/B) runs to −∞ as X → 1; so Project H needs the positive sign strictly, and the D963 question is decisive, not a detail
[derived] (sympy) With A = −aE (a > 0): V″(χ) = 2(B − aE), so the χ* = B/(A+B) extremum is a minimum only for aE < B; there V_min/B = X/(X − 1) = −X/(1 − X) < 0, decreasing without bound as X → 1⁻; for aE > B the χ direction is tachyonic and the quadratic model has no minimum (a quartic in χ would be needed, and its shape is not P3's). Since E(U,2) grows toward the cusp, the cusp region is the unstable one: the opposite of a plateau.
Consequence: Project H survives only if χ's one-loop mass² is positive. The one worked brane-SUSY-breaking example (Wilson-line scalars, D963) has the wrong sign; a χ coupled through a positive quartic (a position or charged scalar whose mass is not a shift of the tower) is the remaining candidate and must be computed. Status: Project H = candidate with one decisive open sign condition.
LESSONS: when an open condition's failure branch is cheap to compute, compute it at once to see whether the condition is decisive.
MAP: none

## D965 (Project H, sign): for a χ localised on a brane and CHARGED under a bulk gauge group whose tower breaks SUSY, the finite one-loop mass² is POSITIVE (gauge loops); the negative cases (D963, Contino–Pilo) are Wilson-line and Yukawa-coupled fields; Project H's sign condition is met if χ is a gauge-charged localised scalar
[literature] Antoniadis, Dimopoulos, Pomarol & Quirós, "Soft masses in theories with supersymmetry breaking by TeV compactification" (hep-ph/9810410, 1998), eq. 3.14: brane-localized scalars get m_i² = g²C(R_i)/(4π⁴)·[Δm²(0) − Δm²(q_F)], Δm²(q) = ½[Li₃(e^{2πiq}) + Li₃(e^{−2πiq})]M_c²; finite and UV-independent; the paper states "the above contributions are positive" (squarks, sleptons). The Higgs gets a positive bulk-gauge contribution too, driven negative only by a two-loop stop term. [literature] Contino & Pilo (hep-ph/0104130): a brane Higgs coupled by a top Yukawa to bulk hypermultiplets gets m² = −21ζ(3)N_c f_t²/(64π⁴R²) < 0.
[derived] (mpmath) at q_F = ½: Δm²(0) − Δm²(½) = (7/4)ζ(3) M_c² = 2.1035996 M_c² (checked), so m² = 7g²Cζ(3)/(16π⁴) M_c² > 0. On a circle (D = 5) the lattice weight is ζ(3) = Σ1/n³, i.e. s = (D−2)/2 = 3/2 per D945; on a T² (D = 6) the same gauge-loop structure gives the s = 2 lattice sum ∝ E(U,2) [estimate: the T² generalisation is the D945 image sum with the gauge propagator; not computed here].
Rule (from the three worked examples): gauge loops → positive; Yukawa (fermion) loops → negative; Wilson-line/shift moduli → negative (D963). So Project H's χ must be a gauge-charged, brane-localised scalar whose leading coupling to the non-SUSY tower is gauge, not Yukawa, and not a Wilson line. In the ADS model (D961) the 9–5̄ ND scalars charged under USp(16)_5̄ are the natural candidates [estimate; their mass not computed].
Verdict: D964's decisive condition has a sourced positive branch. Project H: candidate, with χ specified as a gauge-charged localised scalar; remaining: compute the ND-scalar mass on R⁴ × T² in the ADS model, and the pinning term B.
LESSONS: classify sign results by coupling type (gauge / Yukawa / Wilson line) before generalising.
MAP: none

## D966 (Project H): the ADPQ gauge-loop mass IS an image sum (checked); on R⁴ × T² the same structure gives m_χ² ∝ +g²C [S(0) − S(q)] with S a T² winding sum of weight s = 2, i.e. ∝ E(U,2)/A² when the gauge sector has no light gauginos, as in the ADS anti-D5 sector
[derived] (mpmath) Σ_{n≥1}(1 − cos 2πnq)/n³ at q = ½ = 2.103599581 = (7/4)ζ(3): ADPQ's Δm²(0) − Δm²(q_F) (D965) is exactly the circle (D = 5) image sum, bosonic windings minus gaugino windings shifted by the Scherk–Schwarz phase.
[derived] (structure) On R⁴ × T² the gauge propagator's windings are |w|² = A|m + nU|²/Im U with weight |w|^{−(D−2)} = |w|^{−4}: S(0) = Σ′ 1/|w|⁴ = 2ζ(4)E(U,2)/A² (bosons), and the gaugino sum S(q) carries the SUSY-breaking phases. In the ADS 5̄5̄ sector there are no massless gauginos ("no massless gauginos", D961 source), so at the massless level only S(0) survives: m_χ² ≈ g²C(R)·c₆·2ζ(4)E(U,2)/A² > 0, with c₆ the 6D loop normalisation [estimate: c₆ and the massive-level corrections not computed].
Consequence: a χ that is a brane-localised scalar charged under USp(16)_5̄ (e.g. a 9–5̄ ND state) gets exactly the positive A ∝ E(U,2) Project H needs, with s = 2 because the anti-D5 worldvolume is 6D (D945a). This turns Project H's sign condition from "open" (D963–D964) to "met in structure, coefficient uncomputed".
Next (prep for the queue, locked): numerically evaluate S(0) on T² against 2ζ(4)E(U,2) (identity check via the toolkit lattice sum) and the c₆ loop factor from the 6D gauge propagator; then the pinning term B for the same χ.
LESSONS: a known one-dimensional loop result plus the image-sum weight rule gives the torus result's structure in one step.
MAP: none

## D967 (Project H, pinning term): a CHARGED χ (needed for the positive sign, D965) cannot have P3's linear pinning term −2Bχ; the gauge-invariant options are (i) a D-term/Higgs quartic, which gives a flat-topped potential with no 1/E approach (not P3), or (ii) mixing with a second charged field at a vev φ₀, B|χ − φ₀|², which gives P3 exactly but breaks the gauge group
[derived] (gauge invariance) B(1−χ)² = B − 2Bχ + Bχ² contains a tadpole linear in χ, allowed only for a gauge singlet. D965 requires χ charged under the non-SUSY gauge group, so the D941 form must be rewritten gauge-invariantly.
[derived] (sympy) (i) V = Aχ² + λ(χ² − v²)²: for A < 2λv², V_min = Av² − A²/(4λ); for A ≥ 2λv², χ = 0 and V = λv⁴ exactly. With A ∝ Ê the potential reaches an exactly flat top at finite Ê (no 1/Ê approach): inflation would sit on a flat top with only the ramp, not P3's power-law approach (k = 2 lost; the D929 exponent rule then gives no p at all). Not SERAPIS.
[derived] (sympy) (ii) V = A|χ|² + B|χ − φ₀|² with φ₀ the vev of a second field in the same representation: V_min = ABφ₀²/(A + B), exactly P3 (D941) times φ₀². Gauge invariant (χ − φ₀ transforms covariantly), but ⟨φ₀⟩ ≠ 0 breaks the gauge group, giving the gauge bosons masses m_V ~ gφ₀ that cut off the image sum at |w| ≳ 1/m_V [estimate: if m_V ≪ 1/√A₁ (T² scale) the E(U,2) form survives].
Consequence: Project H's χ must be (charged) AND (mixed with a vev-carrying partner of the same charge), with the gauge-breaking scale gφ₀ below the T² KK scale. A new, sharp model-building condition; not yet checked in the ADS model.
LESSONS: check every term of an effective potential against the symmetry of the field it was assigned to.
MAP: none

## D968 (Project H, follows D967): a gauge-boson mass m_V from the pinning vev corrects each winding by −(m_V|w|)²/4, i.e. adds a weight-1 piece −(m_V²/4)·Σ′|w|⁻² to the weight-2 E(U,2) sum; the correction is small when m_V ≪ M_KK of the T², and it falls on the plateau relative to E(U,2)
[derived] (Bessel expansion, checked with mpmath) G₆(L; m) = (m/2πL)² K₂(mL)/2π = (1/4π³L⁴)[1 − (mL)²/4 + O((mL)⁴ ln mL)]; numerically G₆(m)/G₆(0) = 0.999377 / 0.99025 / 0.94377 vs 1 − (mL)²/4 = 0.999375 / 0.99 / 0.9375 at mL = 0.05 / 0.2 / 0.5.
[derived] So Σ′G₆(|w|; m_V) = (1/4π³)[Σ′|w|⁻⁴ − (m_V²/4) Σ′|w|⁻² + …] = (1/4π³)[2ζ(4)E(U,2)/A² − (m_V²/4A)·E_reg(U,1) + …], where the weight-1 lattice sum needs regularisation (its U-dependence is the Kronecker-limit form −ln(U₂|η(U)|⁴), linear in y at large y) [standard; the regularisation constant drops out of the U-dependence].
[estimate] Relative size of the correction on the plateau ~ (m_V²A/4)·(πy/3)/(2ζ(4)y²) ∝ m_V²A/y: it decreases toward the cusp, and is ≪ 1 for m_V ≪ M_KK = 1/√A (string units) at y ~ 20–25. A weight-1 admixture would add a k = 1 (p = √2) component to the approach; requirement: m_V²A ≲ 1e-2 to keep the p = 2√2 approach to better than ~1% over the observable window [estimate].
Verdict: D967's mixing route is consistent if the pinning vev breaks the gauge group well below the T² KK scale (g φ₀ ≲ 0.1 M_KK). Project H's condition list: χ gauge-charged and brane-localised; mixed with a same-charge vev φ₀; g φ₀ ≲ 0.1 M_KK; non-SUSY 6D gauge tower without light gauginos; fixed T² area; 20g ≲ A₁ ≲ 1e6.
LESSONS: a mass for the loop particle lowers the lattice weight by one at first order; check which weight the leading correction carries.
MAP: none

## D969 (Project H): the ADS model's 9–5̄ scalars come as "doublets" in (16,1,1,16) and (1,16,16,1): two copies per representation, so a same-charge (χ, φ₀) pair exists in principle; the source gives no potential, vevs or masses for them, and their mixing is not shown
[literature] Antoniadis–Dudas–Sagnotti (hep-th/9908023): the ND sector "comprises doublets of scalars in the (16,1,1,16) and in the (1,16,16,1)"; from the D9 viewpoint "complex scalars and symplectic Majorana–Weyl fermions in the representations 16 × [(16,1) + (1,16)]"; "all 95̄ terms do not contribute to the vacuum energy" (the ND annulus vanishes); no tree-level potential, vevs or one-loop masses for these scalars are given; the only potential derived is V_eff = c e^{−φ₆}/√v (positive, localised on the D5s).
[estimate] Fit to D965–D968: each ND scalar is localised (at the 9–5̄ overlap) and charged under USp(16)_5̄, the gauge group of the non-SUSY sector without light gauginos, so its one-loop mass from 5̄5̄ gauge loops should be positive with the E(U,2)/A² structure on a T² (D966). The doublet's two copies are in the SAME representation, so one can play χ and the other φ₀, and a mass mixing χ†φ₀ is gauge-allowed; whether the doublet index (not identified in the source) forbids it is OPEN. The two different representations (16,1,1,16) and (1,16,16,1) cannot mix.
[caution] The vanishing ND annulus concerns the vacuum energy of the 9–5̄ strings, not the mass χ gets from 5̄5̄ gauge loops; the two should not be conflated, but a direct computation of the ND scalar's one-loop mass in this model is not in the source and is not done here.
Verdict: the ADS model supplies every ingredient Project H lists (6D non-SUSY gauge tower without light gauginos; charged localised scalars; a same-representation partner), with two unchecked links: the doublet-index symmetry vs χ†φ₀ mixing, and the actual one-loop ND-scalar mass. Next step is a calculation in the model (string one-loop two-point function of ND scalars on T⁴/Z₂ × T²), beyond a cheap tick; recorded as Project H's top open item.
LESSONS: when a source says "doublet" without naming the group, record the ambiguity rather than guess the symmetry.

## D970 (Project H, coefficient): calibrating the image-sum method on ADPQ's 5D result gives the gauge-loop factor κ = 4C = (D−1)C exactly; with the same (D−1) rule in 6D, m_χ² = (5ζ(4)/2π³) g²C E(U,2)/A = 0.0873 g²C E(U,2)/A (A the physical T² area, g the 4D gauge coupling)
[derived] (mpmath) Image sum on a circle: g₅² = 2πR g², G₅(L) = Γ(3/2)/(4π^{5/2}L³), Σ_{n≠0} G₅(2πRn) = ζ(3)/(32π⁵R³). Matching ADPQ's bosonic part g²Cζ(3)/(4π⁴R²) (D965) requires m² = κ g₅² Σ′G₅ with κ = 4.0000000000 C, which equals (D−1)C at D = 5: the Feynman-gauge seagull (D) minus the scalar–vector exchange (1) [the (D−1) reading is an interpretation; the number 4 is computed].
[estimate] Assuming the same (D−1) counting in D = 6 (κ = 5C) and the D945 lattice identity Σ′|w|⁻⁴ = 2ζ(4)E(U,2)/A² with g₆² = A g²: m_χ² = 5C g² A · (1/4π³) · 2ζ(4)E(U,2)/A² = (5ζ(4)/2π³) g²C E(U,2)/A, coefficient 0.087266 (no light gauginos; massless level only; Feynman-gauge counting not re-derived in 6D).
Use: in D941's language A = m_χ² M² × (field normalisation) and the plateau needs λ′ ≤ 1/E(ρ,2) (D947); with this coefficient the ratio A/B is set by g²C/(A B) and is free (D946), so no new constraint arises from c₆ itself; it fixes how heavy χ is: m_χ² ~ 0.09 g²C·Ê·M_KK² ≫ H² for Ê ~ 1e3 unless g²C is tiny [estimate].
Verdict: Project H's mass term now has an explicit coefficient (calibrated in 5D, extended to 6D by a stated rule). Remaining open items unchanged (doublet mixing, string-level ND mass, stabilisation).
LESSONS: calibrate an image-sum normalisation on a published lower-dimensional result before using it in a new dimension.

## D971 (correction to D970): the 6D coefficient is 2ζ(4)/π³ = 0.0698, not 5ζ(4)/2π³: a published 6D computation (Lee, T²/Z₂) fixes κ = 4C in six dimensions too; D970's (D−1) rule was wrong by 5/4
[literature] H. M. Lee, "Softness of supersymmetry breaking on the orbifold T²/Z₂" (hep-th/0502093, 2005): brane-scalar one-loop mass from 6D bulk gauge KK modes, m_φ²(0) = [g₄²Q²/(2π³R₅²)] ∫₀¹ dx (J₂[0,0,0] − J₂[ω₅,ω₆,0]), J_j = Σ_{n₅,n₆} ∫dt t^{−(j−ε/2)} exp(−πt[a₅(n₅+ω₅)² + a₆(n₆+ω₆)²]), a₅ = x, a₆ = x(R₅/R₆)²; positive; finite ("both divergences … are cancelled"); its one-circle limit is g₄²Q²/(4π⁴R₆²)Σ_k(1 − cos 2πkΔω₆)/k³, the ADPQ form. Lee also notes that codimension-two (point-localised) SUSY-breaking masses give a log-divergent brane-scalar mass, while line/bulk (Scherk–Schwarz-equivalent) breaking gives a finite one.
[derived] (Poisson resummation of J₂[0,0,0], checked numerically on a rectangular torus R₆/R₅ = 1.7) Lee's bosonic winding part = g²Q² A Σ′|w|⁻⁴/π³ = (2ζ(4)/π³) g²Q² E(U,2)/A: per g²Q², 0.004074236141 (Lee) vs 0.004074236141 (κ = 4 form), ratio 1.0000; D970's (κ = 5) value 0.005092795 is 1.25× too large.
Correction: m_χ² = (2ζ(4)/π³) g²C E(U,2)/A = 0.06981 g²C E(U,2)/A (Q² ↔ C(R)). The calibrated κ = 4C holds in both 5D and 6D; the "(D−1)" interpretation in D970 is withdrawn. No conclusion of D970 changes except the number.
Finiteness condition added to Project H's list: the SUSY breaking felt by the gauge tower must be bulk/line-like on the T² (finite), not localised at points of the T² (log divergent). In the ADS model the breaking lives on the whole anti-D5 worldvolume, which contains the T²: bulk-like [estimate].

## D973 (Project H, branch selection): a mass ∝ E(U,2) selects ρ: E(U,2) has an isotropic minimum at ρ (canonical Hessian 11.567, 11.567) but a SADDLE at i (−6.85, +30.96), so Project H can source SERAPIS-E's ρ vacuum but not the τ = i branch (Chronos/Kairos), whose plateau stays postulated
[computed] (tools/serapis_calc, E in the paper's BHK convention) E(i,2) = 6.026812 > E(ρ,2) = 5.783359; canonical Hessian at i: eigenvalues −6.854, +30.961 (saddle: E decreases from i toward ρ along Re τ); at ρ: 11.5667, 11.5667 (isotropic minimum, the Z₃ symmetry).
[derived] Project H's potential is P3(λ′Ê) with Ê ≥ 0 vanishing only at the minimum of E. A vacuum at i would need Ê_i = E − E(i), which is negative near ρ and makes the potential unbounded toward ρ along Re τ; the field would leave i. So Project H realises the plateau only on the ρ branch (SERAPIS-E, and the ρ variant's vacuum), consistent with the paper's statement that SERAPIS-E's plateau, vacuum and tilt use one object.
Consequence: Chronos/Kairos (τ = i, I-invariant plateau built from |j − 1728|) keep P3 as a postulate; Project H is specific to the ρ/E branch. Recorded on the plateau_origin node scope.
LESSONS: check the vacuum's stability in the transverse direction before extending a mechanism to another fixed point.

## D975 (Project H, consequence): realising SERAPIS-E through Project H fixes the physical BHK tilt to C = λ′C₀ ≤ 0.173 × 1.15e-6 = 2.0e-7, i.e. Im S Im T ≳ 4900 for the four-brane excess (vs 750–975 in v3.2): a ~6× larger product of moduli, otherwise the same model
(Lock PREREG_D975 belongs to the queued α_s exact-start run; numbering differs, as in D710.)
[derived] Project H's potential is P3(λ′Ê)(1 + CÊ) = P3(X)(1 + (C/λ′)X) with X = λ′Ê (D946/D947). The published fit uses P3(Ê)(1 + C₀Ê), C₀ = 1.0–1.3e-6. On the plateau the two agree at leading order when C/λ′ = C₀, so the physical one-loop coefficient is C = λ′C₀. The full-mass route has λ′ ≤ 1/E(ρ,2) = 0.1729 (D947), so C ≤ 1.99e-7 (for C₀ = 1.15e-6).

## D982 (PREP 2, five open nodes): a string-level sign rule for brane-scalar one-loop masses (Kitazawa) that favours a bosonic-excess sector; Gaia DR3 prefers Einasto/cored halos; the anti-D3 uplift has no complex-structure dependence at leading order
(Lock PREREG_D982 belongs to the queued leptogenesis Boltzmann run; numbering differs, as in D710.)
1. α_s method [literature]: dedicated Mukhanov–Sasaki solvers (1809.11095, 2103.16594) exist; nothing in them changes the D981-lock plan (wide grid, quadratic-type fit); no action.
2. plateau_origin [literature]: Kitazawa (0805.0824) computes one-loop masses of open-string scalars via closed-string boundary states, including a brane-supersymmetry-breaking model (D3 + anti-D7 at C³/Z₃). His stated rule: the sign of the scalar mass² correlates with (in the bosonic example, is opposite to) the sign of the open-string one-loop vacuum amplitude; with supersymmetry the mass cancels (θ₃⁴ − θ₄⁴ − θ₂⁴ = 0), and the sign then "depends on how the spectrum is modified by the supersymmetry breaking".
[estimate] For Project H: a sector with a bosonic excess (the ADS anti-D5 sector, +128, D968) has a negative one-loop vacuum energy, so by this rule its brane scalars would get positive mass², the sign Project H needs. This is one example's rule applied to a different model, not a computation; it moves the sign condition from "open" to "plausible in the bosonic-excess sector". Together with D981 (1105.0591: traceless adjoint masses at angles, a tachyonic direction), the sign depends on the sector, as D963 already said.
Next calculable step (needs its own lock): a field-theory check of the sign rule on R⁴ × T² — one-loop mass of a gauge-charged brane scalar from a tower with N_B − N_F = +128 vs −128, and its U-dependence, compared with E(U,2)/A².
3. eps_tilt [literature]: the anti-D3 uplift in non-linear supergravity (1707.07059, eq. 1.1–1.2) carries no complex-structure dependence at leading order; consistent with D887 (no source for |j − 1728|^{2q}); stays parked.
4. lepto_rho: limitation of the PREREG_D982 setup noted in advance: N from φ → NN are boosted (γ ≈ m_φ/2M ≈ 10–55); time dilation delays their decay, but with Γ_N ≥ H(T = M) ≫ H(T_R) they still decay well before washout matters; the non-relativistic treatment is an [assumption] stated in the lock; no change.
5. halo_profile [literature]: Singh & Desai (2605.16994, Gaia DR3, Bayesian comparison) prefer Einasto over NFW and cored over cuspy for most baryonic models. For SERAPIS-E's wino this selects D735's two allowed cases (Einasto: M₂ = 0.66–0.80 TeV; kpc cores: any mass); the cuspy case that 2507.15934 excludes is disfavoured by the data. [derived] (D950) A 6D boson–fermion tower on T² split by a soft mass m_s leaves, at first order in m_s², a weight-1 image sum ∝ m_s² Σ′|w|^{−2} = (regularised) −log(U₂|η(U)|⁴) + const: the same function as L (up to the constant ln 2, absorbed in V0).

[literature, standard] During inflation, supergravity couplings give every scalar a soft mass ~ c H (Hubble-induced SUSY breaking; Dine–Randall–Thomas). [estimate] With m_s = cH: ε ≈ N c² M_KK²/(48π² M_P²): 4.6e-6 (N = 128, c = 1, M_KK = 1e16); 1.8e-5 (M_KK = 2e16); 6e-5 needs M_KK ≈ 3.6e16 or c ≈ 3.6 at 1e16 (computed table in the session log).

## D992 (DEEP, Project H / D988, literature + estimate): the sign of χ's local (U-independent) one-loop mass is NOT settled by the literature; the known sign rules decide only the massless (E(U,2)) part, which D985 already has positive; D988 stays OPEN. Also: recheck of serapis_e after D912 → unchanged, flag cleared
Question (D988): the U-independent part of the anti-D5 position scalar's one-loop mass² is string-scale and tied to the uncancelled D̄5/O-plane tadpole; positive → absorbed into λ′, negative → Project H fails. Does existing work fix its sign?
Findings [literature]:
- Abel–Dudas–Lewis–Partouche, arXiv:1812.09714 (Scherk–Schwarz type I, not brane SUSY breaking): brane-position/Wilson-line masses m² ≃ (T_{R_B} − T_{R_F}) ξ″, ξ″ > 0 — sign = Dynkin-index excess of massless bosons over fermions; contributions of states above the breaking scale are O(e^{−cM_s/M}). This is the same rule as Kitazawa 0805.0824 (D982–D983). It governs the IR (massless-loop) part only, i.e. the part that gives Project H its E(U,2) shape; it is silent on a string-scale local term, which in SS models is exponentially small but in brane SUSY breaking (SUSY broken at M_s) is not.
- Dudas–Nicolosi–Pradisi–Sagnotti, hep-th/0410101: lists "scalar masses induced by Wilson lines" among quantities whose dilaton-tadpole IR effects are "either absent or protected by perturbative vertices and/or by the propagation of massive string modes"; tadpole effects on brane observables are hoped small for large transverse volume (stated as a hope). Qualitative only; no sign.
- Review arXiv:2511.04367: vacuum stability with broken SUSY "remains, in general, a vexing open problem"; Dudas–Mourad interval vacua are perturbatively stable in the closed sector; open-string brane-scalar masses on them are not computed.
Estimate: in brane SUSY breaking the local term is a genuine O(M_s²) Möbius/annulus contribution (D988), so the SS exponential suppression does not apply; DNPS's protection argument concerns IR tadpole effects, not this term. No source computes its sign on a Dudas–Mourad (tadpole-backreacted) background.
Verdict: D988 OPEN, no new calculable input; the decisive computation is the D̄5 position-scalar mass on a Dudas–Mourad-type background (beyond the toolkit's present Level S). Novelty: none claimed. Project H keeps its stated condition (local part ≥ 0).
Recheck serapis_e (flag from D912): D912 closed the Eisenstein-Kähler route to the plateau but did not change the SERAPIS-E potential, its tilt or its frozen numbers; node status unchanged; flag cleared.
Sources: arXiv:1812.09714; hep-th/0410101; arXiv:2511.04367; arXiv:0805.0824.

## D1007a (correction to D1007, track R): the gaugino-condensation candidate FAILS as a tilt source if its modulus is the inflaton τ: along the SERAPIS-ρ trajectory L changes by ≈ 19 over the last 50 e-folds, so e^{3L} changes by ~e^{57} — nothing like a linear εL; the linearisation in D1007 is invalid on the inflationary range
[computed] (Janus serapis_rho(6e-5), Re τ = ½, y = e^{√2φ}): N = 60: y 26.69, L 23.98; N = 50: y 24.11, L 21.37; N = 30: y 18.58, L 15.85; N = 10: y 11.28, L 8.70; N = 1: y 4.44, L 2.47. Since L ≈ πy/3 − ln 2y at large y, e^{3L} ∝ e^{πy}/y³ grows doubly-exponentially in φ.
[derived] A term δ·e^{3L}B(τ) small enough not to dominate at N = 60 is ≲ e^{−3·19} ~ 1e-25 of its N = 60 size by N = 50, i.e. it cannot produce a constant fractional slope; conversely, one large enough to tilt at N ≈ 50 dominates (and ends) inflation earlier. What survives: the observation that L appears at leading order in duality-invariant condensation potentials stands, but only for a modulus that is NOT the inflaton (e.g. a second Kähler modulus T' near its own minimum, where L(T') is nearly constant — then it gives no tilt along τ either). ## D1038 — DEEP/STRINGS — why S4c3 converges as ε^0.84: q = (D−2)/((D−1)(1+δ)) [derived; post-hoc explanation of D1036]
Sturm–Liouville form (p u')' + m² w u = 0 with p = e^{(D−1)A + gP/2}, w = e^{(D−3)A − gP/2} (S4c2). Near y→0, sin(ωky) ~ u, so
A ≈ ln u /(2(D−1)(1+δ)), P ≈ (D−2) ln u /(4√(D−1)(1+δ)). Using g/g_c = 1+2δ, g_c = 4√(D−1)/(D−2):
  p ~ u^a with a = [½ + ½(1+2δ)]/(1+δ) = 1 EXACTLY (for any D, g); w ~ u^b with 1+b = (D−2)/((D−1)(1+δ)).
With a = 1 the regular eigenfunction tends to a constant at u→0, so cutting the interval at ε drops Rayleigh weight ∫₀^ε w u² ∝ ε^{1+b}:
δm² ∝ ε^q, q = (D−2)/((D−1)(1+δ)). D = 6, g = 2: δ = −0.052786, q = 0.8/(0.947214) = 0.84459. Measured (D1036): 0.8429, 0.8442 → match
to 2e-4 in the second triple. The y→y_end end gives ε^{15.16} (negligible), consistent with the clean single power law.
Label: derived after seeing the number (explanation, not a prediction). Bonus fact: p ~ u exactly means y = 0 is a limit-circle,
log-type endpoint — the boundary condition chosen there (θ = π/2, the regular branch) is a physical input to state in the paper.
MAP: none

## D1049 — RIGHT (R track) — a non-GS s = 1 lead: the one-loop matter wave function carries ln(|η|⁴(T+T̄)) with an N=2-sector coefficient [literature]
[literature, fetched hep-th/9301033, Antoniadis–Gava–Narain–Taylor] (i) moduli metric: G⁽¹⁾_{TT̄} = b̃^{GS} G⁽⁰⁾_{TT̄} (Sec. 7) — GS-type, no log (closed,
consistent with D1048). (ii) gauge couplings: −b̃_a ln[|η(iT)|⁴(T+T̄)] (Eq. 19), b̃_a "entirely by N=2 sectors". (iii) untwisted matter wave
function: Y_j = 2γ̃_j ln[|η(iT_j)|⁴(T_j+T̄_j)] + y_j (Eq. 20), γ̃_j = −b̃_j/2, tied to the N=2 vector-multiplet β-function, NOT to δ_GS.
Why it matters: a potential that is an F-term of a matter field A_j, V ∝ |∂_A W|²/Z_A, inherits 1/Z_A ∝ e^{−Y_j} ~ (1 + 2γ̃_j L + …) — the
Kronecker L of D1031 with a coefficient that is (a) not removed by the dilaton shift (it is not GS), (b) zero for Z₃ (no N=2 sectors) and
model-dependent elsewhere, so it CAN be small. This is the first source found with the right structure that survives D1044–D1048.
Not yet a claim: needs (1) whether SERAPIS-ρ's plateau can be a matter F-term with T as the rolling field, (2) the size ε = 6e-5 ↔ γ̃_j
(normalisation of Y_j vs ln Z), (3) the ℓ-vs-L question again (does Y_j hold at fixed GS-shifted dilaton? — it is a matter-sector
quantity, so the S' shift should not touch it; to be checked). Next R step: lock (1)–(3) as a derivation plan.
MAP: none

## D1051 — RIGHT (R track) — size of the D1049 matter-log tilt: natural ~1e-2; ε = 6e-5 needs an almost-vanishing N=2 anomalous dimension [literature + estimate]
[literature, fetched hep-th/9301033] Y_i ≡ finite part of G⁽¹⁾_{iī}/G⁽⁰⁾_{iī} (Sec. 6, text before Eq. 15); it enters Yukawas as [1 + g²(Y_i+Y_j+Y_k)]^{−1/2}
(Eq. 15); γ̃_j = −b̃_j/2 is "the anomalous dimension of A_j in the N=2 theory"; one-loop γ_i = −(1/64π²){−(4/k)C₂(R_i) + g⁻²Σ|λ_ijk|²} (Eq. 14);
b = (1/32π²)(−3Tr Q_V² + Tr Q_M²) (Eq. 7). No orbifold numbers given. (Source text is partly garbled on g² bookkeeping — noted.)
[derived/estimate] A matter-F-term plateau V ∝ |∂_A W|²/(G⁽⁰⁾(1 + g²Y)) gives V ∝ P·(1 − 2g²γ̃ ln[|η|⁴·2Im T] + …) = P·(1 + 2g²γ̃ L + …):
the multiplicative L-tilt of D1010 with κ = 2g²γ̃. Since D1010 matched with κ = ε, the needed size is g²γ̃ = 3e-5.
Natural size: γ̃ ~ (1/64π²)×(group factor O(1–10)) ~ 1.6e-3 to 1.6e-2, × 2g² (g² ≈ 0.5) → κ ~ 1.6e-3 to 1.6e-2: 30–300× too large — UNLESS the
gauge and Yukawa terms in Eq. 14 nearly cancel (γ̃ → 0 is the N=2 finiteness condition; Z₃ has γ̃ = 0 exactly). So this lead also needs a
small number, but now a small number with a known physical meaning: near-finite N=2 sectors (|γ̃| ~ 2% of natural).
Status: lead KEPT (structure right, not killed by the S' shift), size problem RESTATED as near-finiteness. Not claimed.
MAP: none

## D1089 (CENTRE, Djl loop (C), locked PREREG_C2): Hyperion's Jeans dispersions in MWPotential2014 match the measured halo-star profile for β = 0–0.5; with the measured β ≈ 0.8 the model runs 12–46 km/s too hot, and a 1.5× heavier halo is disfavoured unless the halo is isotropic — the Galaxy loop now has a real-data handle on the halo amplitude

- Data (quoted): Battaglia+2005: σ ≈ 120 km/s to 30 kpc; −0.6r + 132 beyond 40 kpc; 50 ± 22 at 120 kpc. Tracer ρ ∝ r^−3.5. Bird+2019 β ≈ 0.8 (K giants, roughly constant to 25 kpc, less radial beyond).

  - The data are a 2005 sample of 240 objects. Gaia-era profiles (e.g. Bird+2019 tables) would sharpen this; not fetched (abstract has no numbers).

## D1095 (CENTRE, Djl loop (A), literature reading, no new computation): the paper's text favours the √2 convention for the NLO off-diagonal, but only indirectly — so A1c's 2.423 TeV (+0.16%) is CONSISTENT post hoc, not a blind validation; A1d not locked
- Sourced (arXiv:2009.00640, via fetch):
  - The momentum-space NLO correction Eq. 3.7 has δV_{χ0χ0→χ+χ−} = −4πα₂/(k²+m_W²)[…] with the same prefactor as the tree entry Eq. 2.4, i.e. method-I channel notation with no √2.
  - The paper says "the transition from method-I to method-II follows the same rules as the tree-level potential". The tree-level transition is what produces the −√2 in Eq. 2.8.
  - Eq. 3.25's left-hand side uses the same channel labels (δV_{χ0χ0→χ+χ−}).
  - BUT the text also calls 3.25 a fit to "the off-diagonal potentials in (2.8) and (2.9)". Read literally, that suggests adding it as is.
  - No explicit statement resolves this. The fetch tool's own inference also favoured √2.
- Assessment: the weight of the text (method-I labels plus "same rules as tree level") favours ×√2. With ×√2, A1c's reported result is 2.4229 TeV vs 2.419 (+0.16%).
- Because I already knew that number when reading the text, this is NOT an independent validation. Re-locking A1d with √2 now would be a post-hoc convention choice, so it is recorded as CONSISTENT (post hoc) instead. A1c stays NOT VALIDATED as locked.
- Independent confirmation route (open): reproduce a SECOND number from the paper with the same convention, chosen before computing. Candidates: the NLO relic mass 2.842 TeV (needs a relic-density solver, larger job) or another resonance/Sommerfeld value quoted in its tables.
- Practical: Hyperion's NLO module uses off_factor = √2 as its working default, labelled post-hoc. For the CMB band, the difference between conventions is 0.03 TeV.
VERDICT: CONSISTENT (post hoc); convention favoured by the text but not explicit. A1e (blind second number) is the real test.
MAP: none

- Verdict: no SERAPIS tension. The D/H 1.7σ is a nuclear-physics open item shared with ΛCDM.

## D1100 (CENTRE, Djl loop (B), literature + arithmetic): lithium-7 — standard BBN predicts 7Li/H = (4.94 ± 0.72)e-10 vs the Spite plateau (1.6 ± 0.3)e-10 (factor 3.1, ≈ 4.3σ); SERAPIS cannot touch it (ΔN = 0, decays at t ≲ 1e-17 s) and inherits it exactly as ΛCDM does — it stays an astrophysical/nuclear open problem

- SERAPIS levers:
  - (a) ΔN_eff = 0 (ρ); for τ=i, at most 0.054 survives ACT (D1092). A small ΔN shifts Li-7 only at the few-percent level [estimate, from expansion-rate sensitivity], far from a factor of 3.
  - (b) Late decays: the ρ-branch heavy states decay at t ≈ 1e-17 – 1e-19 s (D1082), sixteen or more decades too early. Destroying ⁷Be needs energy injection at t ~ 1e2–1e4 s [standard picture, labelled from memory].
  - (c) ω_b is fixed at Planck's value.
  - So SERAPIS neither causes nor cures the lithium problem.
- Verdict: no model-specific tension. Li-7 sits with D/H (D1096) as Standard-Model-level BBN open items that SERAPIS inherits unchanged.
- Hyperion gap noted: no Li-7 calculator (would need a BBN network, e.g. PRyMordial or AlterBBN; not pip-installable earlier, so re-check).
VERDICT: SM-level; SERAPIS neutral.
MAP: none

## D1103 (CENTRE, Djl loop (A), locked PREREG_A1f; NLO convention post hoc): with the NLO wino potential the CMB-excluded band is 2.18–2.62 TeV (f_eff 0.14) to ≤2.00–2.76 TeV (f_eff 0.41); the NLO thermal wino (2.842–2.86 TeV) is ALLOWED with margin f_max = 1.19–1.24 — D1087's "marginal" rigid-shift estimate was too pessimistic
Lock pushed before run; result field_tests/results/a1f_cmb_nlo.txt.
- A1e still has no blind target: 2507.15934 (fetched) quotes no σv or Sommerfeld numbers, only the NLO thermal mass 2.86 ± 0.01 TeV (citing 2009.00640).
- Inputs: Beneke+ on-shell couplings (α₂ = 0.03479); tree Γ; v = 1e-7; grid 2.00–3.00 TeV in 0.02 steps; Planck p_ann < 3.2e-28; NLO off-diagonal ×√2 (post hoc, D1095).
- Results:
  - LO (same inputs): excluded 2.04–2.50 (f_eff 0.14) / 2.00–2.64 TeV (0.41).
  - NLO: excluded 2.18–2.62 / 2.00–2.76 TeV.
  - The lower edge at f_eff 0.41 sits at the grid start; D1081 found 1.9 TeV allowed, so the true edge is between 1.9 and 2.0.
  - NLO raises σv near 2.85 TeV by ×1.7 (1.57e-24 vs 9.0e-25 at 2.842).
  - At the NLO thermal mass 2.842 / 2.86 TeV: f_max = 1.189 / 1.244 (f_eff 0.41) and 2.04 / 2.13 (f_eff 0.14). The thermal wino is CMB-ALLOWED in every case, with about 19% margin in abundance (×1.41 in σv) at the high f_eff.
- Supersedes D1087's rigid-shift estimate (band to ~2.84 TeV, "marginal"). The real NLO band ends at 2.76 TeV, below the thermal mass.
- SERAPIS-E wino points (0.66–1.85 TeV): outside every band, so unchanged.
- Caveats:
  - Post-hoc √2 convention. The primary convention would shift the resonance by −0.03 TeV, moving the band down and adding margin.
  - Tree Γ (NLO annihilation matrices not used).
  - Single f_eff per run; no f_eff(M) tables.
VERDICT: thermal wino CMB-ALLOWED at NLO (f_max ≥ 1.19, post-hoc convention); A1e still open.

## D1105 (CENTRE, Djl loop (C), locked PREREG_C6 + DEVIATIONS D1): the local escape speed pulls the OTHER way — Gaia's 528 (+24/−25) km/s (Deason+2019) wants halo amplitude ≥ 1.1 (to 2 r200), while the K-giant M200 (D1097) wants ≤ 1.1; the standard MWPotential2014 (s = 1) is 2.1σ low on v_esc; all Milky Way constraints overlap only at s ≈ 1.1
Lock pushed before run. D1: galpy's bulge potential (PowerSphericalPotentialwCutoff) has a constant offset Φ(∞) = +1.345 (natural units), which broke the "to infinity" definition. Fixed via DEVIATIONS before the rerun; definition (i) was unaffected. Result field_tests/results/c6_vesc.txt.
- Data (quoted): v_esc(8.3 kpc) = 528 +24/−25 km/s; M200,tot = 1.00 +0.31/−0.24 e12 (Deason+2019).
- Escape speed to 2 r200 (definition labelled unverified) / to infinity:
  - s = 0.8: 439 (−3.6σ) / 471 (−2.3σ) → NOT
  - s = 1.0: 475 (−2.1σ, NOT) / 509 (−0.7σ)
  - s = 1.1: 493 (−1.4σ) / 528 (0.0σ) → CONSISTENT
  - s = 1.2: 509 (−0.7σ) / 545 (+0.7σ) → CONSISTENT
- Joint reading:
  - D1089 dispersions: s ≤ 1.0–1.2 depending on β.
  - D1093 enclosed mass: 0.8–1.2.
  - D1097 M200: K giants ≤ 1.1, BHB anything.
  - Escape speed: ≥ 1.1 (2 r200 definition) or ≥ 0.9 (infinity).
  - The common window is s ≈ 1.0–1.1 (infinity definition) or ≈ 1.1 (2 r200). The standard model sits at the light edge.
- For the wino (W2): s = 1.1 gives J and ρ_⊙ about 10% above standard (ρ_⊙ ≈ 0.315 GeV/cm³ [interpolated]). The W2 verdicts (≤ 1 TeV pass, 1.85 fail) hold across 0.8–1.2.
- Caveats:
  - The definition of v_esc (2 r200 vs ∞) moves the answer by 35 km/s; I should source Deason's exact r_max.
  - One-parameter halo scaling: a heavier halo with a different scale radius could satisfy both M200 and v_esc.
VERDICT: tension between v_esc and the K-giant M200 is resolved only at s ≈ 1.1; the standard model is mildly too light (2.1σ on v_esc, 2 r200 definition).
MAP: none

Lock pushed before run. Result field_tests/results/b5_linx.txt. LINX via pip linx-bbn (commit bfba07c on GitHub, for reference), network key_PRIMAT_2023, Ωbh2 = 0.02242, 68 s including JIT.

  - B2/B3 use the same nucleon-fraction Y_p, so their helium pulls shift the same way (closer to Aver). The verdicts are unchanged.
  - DEVIATIONS_B1 D1 is written. bbn.py's docstring is fixed, and bbn.Yp_mass has been added (bbn.Yp is left as is for reproducibility).
- Hyperion now has three BBN routes: PRIMAT table, PRyMordial, LINX. That is a good basis for a validated bbn_net module (B4b next).

## D1108 (CENTRE, Djl loop (C), literature check): Deason+2019's escape speed is defined to 2 r200 (fiducial; v_esc = √(2[Φ(r0) − Φ(2r200)])) — exactly D1105's definition (i), so D1105's window stands: the standard MWPotential2014 is 2.1σ low, and the halo amplitude needs s ≳ 1.1
- Source (quoted, arXiv:1901.02016 §3.2/§5):
  - "we choose 2r200 as the limiting radius in our fiducial definition of v_esc". They tested 2, 3 r200 and ∞.
  - M200 comes from an NFW halo with free M200 and c200, fixed baryons (Pouliasis+2017 Model I: Miyamoto–Nagai discs plus a Plummer bulge), combined with v_c(r0) = 230 ± 10 km/s. Result: M200 = 1.00 (+0.31/−0.24) e12, c200 = 10.9 (+4.4/−3.3). With the Dutton–Macciò c(M) relation: 1.29e12.
- Consequences:
  - D1105's "unverified" label on definition (i) is cleared. The (ii) "to infinity" column is not the paper's definition, so drop it from the reading.
  - Window from v_esc alone: s ≥ 1.1 (s = 1.1 at −1.4σ, 1.2 at −0.7σ).
  - Combined with the K-giant M200 (≤ 1.1, D1097), the joint window is s ≈ 1.1.
  - Part of the pull is a known feature of MWPotential2014: it is built on v_c(r0) = 220 km/s, while Deason uses 230 ± 10. A ~4.5% higher v_c raises v_esc by roughly the same fraction, about 20 km/s [estimate], which alone would move s = 1.0 to about −1.3σ.
  - So "the standard model is too light" partly reflects its older v_c normalisation, not just its halo.
- For the Galaxy loop: next time it makes sense to swap MWPotential2014 for a newer Gaia-calibrated potential (e.g. McMillan 2017, available in galpy) and redo C3–C6 at once. That is one lock instead of patching s.
VERDICT: definition confirmed; D1105 stands; recommend a McMillan17 re-run of C3–C6.
MAP: none

## D1110 (CENTRE, Djl loop (A), locked PREREG_A2): first absolute (normalised) wino γ-line test — at 1 TeV, σv_γγ = 3.2e-27 (LO) / 2.6e-27 cm³/s (NLO, post-hoc √2) vs H.E.S.S. 2018's 4e-28 → f_max = 0.36 / 0.39 at tree-level Sommerfeld; SERAPIS-E's 1 TeV wino (f = 0.26) PASSES, with margin growing to 0.62–0.78 after the one-loop ×3–4 reduction
Lock pushed before run; result field_tests/results/a2_wino_line.txt.
- Normalisation (sourced):
  - σv = c Σ sΓs*, with c = 2 for identical and c = 1 for distinct particles (hep-ph/0610249 Eqs. 6/8; 1307.4082 Eq. A8).
  - Γ^γγ only in the +− entry, with σ^γγ_{+−}v = πα²/M² (1307.4082 Eq. B5).
  - Hence σv_γγ = 2|s_{+−}|²πα²/M².
  - The total Γ (hep-ph/0610249 Eq. 5) matches PREP_A's 1712.07142 form after basis reordering. This is a cross-source check of A1's normalisation.
- Limit (quoted, arXiv:1805.05741): H.E.S.S. γγ-only ≈ 4e-28 cm³/s at 1 TeV, Einasto, 7 ROIs. The 2 and 3 TeV values are plot-only, so not used.
- Results (M = 1 TeV, v = 1e-3):
  - LO: |s_{+−}|² = 0.719 → f_max 0.355
  - NLO: 0.592 → 0.391
  - One-loop bracket: 0.62–0.78
- Cross-check with A7b/W2 (relative-scaling route, D735 read-off): f_max at 1 TeV was 0.27–0.52 across halo amplitudes. The absolute computation lands inside that range.
- γZ is not included. H.E.S.S. 2018 bounds γγ only, so this is the like-for-like comparison. Line-shape analyses that include γZ (later H.E.S.S./CTA work) would tighten it by roughly (1 + ½σ_γZ/σ_γγ)^{1/2} [factor unsourced].
- 1.85 TeV (W2 FAIL) is not re-tested here: there is no quoted H.E.S.S. number at that mass.
VERDICT: A2 PASS for SERAPIS-E at 1 TeV (tree-SE f_max 0.36–0.39 ≥ 0.26).
MAP: none

## D1111 (CENTRE, Djl loop (B), locked PREREG_A2e): tidal phase from Henry–Faye–Blanchet 2020 — 6PN and 6.5PN (tail) match LAL to ≤ 8.8e-10 rad, but 7PN misses by 6.6–7.8e-4 rad (lock 1e-6) — A2e NOT VALIDATED as locked; the 7.5PN term agrees exactly (same residual), so the gap is one 7PN piece
Lock pushed before run; result field_tests/results/janus_astro_a2e.txt.
- Code: gw.taylorf2_tidal_dphase_hfb (Eq. 6.6a, quadrupolar Λ only; σ̃ = μ̃^(3) = 0, as locked).
- E1 (6PN, HFB vs LAL): ≤ 8.8e-10 rad. PASS. This also cross-checks HFB against VFH 2011 (D1098) at 6PN.
- E2 (6.5PN tail): ≤ 8.7e-10 rad. PASS.
- E3 (7PN): residuals 7.40e-4 / 7.81e-4 / 6.59e-4 rad for the three systems. FAIL.
- 7.5PN (reported): exactly the same residual as 7PN, so the 7.5PN term matches LAL. The whole difference sits in the 7PN coefficient.
- The miss is 0.1% of the ~0.8 rad tidal phase: physically negligible for any detector (D1101 needs ~0.13 rad-level differences).
- Hypotheses (untested, no tuning):
  - (a) LAL fills the magnetic σ̃ and octupole μ̃^(3) from quasi-universal relations in Λ2 when only Λ2 is given. Those enter exactly at 7PN, so this fits the pattern.
  - (b) The paper's 7PN coefficient (erratum versions v3/v4) differs from what LAL uses.
  - (c) A transcription issue in the 7PN μ̃ coefficients from the fetched text.
  - A test that separates them, as a future A2f lock: insert explicit zero octupole/magnetic Λ in LAL's dict (SimInspiralWaveformParamsInsertTidalOctupolarLambda1/2 = 0 and the magnetic equivalents, if present). If the residual drops to 1e-9, (a) is confirmed.
VERDICT: A2e NOT VALIDATED as locked (7PN off by ~7e-4 rad); 6PN and 6.5PN VALIDATED-level agreement.
MAP: none

## D1112 (CENTRE, Djl loop (C), locked PREREG_C7 + DEVIATIONS D1): McMillan 2017 (Gaia-calibrated) passes the escape speed, the BHB mass and isotropic dispersions, but is 5.1σ too heavy for the K-giant M200 and 2.7σ for the K-giant enclosed mass — the Milky Way data themselves disagree (K giants want a light halo, v_esc a heavy one); MWPotential2014 and McMillan17 bracket the truth
Lock pushed before run. D1: galpy's McMillan17 returns physical units, and my script multiplied by vo again. Fixed via DEVIATIONS before the rerun. Result field_tests/results/c7_mcmillan17.txt.
- McMillan17 (no rescaling; v_c(r0) = 233.2 km/s):
  - C3 KG M(<73) = 6.85e11 (+2.69σ, TENSION)
  - C3 BHB M(<52) = 5.29e11 (+0.99σ)
  - C4 halo M200 = 1.315e12: KG +5.10σ EXCLUDED, BHB +0.47σ
  - C6 v_esc = 563 km/s (+1.45σ, CONSISTENT; MWPotential2014 was −2.1σ)
  - C2 dispersions: β = 0 CONSISTENT (with +44 at 120 kpc, exactly on the 2σ boundary); β = 0.5 and 0.8 NOT
  - Local halo density (computed after the run, reported only): ρ_DM(R0) = 0.0101 M_⊙/pc³ ≈ 0.385 GeV/cm³ [conversion 1 M_⊙/pc³ = 37.97 GeV/cm³].
- Reading:
  - The halo-mass "tension" in D1105 is not a model artefact but a disagreement between data sets.
    - K-giant Jeans (Bird+2022: M200 0.55e12) and the measured radial anisotropy (β ≈ 0.8) prefer a LIGHT halo.
    - The escape speed (Deason+2019) and BHB stars prefer a HEAVY one (~1–1.3e12).
  - MWPotential2014 (light) and McMillan17 (heavy) bracket the data. The honest MW halo range is about 0.7–1.3e12 M_⊙ in M200, and ρ_⊙ ≈ 0.29–0.39 GeV/cm³.
- For the wino (W2/A2):
  - ρ_⊙ 0.385 vs 0.286 is ×1.35, so J (∝ ρ²) is ×1.8 and f_max is ×0.74.
  - A2's 1 TeV f_max 0.36–0.39 would become ~0.27–0.29 [estimate, local-normalisation scaling]. SERAPIS-E's f = 0.26 would still pass, barely, at tree-level Sommerfeld; with the one-loop line reduction it stays comfortable (0.46–0.58).
  - This narrows the SERAPIS-E 1 TeV margin. Worth a locked recomputation with the McMillan17 J-factor (H.E.S.S. ROIs) on the next A tick.
VERDICT: McMillan17 mixed (passes v_esc/BHB, fails K-giant M200); the data sets disagree; SERAPIS-E 1 TeV wino passes even for the heavy halo [estimate].
MAP: none

## D1113 (CENTRE, Djl loop (D), locked PREREG_A2f, diagnostic): D1111's 7PN tidal gap is NOT LAL's octupole handling (refuted: an explicit 0 changes nothing, and TaylorF2 ignores octupolar Λ entirely) — the residual is a pure v⁹ (7PN) shape, and LAL's 7PN quadrupole piece is 0.99667 × ours, i.e. one coefficient differs by ~0.33% (0.185 in the equal-mass 7PN μ̃₊ coefficient 55.58)
Lock pushed before run; result field_tests/results/janus_astro_a2f.txt.
- P1: octupolar Λ explicitly 0 gives a residual of 7.40e-4 rad, unchanged. Hypothesis (a) REFUTED.
- P2: octupolar Λ = 1000 vs 0 changes LAL's phase by exactly 0. LAL's TaylorF2 phase does not use the octupole.
- P3: the residual fits v⁹ to rms 1.5e-10 (v¹⁰: 1.3e-5; v¹¹: 2.4e-5), so it is purely 7PN. The amplitude ratio of LAL's 7PN tidal piece to ours is 0.99667.
  - Equal mass: our coefficient [136190135/27433728 + 978554825/4572288 ν − 281935/6048 ν² + 5/3 ν³] at ν = 1/4 is 55.5815. LAL implies about 55.396.
- Remaining hypotheses:
  - (b) LAL follows a different version/erratum of the HFB 7PN coefficient (the paper itself flags an earlier flux error, v1→v4).
  - (c) A transcription error in one fetched coefficient. For example, 0.185 equals a change of 2.96 in the ν² coefficient (281935/6048 = 46.62 → ~49.6) or of 0.74 in the ν coefficient.
- No coefficient is fitted or adopted: that would be tuning. Next step: source the coefficient independently, either from LAL's source code (LALSimInspiralPNCoefficients.c, XLALSimInspiralTaylorF2Phasing_14PNTidalCoeff, via GitHub/git.ligo.org through the allowlist) or from the HFB erratum. Then re-lock as A2g with the sourced value.
- Physics impact: none (7e-4 rad ≪ any detectability scale, D1101). The 6PN and 6.5PN pieces are validated.
VERDICT: (a) refuted; gap localised to one 7PN coefficient (0.33%); source-check pending (A2g).

## D1115 (CENTRE, Djl loop (B), literature/code source check): the 7PN tidal gap is fully explained — LAL's 7PN tidal coefficient (read from ripplegw 0.5.1's TaylorF2.get_14PNTidalCoeff, a port of LALSuite) differs from our transcription of Henry–Faye–Blanchet Eq. 6.6a by exactly the observed factor 0.99667 (equal mass: −15.5802 Λ vs −15.6323 Λ); 6.5PN is identical (5.7432 Λ both)
- Route: GitHub and git.ligo.org (LAL C source) and the LAL Doxygen pages are blocked or access-denied from here. pip ripplegw (JAX port that "implements TaylorF2 as described in the LALSuite library") gives the per-body coefficient:
  - 14PN: −X⁴·5·(193986935/571536 − 14415613/381024 X − 57859/378 X² − 209495/1512 X³ + 965/54 X⁴ − 4X⁵)
  - 13PN: X⁴·24(12 − 11X)π
- Arithmetic (equal mass):
  - LAL 7PN term (3/32)·2·c14(½) = −15.58022 Λ, vs HFB as transcribed −15.63230 Λ. Ratio 0.996668, which matches D1113's fitted 0.99667.
  - 6.5PN: both 5.743224 Λ (exact agreement).
- So the whole A2e/E3 residual is this one coefficient difference. Which is physically right is still open:
  - (i) LAL implements an erratum/later version of HFB (the paper flags v1→v4 flux corrections), or
  - (ii) my fetched transcription of Eq. 6.6a has an error in a 7PN fraction.
  - Deciding needs the HFB erratum text (or the LAL comment citing its source), not reachable here.
- Not done: I did NOT adopt LAL's coefficient and call it validated. That would be validating against the referee with the referee's own number. Hyperion keeps the HFB-transcribed form, labelled with a 0.33% open question at 7PN.
- Physics impact: none (7e-4 rad).
VERDICT: gap explained to 5 digits; which coefficient is correct is OPEN (needs the HFB erratum / LAL citation).
MAP: none

## D1135 — RIGHT (R track) — a concrete exactly-vanishing N=2 coefficient (Z6-II-b, U(1)): the D1051 small-γ̃ condition has a known realisation [literature]
[literature, fetched arXiv hep-th/0001062] In the Z6-II-b orbifold, the Θ² N=2 sector's U(1) factor has a_{U(1)} = 0 ("since the gauge group under the
additional threshold scale M_I is abelian", after Eq. 50) and b̃_{U(1)} = 0 (c_{U(1)} = 0, no charged hypermultiplets; after Eq. 51), multiplying the

one loop. So "near-finite" is not a free tuning: the natural values are 0 (abelian, uncharged) or O(1)×1/64π² (non-abelian). ε = 6e-5 then needs a small
correction to an exactly-zero coefficient (e.g. Wilson-line mixing, which hep-th/0001062 treats, or a two-loop term) — a sharper, model-level question.

## D1137 — RIGHT (R track) — Wilson lines do not lift D1135's exact zero (to O(BC)) [literature]
[literature, fetched hep-th/0001062] Wilson lines B, C enter at O(BC) (Eqs. 29, 36, 40–41, 43, 45). The U(1) η-log term is −(a_{U(1)}/16π²){log(9|η(T)η(U/3)|⁴) +

singular at T = U, not the Kronecker L = −ln(2 Im T|η|⁴) the ρ tilt needs.

none found yet. I'll pause this line unless a new source turns up, and switch R effort to S4d.

- ⚠ Inconsistency found: D784/D1080 used f = 0.14 / 0.26 / 0.67 at 0.66 / 1.0 / 1.85 TeV. Those are ≈ (M/1.8–2.2)², not (M/2.9)²: 0.26 at 1 TeV implies M_th ≈ 1.96 TeV. ### D1159 — R2b2 threshold: pointwise FAIL, Rydberg tower below χ⁺χ⁻ threshold SUPPORTED (2026-11-17)
- [CENTRE · computed] **Locks:** PREREG_R2b2_threshold + DEVIATIONS_R2b2 (D1). **Results:** field_tests/results/r2b2_threshold.txt, r2b2_rydberg.txt.
- **Scored test (as locked): FAIL.** Total σv(χ⁰χ⁰ in) ∝ sΓs†, M = 2000 GeV, same LO potential on both sides.
  - Below threshold: S(0.95) = 111, S(0.99) = 3.94.
  - Above threshold: S(1.01) = 36.2, S(1.05) = 35.6, S(1.2) = 32.7, S(1.5) = 27.4. The open side is smooth.
  - Jump = 8.2, against the ≤ 0.20 criterion. FAIL stands.
- **Why:** the lock was ill-posed (my error).
  - The closed χ⁺χ⁻ channel has a −α/r Coulomb tail, so there is an infinite Rydberg tower of χ⁺χ⁻ quasi-bound states (Feshbach resonances) just below 2δm.
  - Pointwise continuity cannot hold there. Only the resonance-averaged σv should join the open side (Gailitis–Damburg).
- **Diagnostic D1 (pre-registered after the FAIL): SUPPORTED.**
  - 7 peaks, at n_eff = 1.53, 2.53, …, 7.54. Spacings 0.999–1.01, so the quantum defect is constant at ≈ 0.47.
  - Peaks S ≈ 340 (heights limited by the grid). Troughs S ≈ 0.37–0.39.
  - The closed solver is therefore behaving physically: a textbook Rydberg series with 1 − x_n = 0.0917/(n − 0.47)².
- **Not yet shown:** that the energy average below threshold equals the open-side value (≈36).
  - The scan mean (113) is uniform in n_eff, not in energy, so it is not that test.
- **Next (R2b3, lock first):** energy-averaged σv over one Rydberg period near n ≈ 6–8 (fine grid that resolves the peak widths, or the analytic area), compared with the open side extrapolated to x → 1⁺. PASS if within 20%.
- **Relevance:** freeze-out is far above threshold, so R2c (thermal average at x ~ 20–30) is unaffected. The tower matters only for late-time/halo velocities, where the D1158–1159 resonance structure must be velocity-averaged.
VERDICT: closed and open solvers each behave physically. Pointwise threshold continuity is not a valid test (lock error, recorded). The averaged-continuity test is OPEN as R2b3.
MAP: none

### D1179 — Literature: Gailitis' theorem concerns the TOTAL (optical-theorem) cross section; below threshold, annihilation also absorbs the flux that goes into χ⁺χ⁻ conversion above threshold (2026-11-17)
- [DEEP · literature] **Sources:**
  - arXiv:1607.07649 (Siegert-state QDT), §3.3. The energy average (over the mean level spacing, density-of-states weight, Eqs. 25–26) of the reduced collision matrix W is continuous across threshold (after Eq. 32).
    - Via σ_aa^t ∼ Re(1 − W_aa) this "results into Gailitis' theorem, σ̄^{<t}_aa = σ^{>t}_aa" (unnumbered).
    - Conditions: the reduced R-matrix is ≈ constant across the threshold region; Im R_ee > 0.
  - arXiv:2312.03883 (GD oscillations in e⁻e⁺p̄) only confirms the qualitative picture: a narrow resonance series below the threshold, Gailitis–Damburg oscillations above.
  - arXiv:1712.07142 (Braaten et al., ZREFT wino III), Introduction: LO ZREFT reproduces the resonances in χ⁰χ⁰ scattering just below the χ⁺χ⁻ threshold. The excerpt read has no annihilation-continuity statement.
- **What this changes:** the theorem is about the TOTAL cross section, which is linear in S via the optical theorem. It is not about one inelastic channel.
  - Below threshold, the χ⁰χ⁰ reaction channels are annihilation only, because χ⁺χ⁻ is closed.
  - Above threshold, the reaction is annihilation plus real conversion χ⁰χ⁰ → χ⁺χ⁻.
  - So the sourced expectation is ⟨σ_ann⟩_below ≈ σ_ann^> + σ_conv^> (+ an elastic-average difference): the quasi-bound χ⁺χ⁻ states can only annihilate or fall back.
  - My R2b3 expectation ⟨σ_ann⟩ = σ_ann^> left out σ_conv. That was the lock error. The R2b3 FAIL stands as scored.
- **Plausibility estimate (not computed):**
  - In S units (σv / (πα₂²/M²)): S_conv = 2PM/(k₀α₂²) ≈ 1.3e5·P at M = 2000, x = 1.01. The identical-particle convention for χ⁰χ⁰ is uncertain by ×2.
  - The D1170 gap needs S_conv ≈ 71, i.e. a conversion probability P ≈ 5e-4. That is plausible for a Coulomb-enhanced threshold channel.
  - So the factor ≈ 3 is now physically plausible, but NOT shown.
- **Next: R2b6 (locked in this tick).** Compute P_conv from the open solver's outgoing χ⁺χ⁻ flux at x = 1.01, and test ⟨S⟩ ≈ S_ann + S_conv within 20%.
VERDICT: the D1170 expectation was incomplete (it left out conversion), now sourced. A quantitative check is OPEN (R2b6).
MAP: none

### D1180 — R2b6: the Gailitis-total test FAILS because conversion is O(1), not small; the threshold question is PARKED, and the relic work moves to R2c (2026-11-17)
- [CENTRE · computed] **Lock:** PREREG_R2b6_conversion. **Result:** field_tests/results/r2b6_conversion.txt.
- **Self-check:** S_ann = 36.1988 vs 36.20 → OK (the copied integration is faithful).
- **Unitarity:** |S₀₀|² + P_conv = 1.000000 exactly (|S₀₀| = 0.3591, P_conv = 0.8711).
  - The open solver conserves flux, which is a strong independent validation of two_channel_open.
- **Conversion:** at x = 1.01, χ⁰χ⁰ → χ⁺χ⁻ happens with probability 0.87. In S units, S_conv(A) = 1.12e5 and S_conv(B) = 2.24e5.
- **Score:** ⟨S⟩ / (S_ann + S_conv) − 1 = −0.999 → **FAIL** for both conventions.
- **Why D1179's expectation was wrong too:** strong mixing makes conversion and elastic scattering O(1), while annihilation is perturbative (O(α₂²), added as sΓs† and not inside the Hamiltonian).
  - Below threshold, each quasi-bound χ⁺χ⁻ state mostly decays BACK to χ⁰χ⁰ (Γ_back ≫ Γ_ann). So Gailitis continuity of the total (elastic + conversion) says almost nothing about the tiny annihilation piece.
  - The correct object is MQDT with Γ_ann put into the Hamiltonian as an absorptive term, i.e. averaging with Γ_ann/Γ_back per resonance.
  - My "≈ 1 in 2,000 conversion" plausibility estimate in D1179 was wrong by ×1700.

  - (iii) Freeze-out (v ~ 0.3, open side) and halo velocities (v ~ 1e-3, closed side, validated vs Beneke in A1) both lie outside that band.
  - Reopen it only if R2c's thermal average turns out sensitive to x ∈ [0.9, 1.1]; R2c will report that weight.
- Three locks in a row (R2b2, R2b3, R2b6) had wrong expectations, and each is recorded as FAIL. Lesson: source the expectation BEFORE locking a physics-continuity test, not after.

### D1182 — R2c-b sourcing: wino Sommerfeld potentials and Γ for every charge/spin sector (Hisano et al. hep-ph/0610249, Eqs. 2–8, 13) (2026-11-17)
- [DEEP · literature, fetched this tick] **Potentials** (attractive < 0), with **Γ** in units of πα₂²/m²:

  | Sector, spin | Potential | Γ | Eq. |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | χ⁻χ⁻, S=0 | V = +α/r + α₂c_W² e^{−m_Z r}/r (the only repulsive channel) | 1/2 | (2) |
  | χ⁰χ⁻, S=0 and S=1 | V = −α₂ e^{−m_W r}/r | S=0: 1/2; S=1: 25/24 | (3) |
  | χ⁻χ⁺, S=1 | V = −α/r − α₂c_W² e^{−m_Z r}/r | 25/24 | (4) |
  | (χ⁰χ⁰, χ⁻χ⁺), S=0 | 2×2 with off-diagonal −√2α₂e^{−m_W r}/r and 2δm on the charged diagonal | ½[[2,√2],[√2,3]] in our (00, +−) order (paper order is (+−, 00): ½[[3,√2],[√2,2]]) | (5) |

  - χ⁰χ⁰ and χ⁻χ⁻ with S=1 are forbidden in the s-wave.
  - By CP, χ⁺χ⁺ = χ⁻χ⁻ and χ⁰χ⁺ = χ⁰χ⁻.
- **σv:** σv = cΓ|A|², with c = 2 for identical particles, else 1 (Eq. 6). The matrix form is σ_i v = c_i Σ A_ij Γ_jj' A*_ij' (Eq. 8).
- **Thermal sum:** Eq. 13 sums over ordered species pairs i, j ∈ {χ⁰, χ⁻, χ⁺} with 4/g_eff². The spin average is not written out; I take it as the s-wave spin weight ¼ (S=0) + ¾ (S=1). That is an assumption, but it is the one relic.py's Born σ_eff uses.
- **Cross-check against our code:** the Born limits match relic.py's sigma_eff_born term by term:
  - χ⁰χ⁰: ¼·2·1;
  - χ⁰χ^±: ¼·½ + ¾·25/24;
  - χ⁺χ⁻: ¼·3/2 + ¾·25/24;
  - χ^±χ^±: ¼·2·½.

  So the R1b 37/12 normalisation is consistent with Hisano. The sommerfeld_nlo LO potential also matches Eq. (5).
- **Locked this tick:** PREREG_R2c_b. Compute next tick.

  - a sourced α₂(μ = M) running.

### D1203 — κ tick: the McMillan17-vs-Horta κ gap (41.2 vs 36.9) is not a definition issue. McMillan17's local rotation curve RISES (dv/dR ≈ +1.3 km/s/kpc) while measurements say it FALLS (2026-11-17)
- [CENTRE · arithmetic + literature]
  - **Identities** (flat-disc epicycle): Ω = A − B, κ² = −4B(A − B), dv_c/dR = −(A + B).
  - **Horta+2026** (A = 16.5, B = −11.9): κ = 36.8, consistent with their quoted 36.9, so their κ follows the standard definition. Ω = 28.4, dv/dR = −4.6 km/s/kpc.
  - **Gaia DR1 Oort constants** (Bovy 2017; A = 15.3, B = −11.9, recalled and labelled): κ = 36.0, dv/dR = −3.4.
  - **Eilers et al. 2019** (arXiv:1810.09466, found in this search; value recalled): dv_c/dR ≈ −1.7 km/s/kpc.
  - **McMillan17 at R = 8.178** (from C8: v_c 233.2, κ 41.24, so Ω 28.52): B = −κ²/(4Ω) = −14.9, A = 13.6, dv/dR = **+1.3** km/s/kpc.
- **Reading:**
  - McMillan17 matches v_c and Ω at the Sun (C8 PASS), but its local rotation curve is slightly rising, against every listed measurement (falling by 1.7–4.6 km/s/kpc). Hence κ is 12% high.
  - So the κ gap is a genuine model-shape mismatch, not a definitional one.
  - For the Star Mapper this affects mainly the epicyclic amplitudes of near-circular disc orbits (r_peri/r_apo of thin-disc stars at the few-% level). It hardly affects halo stars.
  - No published 2025–26 Milky Way potential that fixes both v_c and dv/dR was found in this search. arXiv:2407.12551 ("New Galactic mass model for orbit computations") is a candidate to read next.
- **No computation.**

### D1210 — C9: refitting only the NFW halo (McMillan17 baryons fixed) to the Eilers+2019 rotation curve fixes the slope sign (Q2 PASS) but needs an implausibly compact halo (r_s ≈ 3 kpc); χ²/dof = 2.09 (Q1 FAIL, marginal) (2026-11-17)
- [CENTRE · computed] **Lock:** PREREG_C9_halo_refit. **Data:** field_tests/data/eilers2019_table1.csv (Eilers et al. 2019, arXiv:1810.09466v2 Table 1, fetched this tick; 32 points with R ≤ 20.78 kpc). **Result:** field_tests/results/c9_halo_refit.txt. No deviations.
- **Statistical errors only:**
  - ρ_s = 4.88e8 M☉/kpc³, r_s = 3.04 kpc.
  - χ²/dof = 2.09 → **Q1 FAIL** (criterion < 2). The original McMillan17 has χ²/dof = 122 on the same points.
  - dv_c/dR(8.178) = −1.09 km/s/kpc → **Q2 PASS** (McMillan17: +1.3).
  - v_c(8.178) = 228.7 (Horta −1.8σ); Ω = 27.97; κ = 38.8 (Horta +2.3σ; McMillan17 +5.4σ).
  - ρ_DM☉ ≈ 0.51 GeV/cm³.
- **With a 2% systematic floor:** χ²/dof = 0.25 (McMillan17 5.6), r_s = 2.91 kpc, dv/dR = −1.31, κ = 38.65.
- **Reading:**
  - (i) With McMillan17's baryons held fixed, the declining Eilers curve can only be matched by a very compact NFW halo (r_s ≈ 3 kpc vs ≈ 20 kpc in McMillan17, and vs typical Milky Way fits of ~10–20 kpc). That is implausible for a CDM halo; it means the baryons, not the halo, carry the misfit.

- **Decision:** McMillan17 stays the Mapper default (it fits Horta's v_c and Ω). Its local-slope defect (D1203) is recorded. The halo-only refit is rejected (r_s implausible).
- **Next (optional, lock first):** a 4-parameter fit (disc mass and scale length plus NFW ρ_s, r_s) to Eilers, with a prior on r_s (10–25 kpc) and on the local baryon surface density (as in 2407.12551's constraint).
VERDICT: Q1 FAIL (marginal), Q2 PASS. The refit is rejected as physically implausible. McMillan17 is retained.

Fact used (analytic): shifting A → A + a rescales the η-frame eigenvalue m² by e^{2a} and leaves L = ∫e^B dy fixed, so m L scales by e^{a}; quoting masses
with e^{A}=1 at a reference point multiplies S4e's m L/π by e^{−A_ref}. Needed factor: 1.041 (mode 1), 1.044 (mode 2), i.e. A_ref ≈ −0.040 to −0.043.

(A_ref −0.0526) [0.9821, 2.1504]; C3 9D-Planck-weighted (A_ref −0.0805) [1.0098, 2.2112]. None within ±0.01 of (0.97, 2.13) for both modes.
Verdict: NOT EXPLAINED by these four conventions. The needed shift sits between C1 and C2, so a convention of this kind is plausible, but we did not find
one stated in BTR, and fitting a reference point to the target would be curve-fitting. S4e stays NOT VALIDATED vs BTR; the ratio m₂/m₁ (2.190 vs 2.196)
and the solver (D1214, two methods agree to 1e-7) are unaffected. Next: our 6D masses are quoted as ratios and in the C0 convention, stated explicitly.

## D1224 — JANUS — JMF13: scale-factor normalisation bug in all four Janus-MF codes, found and fixed [FIX ADOPTED; nc-jit adopted]
Locks: field_tests/rules/PREREG_I25_pyt_radius.md (diagnostic) and PREREG_JMF13_ascale.md (fix). Results: field_tests/results/i25_pyt_radius.txt, janus_jmf13.txt.
I25: PyTransport NC on the same DoubleQuad model gives physical n_s at sphere radius R = 1.5 (0.933687) and R = 2 (0.936712) where Janus-MF-NC gave −0.83 and 3.49 → our bug.
Root cause (debug before the fix lock): modes were normalised with a = e^N. In long runs (horizon exit at N ≈ 114–121 for R ≥ 1.5) the mode amplitudes Q ~ u/a ~ 1e-50 sit far
below the ODE absolute tolerance (1e-30), so error control is off and P_R comes out as scattered garbage (~1e53). Short runs (R = 1, flat; exit at N ≈ 25–30) were safe by luck.
The same a = e^N was in mfms.py, mf_jit.py, mfms_nc.py, mfms_nc_jit.py (the single-field reference ms.spectra_fast already used a = e^(N − N_p)).
Fix: a = e^(N − N_p), k in the same units (k_p = H(N_p)) — a comoving rescaling, physics unchanged.
A1 (unchanged where it worked): flat Q3 spectra_mf 0.945476967, spectra_mf_fast 0.945476944, spectra_jit 0.945476945; NC R=1 python 0.925024148, nc-jit 0.925024083 —
all within 1e-7 of their pre-fix values. A2 (fixed): R = 1.5 python & nc-jit 0.933727 vs PyTransport 0.933687 (|Δ| 4.0e-5); R = 2 0.936746 vs 0.936712 (3.4e-5) → PASS.
Note: PyTransport's own n_s shifts by 4e-5 between its time grids (R=1: 0.925023 on 6000 steps/300 e-folds vs 0.924982 on 8000/400), the same size as these residuals.
Consequences: JMF9's VALIDATED scope extends to R = 1.5 and 2; JMF12/12b case (c)/(e) failures are explained; nc-jit adopted as the curved-space PC default; every
earlier Janus-MF verdict stands (all were short runs, and A1 shows no change). Item 25 → DONE.
MAP: none (tool correctness).

  - **Result:** field_tests/results/r2e_b_gstar.txt. No deviations.
- **g_*^{1/2}** (Gondolo–Gelmini, with the h_* derivative term) = 10.28 at T = 100 GeV (vs √106.75 = 10.33), 8.65 at 1 GeV, 4.66 at 0.1 GeV.
- **B1:** Born M_th = 2.2521 TeV vs Beneke 2.207, +2.04% → **PASS** (≤ 3%). R2e-a, with constant g_*, gave 2.325. Starting at x = 1 instead of 3 gives the identical 2.2521.
- **L1:** LO-Sommerfeld M_th = 3.013 TeV vs Beneke 2.886, +4.4% → **FAIL** (≤ 3%). R2e-a gave 3.135.
  - Ω h² = 0.0551, 0.0736, 0.0902, 0.1048, 0.1195, 0.1349 at M = 2.2–3.2 TeV.
- **Progress of the relic chain against Beneke:**
  - Born: +14.7% (R1b) → +5.4% (MS-bar α̂₂) → **+2.0%** (EOS).
  - LO Sommerfeld: (R2d est. 3.47) → +8.6% → **+4.4%**.
  - So the EOS was the D1187/D1230 suspect, and it accounted for ~3.5 points of the Born gap and ~4 points of the Sommerfeld gap.
- **Remaining gap is in the Sommerfeld factor:** M_Som/M_Born is 1.338 (ours) vs 1.308 (Beneke), +2.3%. Candidates, not tested and no rerun:
  - (i) R_eff is held fixed beyond x = 3e4, while Beneke tabulates to x = 1e8;
  - (ii) the 25-point x grid and the n = 40 velocity grid near the late-time resonance tail;
  - (iii) the spin-weight assumption ¼/¾ (D1182) vs Beneke's full matrices;
  - (iv) the remaining Born offset (+2.0%) enters as well.
- **For SERAPIS:**
  - The thermal-mass anchors used in the fraction bracket (D1152: 2.207 and 2.842) are Beneke's, and our own code now agrees with Beneke's Born to 2%. The f(M) bracket is therefore corroborated, not changed.
  - The paper needs no edit (it quotes Beneke's numbers).
VERDICT: B1 PASS, L1 FAIL (+4.4%). Most of the gap is closed by the sourced EOS. The residual is in the late-time Sommerfeld treatment and is OPEN.

### D1259 — Sourcing for the L1 gap: Beneke's relic includes P-wave and O(v²) S-wave annihilation, while ours is leading S-wave only. A new main candidate (v) (2026-11-18)
- [DEEP · literature, fetched] **arXiv:2009.00640, Sec. 4.1–4.2** (quoted, short):
  - "We therefore include P-wave and O(v²)-suppressed S-wave annihilation."
  - The annihilation matrices f̂(^{2S+1}L_J) are "tabulated in Appendix C of [30]".
  - Short-distance couplings are "the MS-bar couplings evolved with one-loop accuracy to the scale μ = 2m_χ".
  - Thermal average on 160 log-spaced x points.
  - Eq. (4.3) combines ¹S₀ + 3·³S₁ + O(v²) S-wave + ¹P₁ + ³P_J, each Born term weighted by its own Sommerfeld factor (Eq. 4.1).
  - Kinetic equilibrium is not addressed in the part read.
- **Ours (R1–R2e):** leading S-wave only (Hisano Eqs. 2–5, D1182) with Born-ratio α̂₂ scaling. So both our Born (+2.0%) and our LO-Sommerfeld (+4.4%) masses lack the v² terms.

### D1266 — Sourcing candidate (v): ref. [30] is Hellmann & Ruiz-Femenía 1303.0200. Its pure-wino appendix gives the v² terms only for χ⁺χ⁻ → W⁺W⁻, and they are POSITIVE, which points the wrong way for our Born residual (2026-11-18)
- [DEEP · literature, ar5iv HTML via summariser] **Reference [30] of 2009.00640:** C. Hellmann and P. Ruiz-Femenía, "Non-relativistic pair annihilation of nearly mass degenerate neutralinos and charginos II", JHEP 08 (2013) 084, arXiv:1303.0200. Ref. [31] is Beneke–Hellmann–Ruiz-Femenía, arXiv:1411.6924.
- **Appendix C.2** (pure-wino, χ⁺₁χ⁻₁ → W⁺W⁻ only; units πα₂²/m_χ²):
  - S-wave: ³S₁ 1/48, ¹S₀ 1/2 (Eqs. 143–144);
  - P-wave: f̂(¹P₁) = 2/3, f̂(³P_J) = 14/3;
  - O(v²) S-wave: ĝ(¹S₀) = −8/3, ĝ(³S₁) = −1/9 (Eq. 145);
  - σv_rel = (9/16) + (7/48) v_rel² (Eq. 146), in units of πα₂²/m_χ².
  - Numerically at m_χ = 2748.92 GeV: a = 3.06e-27, b_P = 1.81e-27, b_S = −1.02e-27 cm³/s.
- **The full exclusive table for every sector** (C.3, Table 5) and the NNLO S-wave coefficients are in a Mathematica supplement. The summariser could not reach them (the HTML is 1.5M characters, truncated). They are NOT obtained.
- **Direction check (ESTIMATE):** for this channel the net v² coefficient is positive, (b_P + b_S)/a = +0.26. At freeze-out, ⟨σv⟩ ≈ a + 6b/x adds ≈ +6% at x = 25.
  - If the other channels behave similarly, including v² terms RAISES σ_eff. Our Born M_th then goes UP (≈ +3%, M ∝ √σ), away from Beneke's 2.207.
  - So (v) can explain our B1 residual (+2.0%) only if Beneke's "Born" 2.207 excludes the v² terms or the net sign differs in other channels. Neither is established.
  - For L1, the v² terms are only weakly Sommerfeld-enhanced, so they lower M_Som/M_Born, the right direction. Their net effect on the L1 mass is therefore unclear.
- **Status:** (v) is downgraded from "leading" to "unresolved" (it cannot be quantified without the full Table 5 or the supplement). Candidates (ii) velocity grid, (iii) spin weights and (iv) per-channel MS-bar scaling stay open.
  - The most decidable next step is (ii): a locked grid-doubling at intermediate x. It is cheap and needs no new sources.
VERDICT: partial source obtained (χ⁺χ⁻ → WW only). Candidate (v) is unresolved and likely the wrong direction for B1. Next cheap test: (ii).

## D1277 — Shape selection vs scale: in 2D hexagonal wins at every scale; in 3D BCC and FCC swap exactly at the self-dual scale (2026-11-18)
MAP: node=n_sector_rho status=computed
LABEL: numerics (computed) + literature (theorems). No new physics claim.

- 2D (square vs hexagonal, α = 0.25…4): hexagonal lowest at EVERY α — no flip (reproduces Montgomery).
- 3D (SC, BCC, FCC, α = 0.25…4): BCC wins for α<1, FCC for α>1, exact tie at α=1 (0.231536 both); SC never wins.
MECHANISM: Poisson summation, θ_L(α) = α^{−d/2} θ_{L*}(1/α). FCC and BCC are mutual duals, so they must exchange order at the
self-dual scale α=1. The 2D hexagonal lattice is self-dual up to similarity, so it has no distinct partner to swap with and
cannot flip. E8 and Leech — optimal at every scale — are self-dual too. So a shape can only lose to its own dual, and only on
the far side of the self-dual scale.
RELEVANCE: 2D lattice duality is τ → −1/τ in our modular parameter; τ=i and τ=ρ are fixed points of modular maps. The
d=2 preference for the ρ (hexagonal) sector in D1276 is therefore scale-robust, not an artefact of the exponent chosen.
The T-/S-duality parallel is the same Poisson-duality mathematics, recorded as such — not a derived physical link.
Result file: field_tests/results/shape_duality_flip_2026-11-18.txt.

## D1279 — Running it backwards: a torus started at any shape slides to the hexagon; the square is a saddle held only by mirror symmetry (2026-11-18)

## D1280 — τ = i is a SADDLE of the actual SERAPIS-E potential (unstable only along the axion); any potential monotone in E(τ,2) has its vacuum only at ρ (2026-11-18)

## D1283 — Literature: the string-theory version of our shape results — optimal Narain lattices (Angelinos–Chakraborty–Dymarsky 2022) (2026-11-18)
MAP: node=n_sector_rho status=literature
LABEL: literature + comparison. No new physics claim; one honest mismatch recorded.
Source read: N. Angelinos, D. Chakraborty, A. Dymarsky, "Optimal Narain CFTs from Codes", arXiv:2206.14825 (JHEP 2022).
What it says (fetched text): a toroidal string compactification of c dimensions is fixed by an even SELF-DUAL lattice in R^{c,c}
(the Narain lattice); the "best" one maximises the spectral gap Δ* (lightest state). Optimal theories for c ≤ 8 are built from codes:
c=1: Δ*=1/2, boson at the self-dual radius; c=2: Δ*=2/3, the SU(3)₁ point with t = b = (1+i√3)/2 (hexagonal shape AND hexagonal
B+i·volume); c=3,4,5: 3/4, 1, 1; c=6,7: √(4/3). Large c: random codes reach Δ* ≈ c/(2πe), the conjectured asymptotic maximum.
Comparison with our results:
1. [matches D1276–D1280] The c=2 optimum sits at the hexagonal shape τ=ρ — the same point where SERAPIS-E has its only vacuum
   (D1280) and where the hexagon wins the lattice energy at every scale (D1277). Two independent "best shape" criteria agree.
2. [matches D1278/D1282] Narain lattices are self-dual by construction, and T-duality (R → 1/R) is exactly the Poisson map
   α → 1/α we used. D1278's rule says a self-dual winner never flips with scale — the string-theory statement that physics at
   R and 1/R is the same. The flips we found (FCC/BCC, D5, E6, E7) are flips of a non-self-dual sublattice (momenta alone),
   which T-duality swaps with its dual (windings) at the self-dual radius.
3. [MISMATCH, honest] The c=2 optimum also needs the Kähler modulus at the hexagonal point (volume ~ string scale). In
   SERAPIS-E the Kähler side is large (Im S·Im ρ ≈ 780, the supergravity regime). So only the SHAPE half of our vacuum
   coincides with the string-optimal point; the size half does not. Not a contradiction — the max-gap criterion is not a
   dynamical vacuum selector — but it means "SERAPIS-E sits at the optimal string lattice" would be an overclaim.
Verdict: PASS (literature). Paper: added as SERAPIS_DERIVATION §9 (geometry). Next: whether any known mechanism selects
max-gap points dynamically (would turn item 1 from coincidence into derivation) — SEARCH.

Source read: Kofman, Linde, Liu, Maloney, McAllister, Silverstein, "Beauty is Attractive: Moduli Trapping at Enhanced Symmetry
Points", arXiv:hep-th/0403001 (JHEP 2004). Content (fetched): a modulus rolling past an "extra species point" (ESP), where new
states become light, produces those particles; their energy grows with distance from the ESP and pulls the modulus back;
Hubble friction damps the orbit so it settles AT the ESP. The self-dual radius of toroidal compactifications is their example
("all circles end up at the self-dual radius"); the strongest attraction is to points with the most light species, often the most
symmetric ones. They present "beauty is attractive" as a speculation conditional on early-universe dynamics, not a theorem.
Comparison with D1283:
1. [literature] So a dynamical mechanism that favours maximal-symmetry points DOES exist, and the c=2 max-gap SU(3) point is such
   an enhanced-symmetry point (extra light W states there — standard toroidal-string fact, [estimate]-level reading, not re-derived).
2. [derived, reasoning] The extra light states at that point need BOTH moduli at the special value: their masses depend on the
   shape and on the complexified size (winding/momentum). At SERAPIS-E's large volume (Im S·Im ρ ≈ 780) they are heavy whatever
   the shape, so the shape alone is NOT an extra-species point and trapping gives no pull toward τ=ρ there.
3. [derived] Hence trapping would drive the torus to the string-scale SU(3) point — the opposite of the large volume SERAPIS-E needs
   — and cannot be the reason for the shape-only match. The shape preference in SERAPIS-E stays explained by D1280 (potential
   monotone in E(τ,2)), not by trapping.
Verdict: PASS (literature). D1283's open question narrowed: a selector exists but it is the wrong kind (shape+size). A shape-only
selector would need extra light states depending on τ alone at large volume (e.g. from branes/fluxes on that torus) — new open item.

statement, not an accident of s=2. One Eisenstein family runs from the d=2 inflaton torus (non-holomorphic E(τ,s)) up to the
E8/heterotic/Leech lattices (holomorphic E4, E4², E4³−720Δ).

## D1295 — Why the two SERAPIS sectors are τ=i and τ=ρ: they are the Gaussian and Eisenstein integers, the only lattice shapes with extra rotations, and symmetry forces every shape-energy to be stationary there; PREREG P1–P3 PASS (2026-11-18)

- P1 PASS: automorphism group orders — generic oblique 2, rectangle (τ=2i) 4, rhombus (τ=0.5+1.4i) 4, square (τ=i) 8, hexagon (τ=ρ) 12.
- P2 PASS: units of Z[i] = 4 (±1, ±i), of Z[ω] = 6 (sixth roots of 1); 8 = 2·4 and 12 = 2·6 (units × complex conjugation). The square
  torus IS the Gaussian integers and the hexagonal torus IS the Eisenstein integers — the only imaginary-quadratic rings with units
  beyond ±1, hence the only 2D lattices with rotations other than 180°.
- P3 PASS: the Gaussian energy's gradient at τ=i and τ=ρ is ≤4.5e-10 at α=0.5, 1, 2, while at the rectangle τ=2i (only 4 symmetries)
  it is 0.14–0.32. A rotation that fixes the shape turns the tangent plane, so any shape-energy (Gaussian, Epstein E(τ,s), the SERAPIS-E
  potential) must have zero gradient there — that is WHY i and ρ are the two critical points (D1292) and the two sectors of the model.
  Which one is the minimum is then a property of the energy (hexagon for all energies we tested, D1277/D1280/D1293).
CHAIN: number theory (units of Z[i], Z[ω]) → lattice symmetry (8, 12) → forced stationary shapes (i, ρ) → SERAPIS-E's two sectors.

## D1305 — CERN+1 LHC6: symmetry self-tests — the tables obey Drell–Yan scaling of ratios to 0.1% and the SU(2) charged/neutral ratio to 0.05%, but the charge asymmetry turns over above ~1.5 TeV (T1 FAIL as locked); PREREG T2–T3 PASS (2026-11-18)

  2 TeV (13 TeV; at 13.6 TeV peak 3.357 at 1600 GeV, 3.30 at 2 TeV). I predicted a monotonic rise (more u than d valence quarks at large x).
  The turnover sits exactly where the table's quoted PDF uncertainties become very large (≫ 10% above ~1.5 TeV), i.e. where the global
  PDFs are least constrained — the u/d behaviour of the PDF set at x ≳ 0.3 drives it. Flagged, not explained away: the self-test
  reports the table's charge asymmetry above 1.5 TeV as PDF-limited.
- T2 PASS: at equal τ₀ the asymmetry at 13.6 TeV equals that at 13 TeV to 0.093% (ratios cancel the evolution that κ absorbed in D1299).
- T3 PASS: R = (χ̃₂⁰χ̃₁⁺ + χ̃₂⁰χ̃₁⁻)/χ̃₁⁺χ̃₁⁻ = 1.94 → 2.20 → 2.04 across 100–2000 GeV is a function of τ₀ only to 0.050%.
- T4: tools/lhc/selftest.py runs all three; T2/T3 guard the tables against corruption; T1 marks the PDF-limited region.

## D1327 — A tick: continuum γ-ray probes (dwarfs, Galactic diffuse, isotropic) do not constrain the computed window (0.67 to 1–1.5 TeV) (2026-11-18)
- [CENTRE · literature + arithmetic]
- **Probes as recorded in D1084** (Hryczuk et al. 2014, arXiv:1401.6212, wino = 100% of DM, f = 1):
  - dwarfs exclude only near the resonance (≈ 2.4 TeV);
  - diffuse Galactic excludes < 0.65 and 2.0–2.65 TeV;
  - isotropic excludes < 0.75 and 1.92–2.7 TeV.
- **The newer combined dwarf analysis** (Fermi-LAT, HAWC, H.E.S.S., MAGIC, VERITAS; arXiv:2108.13646, ICRC 2021 proceedings) gives only bb̄ and τ⁺τ⁻ limits in the text read, with W⁺W⁻ "in progress". So there is no newer WW dwarf number to use.
- **Window check:** inside 0.67–1.5 TeV, the f = 1 exclusions above are absent except the diffuse/isotropic low-mass edge (0.65–0.75 TeV).
  - At 0.67–0.75 TeV the thermal fraction is f ≈ 0.05–0.12, so the signal scales by f² ≲ 0.014. That is ~70× below an f = 1 exclusion that is itself only marginal there.
  - Across the window f² ≤ 0.21 (1.5 TeV upper edge), and no f = 1 exclusion exists at 0.75–1.92 TeV.
- **Verdict:** the continuum probes add no constraint. The line (IGS) remains the binding astrophysical test (D1324).
- Caveat: the f = 1 exclusion bands are 2014 values. A W⁺W⁻ dwarf combination with modern J-factors would sharpen them, but cannot reach f² ~ 0.1 at these masses unless it improves by ×10.
VERDICT: NULL for new constraints; the window is confirmed against continuum probes.

## D1335 — Hyperion tick: a computable line+endpoint formula is sourced. Baumgart, Bottaro, Redigolo, Rodd, Slatyer, arXiv:2507.15937, Eq. 2.9 (leading-log, any SU(2) multiplet, wino n=1) (2026-11-18)
- [LITERATURE, via an HTML-to-text summary, so not character-exact]
  - dσ/dz|_LL = (F₀+F₁) σ₀ e^{−(4α_W/π)L_χ²} δ(1−z) − (2α_W/π) σ₀ e^{−(4α_W/π)L_χ²} { 2F₀ 𝓛₁^J e^{(4α_W/π)L_J²} + F₁ (2𝓛₁^J − 3𝓛₁^S) e^{(4α_W/π)(Θ_J L_J² − ¾Θ_S L_S²)} }
  - L_χ = ln(m_W/2M), L_J = ln(m_W/(2M√(1−z))), L_S = ln(m_W/(2M(1−z))), 𝓛₁^{J,S} = Θ L/(1−z).
  - Thresholds: Θ_J for 1−z > m_W²/4M², Θ_S for 1−z > m_W/2M.
  - Group factors F₀ = (|𝓜⁰⁰|² + 2|𝓜⁺⁻|²)/192M², F₁ = (|𝓜⁰⁰|² − |𝓜⁺⁻|²)/96M².
  - Wino amplitudes: 𝓜⁰⁰ = 16M s₀₁, 𝓜⁺⁻ = 4√2·2M s₀₀ + 8M s₀₁.
  - Normalisation: Eq. 2.1 spectrum per σ_line = σ_γγ + ½σ_γZ; the δ term is doubled in the flux (two photons).
- Sign check [arithmetic]: L_J < 0 for z near 1, so the −(2α/π)·2F₀𝓛₁^J term is positive, which is right for an endpoint.
- Also stated: NLL scale uncertainty ≈5% (1808.08956); CTAO resolution 5–7%; thermal triplet "percent-level" (2.86 TeV).
- Use (next Hyperion rung, A2p): lock a computation of the ratio (line + endpoint within 1−z < 10% H.E.S.S. resolution)/(line), using our Sommerfeld s₀₀, s₀₁ at 1.0/1.25/1.5 TeV. If the ratio is > 1, the IGS f_max in D1324 is conservative.
  - Expectation not yet sourced. The lock must fix the comparison to the 2.9 TeV Fig. 1 of 1808.08956 (read off), or else run as an "estimate" with no pass bar.
  - Before locking, the formula needs a character-exact check (PDF).

## D1340 — Hyperion tick: A2p's one labelled assumption (paper s₀ₘ = our Sommerfeld vector) is now CHECKED analytically against two of our validated rates (2026-11-18)
- [arithmetic] **Line.**
  - Paper: σ_line v = (F₀+F₁)σ₀v = 4s₀₁²·πα_W²s_W²/(2M²) = 2πα_W²s_W² s₀₁²/M² (Eqs. 2.10, 2.13).
  - Ours (a2l_burkert_J.py, the D1114/D1118 line chain): σ_γγ v = 2πα² s₁²/M² with α = α_W s_W². Adding ½σ_γZ (relative weight c_W²/s_W²) gives 2πα_W²s_W² s₁²/M².
  - These are identical, so s₀₁ = s₁ with no √2.
- [arithmetic] **WW.**
  - Paper: 𝓜⁺⁻ = 8M(√2 s₀₀ + s₀₁).

  - Same combination, so s₀₀ = s₀.
- Both solvers share the LO potential (off-diagonal −√2α₂e^{−m_W r}/r) and the free normalisation s = (1, 0). Checked numerically at 1 TeV, v = 1e-3: sommerfeld (1.289, 0.794) vs sommerfeld_nlo LO (1.320, 0.848). The difference is only the inputs (α_W 0.0335 vs the on-shell α₂, and δm).

- Small note: the sommerfeld.py inputs give s₁ ≈ 6% lower than the on-shell set at 1 TeV. R depends only on s₀₀/s₀₁ (0.616 vs 0.642), so the effect on R is second-order. Not rerun (no chasing).
