- [derived] With b̂ = 0 (D1367) and Y ⊃ (90/π³)E(U,2)/T₂ (D1366): Λ³ ∝ exp[+(3k/(2|b|))·Y] ⊃ exp[c·E(U,2)/T₂], c = (3k/(2|b|))(90/π³) > 0. |W|² ∝ exp(2c·E/T₂) is smallest where E(U,2) is smallest, i.e. at ρ (E(ρ,2) = 5.7834 < E(i,2) = 6.0268, saddle at i). So for a positive-definite (|W|²-dominated) potential the vacuum sits at the hexagon ρ — the sign question from D1363 is settled in this route, given the convention above.
- [estimate] Shape: expanding about ρ, V ∝ exp(2cE(ρ)/T₂)·[1 + (2c/T₂)(E(U) − E(ρ)) + …] — linear in e = E(U) − E(ρ) near ρ, then exponential; toward the cusp E ~ 2ζ(4)U₂² so V grows like exp(U₂²) — no plateau. The SERAPIS-E form V = e/(e+1)(1 + Ce/λ) is NOT reproduced at leading order. Neglected: e^K, D_UW and −3|W|² SUGRA terms, a second condensate or uplift, which could supply the saturation.
- Verdict: vacuum location (ρ) and sign: supported by this route. Plateau shape: BLOCKED at leading order — needs a structure giving a ratio (e.g. V ∝ 1 − |W(ρ)|²/|W(U)|²-type, or a racetrack). P3 stays a postulate; blocker list now: (a) 4D N=1 embedding of the b̂ = 0 E7, (b) saturation mechanism for the plateau.

## D1369 — DEEP / LEFT: P3 — the saturation blocker (D1368) restated with D699: the plateau needs V = V_up − a/E(U,2) with a > 0. Sign check of three candidate sources: D-term 1/Re f → +1/E (WRONG sign); condensate |W|² → exp(cE) (no saturation, D1368); F-term −3e^K|W|² with e^K ∝ 1/E(U,2) → −3|W₀|²/E (RIGHT sign, needs K ⊃ −log E(U,2)) (2026-11-18)
- [literature] D699 (ours): e/(e+1) with a = E(ρ,2) is exactly 1 − E(ρ,2)/E(U,2), i.e. a constant uplift minus a term ∝ 1/E(U,2), tuned to vanish at ρ. Pattern matches "uplift minus decaying correction" plateaus in string models, e.g. loop blow-up inflation V = V₀(1 − b c_loop/φ^{2/3}) (Bansal et al., 2403.04831; overview 2604.07288).
- [derived] (i) D-term from a factor whose Re f is threshold-dominated, Re f ∝ E(U,2)/T₂ (D1366): V_D = D²/(2Re f) ∝ +1/E — positive, so it is a MAXIMUM at ρ. Ruled out as the negative piece. (ii) Condensate (D1368): exp(cE), no 1/E. (iii) F-term: V ⊃ −3e^K|W|²; if K ⊃ −log E(U,2) then e^K ∝ 1/E(U,2) and V = V_up − 3|W₀|²/E(U,2)·(…) — the D699 form with a > 0.
- [estimate] (iii) needs a modular-invariant Kähler potential −log E(U,2) in place of the tree −log U₂ (large U₂: E ≈ 2ζ(4)U₂², so −log E ≈ −2 log U₂ — weight differs from tree). Whether a loop-corrected K resums to this is unshown; the known BHK loop term is ADDITIVE, δK ∝ E(U,2)/(T₂·Re S) (Berg–Haack–Körs), which gives e^K ≈ e^{K₀}(1 + δK) — a +E correction to −3|W|², not 1/E.
- Verdict: the only right-sign route found needs K ∝ −log E(U,2) (unproven). Next: check whether −3e^{K₀}|W|²·(1 + δK)⁻¹-type terms (e.g. from the inverse Kähler metric K^{TT̄} with δK) produce 1/(1 + εE) ≈ the ratio form at small ε. P3 stays a postulate.

## D1370 — DEEP / LEFT: P3 — D1369's inverse-metric check done exactly: K = −3 log T₂ + εE(U,2)/T₂ with constant W₀ gives V = e^K|W₀|²·u²/(2u+3), u = εE(U,2)/T₂. The 1/(1 + 2u/3) factor DOES appear (from K^{TT̄}), but the linear term cancels (extended no-scale) and the u² numerator wins: no plateau (2026-11-18)
- [derived] For functions of T₂ only: K_TT̄ = K''/4, |K_T|² = K'²/4. K' = −3/T₂ − u/T₂, K'' = 3/T₂² + 2u/T₂² (u = εE/T₂ at fixed U) → K^{TT̄}|K_T|² − 3 = 3(1 + u/3)²/(1 + 2u/3) − 3 = u²/(2u + 3). Checked with sympy (exact).
- [derived] So V_T = (|W₀|²e^u/T₂³)·u²/(2u+3): ∝ u²/3 for small u (∝ E(U,2)² — minimum at ρ, positive), ∝ (u/2)e^u for large u. The U-direction term K^{UŪ}|∂_U δK|²|W₀|² is O(ε²) and ≥ 0, same conclusion.
- [derived] Consequence: the BHK-type additive loop term gives a potential ∝ E(U,2)² near ρ — consistent with the known LVS loop result V_loop ∝ (g_s C^{KK})² with C^{KK} ∝ E(U,2) — vacuum at ρ again, but it rises without bound toward the cusp. The inverse-metric 1/(1 + xE) factor is real but multiplies x²E², so no 1 − E(ρ)/E(U) form.
- Verdict: route (iii) via additive δK is closed (no plateau). Every route tried so far (D1366–D1370) agrees on the VACUUM at ρ; none yields the plateau. Remaining: a genuine −a/E(U,2) term (D699 form) — e.g. a K that is −log of a modular object, or a field whose stabilised value ∝ E(U,2) feeding a 1/(that field) correction. P3 stays a postulate.

## D1371 — DEEP / LEFT: P3 — a second-field route that DOES give the plateau: if the threshold shifts the stabilised dilaton, Re S* = s₀ + εE(U,2), the AdS term −3e^K|W|² ∝ −1/Re S* plus an uplift tuned at ρ gives exactly V = (b/A)·x/(1+x), x = λ(E − E_ρ), λ = ε/A — the SERAPIS-E e/(e+1) form (2026-11-18)

- [derived] e^K ⊃ 1/(2Re S*) so the AdS piece is −3e^K|W|² ≈ −b/(s₀ + εE) with b ≈ (3/2)|W*|²e^{K_rest} > 0. Add an uplift V_up tuned so V(ρ) = 0: V = b/A − b/(s₀ + εE), A = s₀ + εE_ρ. Exactly V = (b/A)·x/(1+x), x = (ε/A)(E(U,2) − E_ρ) (sympy-checked, difference ≡ 0). This IS the SERAPIS-E plateau e/(e+1) with λ = ε/A and V₀ = b/A; minimum at ρ, saturation toward the cusp.

- Verdict: first route found that produces the plateau FORM from string ingredients (threshold → dilaton shift → 1/Re S). Not a derivation: caveat (a) decides it. Next: check the GS/modular-weight bookkeeping for the b̂ = 0 E7, then compute λ = ε/A for sensible s₀, k, T₂. P3 stays a postulate.

- [literature] Green, Russo & Vanhove, "Automorphic properties of low energy string amplitudes in various dimensions" (arXiv:1001.2535; ar5iv): (4.10) ℰ⁽⁸⁾₍₁,₀₎ = ½E^{SL(3)}_{5/2} − 4E^{SL(3)}_{−1/2}E₂(U); (4.13) ∫E^{SL(3)}_{5/2} = 2ζ(5)y₈^{−5/3} + (4/3)y₈^{1/3}E₂(T); (4.14) ∫E^{SL(3)}_{−1/2} = −(1/6)y₈^{1/3} − (1/2π³)y₈^{−2/3}E₂(T); (4.15) ℓ₈⁴∫ℰ⁽⁸⁾₍₁,₀₎ = ℓ_s⁴[ζ(5)/y₈ + (2/π³)E₂(T)E₂(U) + (2/3)y₈(E₂(T) + E₂(U))]; genus one = (2/π²)… I₁⁽²⁾ = E₂(T)E₂(U) (4.16); y₈ = e^{2φ₈} = g²ℓ_s²/V₂. R⁴ (3.28): 2ζ(3)/y₈ + 2(Ê₁(T) + Ê₁(U)) + (2π/3)log(y₈/μ̃₈).
- [derived] Write the D⁴R⁴ constant term as A₀ + B·E₂(U), A₀ = ζ(5)/y₈ + (2/3)y₈E₂(T), B = (2/π³)E₂(T) + (2/3)y₈ (both > 0). Then any structure ∝ 1/(A₀ + BE₂(U)) gives exactly the D699 plateau with a = (A₀ + BE_ρ)/B·… i.e. Ê/(a + Ê), a = A₀/B + E_ρ. E₂(U) is EXACT here (not a large-volume expansion), so — unlike Y — there is no U₂ < T₂ chamber, and horizon exit at y* = 14.58√a is allowed for any a.
- [derived] Sizes (E₂(T) ≈ 2ζ(4)T₂²): T₂ = 2, y₈ = 0.01 → a ≈ 184 (y* ≈ 198); T₂ = 5, y₈ = 0.1 → a ≈ 3.9; T₂ = 10, y₈ = 0.1 → a ≈ 1.8 (y* ≈ 19). Moderate weak coupling and volume give a = O(1–100): natural.
- [estimate] Still missing (the D1363 obstacle in a new form): a mechanism that turns the D⁴R⁴ COEFFICIENT into a potential ∝ 1/(A₀ + BE₂(U)) (e.g. via the four-derivative/F⁴ supergravity terms of Ciupke–Louis–Westphal, D1363, or a Kähler-type resummation). And the lower-order R⁴ term carries 2Ê₁(U) (s = 1) — by D1364 the plateau shape tolerates s = 1 admixture at fixed C.
- Verdict: a cleaner source than the threshold Y — exact E₂(U), no chamber, natural a. P3 origin remains a postulate pending the coefficient → potential mechanism.

## D1476 — DEEP / LITERATURE: string-calc S6a — the genus-two lattice integral is pinned from the source: for d = 2 the SO(2,2) Langlands–Eisenstein series in the Λ²V representation is a SUM, E*(2s,T) + E*(2s,U) — so at genus two U enters ADDITIVELY and alone, never as the E(T)E(U) product of genus one; GRV's genus-two D⁴R⁴ term (2/3)y₈(E₂(T) + E₂(U)) has exactly this form (2026-11-19)
- [literature] Pioline, "On the Rankin–Selberg method for higher genus string amplitudes" (arXiv:1602.00308): (3.49) R₂*(Γ_{d,d,2}, s) = 2E^{SO(d,d)*}_{Λ²V}(s + (d−3)/2); (3.54) E^{SO(2,2)*}_{Λ²V}(s) = ζ*(2s+1)ζ*(2s)ζ*(2s−1)[E₁*(2s,T) + E₁*(2s,U)]; (3.55) R.N.∫_{F₂}dμ₂Γ_{2,2,2} = 2ζ*(2)[E₁*(3,T) + E₁*(3,U)]; the two-loop D⁴R⁴ amplitude on T^d is the residue of E^{SO(d,d)*}_{Λ²V}(s′) at s′ = d/2. E₁*(s,τ) = ½ζ*(2s)Σ_{(c,d)=1}τ₂^s/|cτ+d|^{2s} (2.3).
- [derived] d = 2: s′ = 1 ⇒ the bracket is E₁*(2,T) + E₁*(2,U) (index 2s′ = 2), and the prefactor ζ*(2s′−1) = ζ*(1) supplies the pole whose residue is taken — so the genus-two D⁴R⁴ coefficient is ∝ E₂(T) + E₂(U), matching GRV 1001.2535 eq. 4.15's (2/3)y₈(E₂(T) + E₂(U)) in structure. [overall constant not checked against GRV's 2/3]
- [derived] Consequence for the D1406 target: at genus two the U-dependence is E₂(U) with a U-INDEPENDENT companion E₂(T) — of the form A₀ + B·E₂(U) with A₀ ∋ E₂(T). So in any quantity built from the genus-two D⁴R⁴ coefficient, a ≈ A₀/B + E_ρ with A₀/B ≈ E₂(T) + (tree)/(genus-two) — large when T₂ is large. The "a + Ê" structure of D1401 persists at genus two; still no mechanism places it in an overall e^K factor.

## D1484 — DEEP / LEFT: heavy-field check of the area-integration mechanism (D1482) — it FAILS as a two-term model: (i) the extremum in the area is a MINIMUM only with flipped signs (negative shape-blind source, positive Casimir, i.e. N_F > N_B); (ii) even then the area's mass on the plateau is m_A²/H² = 3pq(1 − P*) ≈ 0.06, so the area is LIGHTER than H at horizon exit and cannot be integrated out (2026-11-19)
- [derived] With u = ln A (canonical for K = −2 ln A), V(u) = a e^{−pu} − cE e^{−qu}, p < q: V′ = 0 ⇒ cE e^{−qu} = (p/q)a e^{−pu}; V″ = −p(q − p)a e^{−pu} and V_min = (1 − p/q)a e^{−pu} ⇒ V″ = −pq·V_min (sympy-checked for p = 2, q = 4: V″/V_min = −8). For a, c > 0 (positive tension/CC, negative bosonic Casimir) V_min > 0 and V″ < 0: a MAXIMUM — the area runs away. A minimum needs a, c < 0: V_min = −|a|²/(4|c|E) (p = 2, q = 4) — the 1/E form survives (m = 1) — with a negative shape-blind source (negative-tension brane / AdS₆) and a positive Casimir (fermion excess).
- [derived] Mass: m_A² = V″ = pq|V_min|. On the plateau V ≈ V_up and |V_min|/V_up = 1 − P, so m_A²/H² = 3pq(1 − P*). For the SERAPIS-type approach (s·m = 2, SMSCAN (2,1): r = 3.94e-4, ε = r/16, 1 − P* = √(2ε)/(√2·s·m) = 2.5e-3) and p = 2, q = 4: m_A²/H² = 0.06 (m_A ≈ 0.25H). For s·m = 3 (tension + Casimir) 1 − P* is smaller still ⇒ lighter.
- [derived] Consequence: the area is a second light field during inflation; the "integrate out A" step is invalid in the two-term model, and the true dynamics is two-field (isocurvature, different n_s, r). The mechanism survives only if a third, A-dependent term (e.g. the uplift's own A-scaling, or a non-perturbative/flux stabiliser) gives m_A ≫ H while preserving the E^{−m} form — then m changes with that term (D1396-type analysis).
- Verdict: area-integration as a two-term single-field model: KILLED (light area, sign requirements). Survives only with extra A-stabilisation — open. SMSCAN results remain valid as shape tests of the family 1 − (E_ρ/E)^m, not as tests of this mechanism. Lead route returns to the axio-dilaton (D1479), whose volume must also be checked the same way (LVSDIL's 𝒱 is heavy in LVS by construction — check pending).

With ξ(τ) = −χ/(4(2π)³)·E(τ,3/2) and form A (e^K ∝ 1/(𝒱 + ξ/2)): a = 1/λ ≈ 5e2–2e5, horizon exit at Im τ* ≈ 1.5e3–8e4 (g_s* ≈ 1e-5–7e-4), canonical excursion Δφ ≈ 5–8 M_P, physical tilt C_phys ≈ 6e-4–0.25; scales are safe (M_s, M_KK ≫ H); but the VACUUM sits at g_s = 1/Im ρ ≈ 1.15 and the excursion is super-Planckian (2026-11-19)

No map turns a heterotic one-loop (T,U) function into a tree-level function inside the dilaton's Kähler log.
- [derived] Verdict (1): triality is not the missing placement mechanism of D1406 — the corrections we need live in N ≤ 2 where triality is broken, and the known N = 2 maps keep loop order. Route CLOSED (as a placement mechanism).

E8 Epstein (lattice_lab, norm-2 roots) = 240·2^{−s}ζ(s)ζ(s−3): 12.7925834197 (s = 5), 4.5858909395 (s = 6) — exact.
- [derived] So SERAPIS's vacuum value is arithmetic: E(ρ,2) = (9/2)ζ(2)L(2,χ₋₃) = (3π²/4)·L(2,χ₋₃) — the Dedekind zeta of Q(√−3), an Euler product over primes (p ≡ 1 mod 3 split, p ≡ 2 mod 3 inert, 3 ramified). Up the chain: A2 = Eisenstein integers (inside C), D4 ≅ Hurwitz quaternions (H), E8 = Cayley/octonion integers (O) — Cayley–Dickson doubling 2 → 4 → 8; each lattice zeta is a product of ζ's/L's. Leech (24) is the first with a cusp-form (Ramanujan τ) piece — not a pure prime product. [estimate: D4 formula not checked here]
- [estimate] Physics use: none yet — this is structure, not a mechanism. It does make the SERAPIS constants exact closed forms (E_ρ, C·E_ρ combinations) and suggests a circuit law (A2/E8 Euler products) and a paper sentence.
